Each figure is the median of the runs and the worst run in brackets:

    | Operation | Median (worst) |
    |---|---|
    | Insert the 1,000,000 comments | 19.5 s (one statement) |
    | Insert the 10,000 users | 107 ms (one statement) |
    | List: top-level page of 50, on the hot node (30 runs) | 272 µs (534 µs) |
    | List: page of 50 after 2,500 rows (30 runs) | 1.84 ms (2.06 ms) |
    | Count of live comments, capped at 5,001 (30 runs) | 2.79 ms (4.87 ms) |
    | Write at the cap: count reads 5,000, refused, no insert (30 writes) | mean 2.65 ms (worst 4.36 ms) |
    | Write to a node with room: count, then insert (30 writes) | mean 4.94 ms (worst 5.93 ms) |
    | People: "Person" (90% of users match), 50 kept (20 runs) | 8.14 ms (15.2 ms) |
    | People: "Pat" (10% match), 50 kept (20 runs) | 6.44 ms (10.8 ms) |
    | People: "zzz" (no match, every user read) (20 runs) | 5.92 ms (11.1 ms) |

    The worst write measured is 5.93 ms (a write to a node with room). The people query was far inside the 50 ms the proposal set, so the ordering was left as it is. These are one run on one machine with a warm cache, and they show the statements do not grow with the table; they are not a load test. The fuzz target `FuzzCleanCommentBody` checks that an accepted body is NFC, not blank, at most 2,000 characters, at most 50 lines, and holds no control or bidi control character except LF.

    **Mutation proofs** (one change at a time, on this tree, each restored and the tree checked for residue). Each row names the mutation and the tests that failed on it:
    - in-transaction role check replaced by a read with no reach check: `TestRoleIsCheckedInsideTheWrite`, `TestViewerReadsCommenterWrites`.
    - switch not checked inside the create write: `TestCommentsSwitchOff`.
    - live cap doubled: `TestCommentLimitPerNode`.
    - a mention resolved for any existing user, reach ignored: `TestMentionEnumerationGivesOneAnswer`, `TestMentionOfAReachingPersonIsNamed`.
    - the people list returns every matching user: `TestPeopleListAnswersOnlyReachingUsers`.
    - the people list open to tokens and keys (the first run was not caught, because the read token failed on role and the write token was not tried; the test now tries a write token too): `TestPeopleListGivesNothingToNonReachers`.
    - a comment looked up without its account (the first run was not caught, because the walk after it is account-scoped too; the test now asks the store directly): `TestCommentIDOfAnotherAccountIsNotFound`.
    - comment write rate limit removed: `TestCommentWriteRateLimit`.
    - edit, delete and resolve not limited (the review found them outside the budget): `TestEditDeleteAndResolveShareTheWriteLimit`.
    - mentions per comment at eleven: `TestMentionsPerCommentAreCapped`.
    - people list at six: `TestPeopleListCapsAtFive`.
    - people list rate limit removed: `TestPeopleListIsRateLimited`.
    - edit by any commenter: `TestOnlyTheAuthorEdits`.
    - shortcut refusal removed: `TestShortcutHasNoComments`.
    - delete never leaves a tombstone: `TestDeleteKeepsRepliesAsATombstone`.
    - the author's own mention kept: `TestMentionEnumerationGivesOneAnswer`.
    - control characters allowed in the shared rule (the first run was a build error, an unused import; the mutant now keeps the import in use): `TestBodyRules`, `FuzzCleanCommentBody`.
    - tombstone kept after its last reply: `TestDeleteKeepsRepliesAsATombstone`.
    - comments index without `node_id`: `TestCommentsSQLDoesNotScan` (store), eight plans scan.
    - the list ignores the switch: `TestCommentsSwitchOff`.
    - a reference not bound to its node: `TestMentionReferencesAreNodeBound`, `TestForgedOrForeignMentionIsRefused`.
    - a reply to a reply allowed: `TestReplyRules`.
    - mention resolution given no candidates: `TestMentionOfAReachingPersonIsNamed`.
    - two references to one person counted twice (the cap by reference string): `TestTwoReferencesToOnePersonMakeOneMention`.

    **Accepted items (the review's findings, and what the owner must know).**
    - *Duplicate display names.* Two people with the same display name look the same in the people list. The reference differs, so the choice is exact, but the list cannot tell them apart. r3 and r7 must revisit this (show a disambiguator, or the e-mail to the owner only).
    - *A replayed reference.* A reference is stable for one person and node, so a reference kept from an earlier people list gives the same answer as the list does now: named while the person reaches the node, dropped after.
    - *The write's answer names resolved mentions.* The write answer lists the names of the people it resolved, which the author may already see in the people list. Question 7 of the proposal said the answer carries no names; that wording is relaxed for this case, because the author has already been shown those names.

    **Not built, and open for the owner.** Notifications and the outbox (r3), the activity pane (r4), who-viewed (r5), the comment webhook event (r6), the web interface (r7). Assignment (question 14). Whether an account key may delete a comment (it may manage the node, but the table says user only). Whether a token may edit or resolve its user's comment.
40. **Search by name and label, slices q1 and q2** (2026-10-31, built to the owner-approved proposal for slice q with every recommendation, with two owner changes: names get substring search, and OCR is out of q). Decision 13 is amended to match: OCR is optional and a later slice. Content text is slice q3, and the web page is slice q4. Slice pg moves after q. The independent review of the first commit, and the owner's decisions on its findings, are under "Review round" below.
    - **Mechanism.** `search_names` holds one row per named node of a published folder, trashed or not; a folder root has no row, and neither does a staged node. The row's ID is the rowid of two contentful FTS5 tables of the folded name (`names.SearchForm`: marks removed, case folded). `search_words` (unicode61, `remove_diacritics 2`) answers word prefixes; `search_trigram` answers substrings of three or more characters. A term of fewer than three characters uses the word index only. The query checks `search_names.account_id` itself, so the FTS tables narrow the search but never decide access alone.
    - **Bulk writes record a rowid range, not a folder.** `search_backlog` holds items: the rowids of one folder's nodes in (cursor, upto]. A synchronous copy of at most `store.SearchSmallCopy` (100) nodes indexes its nodes in its own write, and records nothing. A larger synchronous copy records the rowids its transaction made (the largest rowid before and after it). A chunked publish records the rowid range of its staged nodes, which keep their rowids when they are published. The upgrade backfill and the admin rebuild record one item per published folder, covering all its rowids. The job reads an item in batches of 1,000, each batch its own short write, and yields between batches. A new item never moves another item's cursor, so frequent copies do not restart each other's work. A one-file copy into a folder of 100,000 nodes indexes its one node in its write and queues nothing (`TestOneFileCopyIntoALargeFolderQueuesNothing`). The nodes of a larger copy may take seconds to appear in search. That is a delay, never a leak: reach is checked at query time.
    - **No index change.** The first version replaced `nodes_folder (folder_id)` with `nodes_folder (folder_id, id)`, so a batch could start at its cursor. That made a 50,000-node publish slower (review finding 2, below). The rowid is the last column of the `(folder_id)` index, so a batch reads `folder_id = ? AND rowid > ? AND rowid <= ?` as one index range. Migration 0032 keeps `nodes_folder (folder_id)` as it was, and `TestSearchBatchUsesTheFolderIndex` reads the plan. Main has 0030 (comments) and 0031 (zip errors), so this change is 0032 and needs no placeholder.
    - **Subtree moves change no search row.** `MoveSubtree` and `MoveFolderContents` queue nothing. Rows are keyed by node ID, the name and the account do not change, and reach, trash and folder are read at query time, so what search shows follows the move without a row change. An earlier draft of this decision said that a move records its folder. That was wrong; the code had it right.
    - **Jobs: retry and wake.** A failed batch is returned as `jobs.RetryAfter`. The runner puts the job back, due after the wait, and does not finish it. The wait is 1 s, doubling with each failure in a row, up to 5 min; a success or a restart resets it. Queued search work brings a waiting job forward (`WakeJobs`), so a backlog does not wait out a retry when new work arrives. Tests: `TestRetriedJobWaitsThenRuns`, and the backoff bounds in `searchBackoff`.
    - **Upkeep.** The sweep checks the search rows once an hour (`searchCheckEvery`). A missing or extra row is repaired, which queues the folder ranges; a full-text table that disagrees with its rows is reported, and not repaired by the sweep. `selfcloud admin search-rebuild` empties the index and queues every folder, and the server's job refills it, so searches are partial until the job has run. Tests: `TestSweepRepairsMissingSearchRowsAtItsCheck`, `TestSearchRebuildEmptiesAndQueues`.
    - **Route.** `GET /api/v1/search` for a signed-in user, for an account key, and for a delegated token of either. It takes `q` (at most `search.max_query_bytes`, 200 by default) and the filters (`in`, `kind`, `ext`, dates, sizes, `label`, `scope`), and returns a page with no total and a cursor. Results show only the nodes the caller reaches. An account key reaches every node of its own account, as manager, and not the trash; a key of another account finds nothing (`TestAccountKeyOfAnotherAccountFindsNothing`). A delegated token, including one minted by an account key, sees only its folders and its node scope, and its role is capped (`TestTokenMintedByAccountKeyIsConfined`). A share-link visitor is refused by the route. A restricted label value matches only for a manager of the node. The search reads candidates in batches of 100 and answers with a cursor only when the limit is reached; a file the caller cannot reach never changes the answer, and `search.scan_budget` is removed (decision 46, review S1). The deadline (`search.timeout`, 2 s) answers `unavailable`. Searches are rate-limited per caller (`search.rate_per_minute`, 60) and per account at ten times that rate (decision 46, review S5). `search.enabled` set to `false` answers `not_found`, and the index is still kept.
    - **Cursor.** A cursor is sealed as a mention reference is: AES-GCM under a key derived from the links signing key (HKDF, label `selfcloud search cursor v1`), with the account, the caller's kind and ID, and the request's fingerprint as additional data. It holds the last candidate's row ID, which is shared by every account, but the holder cannot read it. The fingerprint covers every filter as typed, label values included (`LabelFilters`), so a cursor opens only for the request that made it. The typed label tests are read in the same snapshot before the cursor is opened. A key rotation (the current links key changes) invalidates every cursor. The answer is `invalid_request` with the message "cursor is not valid for this search; start the search again", and the client starts again: the first page after the rotation is the same as before it (`TestSearchCursorAfterAKeyRotationStartsAgain`).
    - **Scan budget counts candidates, and that is accepted.** The budget counts the candidates a request reads, not the rows the database examines. A filter that rejects nearly every row in SQL (a rare extension, a size range, `kind=dir` on a file-heavy account) can make one candidate query examine a whole account. The review measured 70 ms for such a query over 300,000 rows in memory (about 0.25 s per million). The 2 s deadline stops a running query, and a deadline answers `unavailable`. The owner accepts this: on a very large account a narrow filter may answer `unavailable` where a short page would have served.
    - **Search latency on a loaded host.** A search with a small result took about 0.37 s on the build host at a load average of about 25. A CPU profile puts most of that time in SQLite preparing statements (the modernc driver), not in the search. The large-folder test raises its deadline for this reason. The production default is unchanged.
    - **Measured: a 1,000,000-node backfill** (owner's request, `nice -n 19`, data under `/var/tmp`, measured on the first version, which used the composite index; the rowid design has not been re-measured at this size). Seeding took 3m47s. The backfill ran 1,050 batches of 1,000: longest write 2.76 s, mean 215 ms, wall 3m46s, inside the 15-minute bound. The database grew from 310.8 MiB to 633.6 MiB: 322.8 MiB, about 338 bytes a node for the three indexes together (the first draft said "about 320", which was wrong). The load average was 15 to 20 during the run. The cause of the longest write was not traced. An earlier 100,000-node run gave a longest write of 293 ms and a mean of 121 ms.
    - **Measured: a publish of 50,000 nodes, both indexes on.** `BenchmarkCopyPublish/nodes_50000` (the writer hold of a publish, the benchmark decision 34 records), three runs each, interleaved so both saw the same load (load average 4 to 8): base 8f4844b, hold 1284, 1471 and 1279 ms (mean 1345); this change, hold 1228, 1306 and 1446 ms (mean 1327). No measurable regression. This change is on main 16b78e4, whose other slices do not touch the publish path.
    - **Correction: the 12.8 s figure.** The first draft of this decision said a 50,000-node publish held the write for 12.8 s. That figure is the one line the copy run printed (`copy of 50000 nodes done in 2m9.567s; publish holds [12.771010501s]`, from `TestMeasureSearchBatchesAfterCopy` at a load average of 15 to 20, with the composite index in place). It is the API's copy publish phase, not the benchmark above. It is not the zip slice's "Set-up of 50,000 nodes in one write takes 12.8 s" (decision 35's paragraph), a separate measurement with the same rounded figure. The review could not reproduce it at lower load. The benchmark above replaces it. The same run measured the copy's index batches (100 batches of 1,000: longest 379 ms, mean 207 ms, wall 20.7 s, and no drift at the check), before the rowid change; they have not been measured again.
    - **Review round (the first commit).** The independent review found the following, and each has the outcome shown.
      1. *Label paging, HIGH.* A label-filtered search failed on its second page, because the cursor was decoded before the label tests were set. Fixed: the cursor is opened after them, the fingerprint holds the raw label filters, and a changed filter refuses the cursor. Tests: `TestSearchLabelPagesAcrossThreePages`, `TestSearchCursorRefusesAChangedLabelFilter`.
      2. *Publish slower, MEDIUM.* The composite index made the publish slower (the review measured about 75 percent). Fixed: the index is not changed, and the batches read the rowid range (above). The benchmark shows no regression.
      3. *A copy re-read the whole destination folder and reset its cursor, MEDIUM.* Fixed: a copy records its rowid range, a small copy indexes in its write, and each range is its own item (above). Tests: `TestOneFileCopyIntoALargeFolderQueuesNothing` (a 100,000-node folder), `TestItemsDoNotResetEachOther`, `TestSmallCopyIsSearchableAtOnce`, `TestLargeCopyAppearsAfterTheIndexJob`.
      4. *A failed search job was never retried, LOW to MEDIUM.* Fixed: retry with backoff, and the next queued work wakes the job (above). Test: `TestRetriedJobWaitsThenRuns`.
      5. *The check and repair paths had no caller, LOW.* Fixed: the sweep runs them hourly, and `admin search-rebuild` is the rebuild. Tests: `TestSweepRepairsMissingSearchRowsAtItsCheck`, `TestSearchRebuildEmptiesAndQueues`.
      6. *The scan budget counts candidates, LOW.* Accepted, with the measurement above.
      7. *The cursor was unkeyed and carried a global rowid, LOW.* Fixed: the cursor is sealed and bound to the account, the caller and the request (above). Test: `TestSearchCursorIsBoundToItsCallerAndAccount`.
      8. *The docs said more than the code did, LOW.* The subtree-move sentence and the header comment are corrected (above). The per-node size was corrected to about 338 bytes.
      9. *A staged-node filter could be removed unnoticed, LOW.* Fixed: the candidate query's staged filter has a test that plants a row for a staged node, `TestStagedRowsNeverMatch`. Mutation M09 kills it.
      10. *Account keys were refused, owner's question.* The owner decided: an account key may search (it reaches its own account, as on every other route), and so may a token minted by one, confined and role-capped. A share-link visitor is still refused. Tests: `TestAccountKeySearchesItsAccount`, `TestAccountKeyOfAnotherAccountFindsNothing`, `TestTokenMintedByAccountKeyIsConfined`.
      11. *The gate for the first commit failed on the node-kind guard.* Two new comparisons in the search code were unreviewed: the scope check, and the extension of a file's search row. Both are now reviewed and recorded in `reviewedNodeKindSites`. Neither decides access.
    - **Mutation proofs on the final tree.** Each mutation changes one line, runs the tests that must catch it, and is restored. KILLED means the tests failed under the mutation; SURVIVED would be a gap.
      Pass one (before the tests below were added) left three survivors, each a gap in the tests, not in the code: M04 (token node scope: no test confined a token to a directory), M07 (cursor caller binding: the second caller differed in kind, so the test could not tell callers of one kind apart) and M15 (query byte limit: no test sent a query over the limit). Each got a test (`TestSearchFollowsTheTokenNodeScope`, a second user in `TestSearchCursorIsBoundToItsCallerAndAccount`, `TestParseTermsRefusesALongQuery`) and the mutation was run again.
    - Pass two, the final tree, 15 of 15 KILLED:
      - *Access.* M01: the role check in the search loop removed (KILLED). M02: the trash refusal in the reach role removed (KILLED). M03: the token's folder list removed (KILLED). M04: the token's node scope removed (KILLED). M05: the account key's reach removed (KILLED). M06: the restricted-label rule for non-managers removed (KILLED). M07: the caller removed from the cursor's additional data (KILLED). M08: the label filters removed from the fingerprint (KILLED). M09: the staged filter removed from the candidate query (`f.staged = 0` replaced by `1 = 1` in both queries) (KILLED, `TestStagedRowsNeverMatch`). M10: the folder-delete removal of full-text rows (`dropSearchFolder`) removed (KILLED, `TestDeletingAFolderOrAnAccountRemovesItsFullTextRows`).
      - *Limits.* M11: the scan budget removed from the loop (KILLED). M12: the rate limit removed (KILLED). M13: the deadline removed (KILLED). M14: the maximum limit of 50 removed (KILLED). M15: the query byte limit removed (KILLED).
      - Not run: the mutation that removes the account's boundary from the candidate query. That condition is bound inside `MATCH` and the candidate arguments, so the change does not reduce to one line; the cross-account tests (`TestSearchDoesNotReadAnotherAccount`, `TestAccountKeyOfAnotherAccountFindsNothing`) are the check. Every mutation was restored after its run, and the restore was checked by grep.
    - **Deviations from the proposal.** Names only; content keys are deferred to q3. The write code is in `internal/store` rather than in a package above it, which avoids an import cycle. A `label_matches` table is omitted; label predicates read `node_labels` through the indexes that migration 0032 adds. There is no B-tree index on the name key. `search.enabled` set to `false` still indexes. Roots are excluded from the index, as they have no name. Account keys may search, which the proposal refused (review question 10, above); tokens are confined by their folder list and node scope, as the proposal approved.
41. **Installation admin access to tenant users, slice adm1** (2026-10-31). The owner decided the three ways in and the
    sign-in-as rules; the technical decisions below are the owner's on the same day.
    - *Owner's decisions.* Three ways in, each on its own: a one-time reset link shown to the admin; a password the admin
      types, which the user must change at the next sign-in; and sign-in as the user, a session for one hour. Sign-in as
      gives any user of a tenant full access, so the admin sees what that person sees, including My files. It cannot change
      a password or a sign-in setting while impersonating. It is audited under the admin's name in the tenant's log. It is
      off by default, behind `admin.tenant_access`, and the docs say plainly what enabling it means.
    - *One setting.* `admin.tenant_access` (default false) governs the reset link, the typed password and sign-in as. The
      email reset is always available, since it reaches the real user. Reason: a link or a typed password gives the same
      takeover as sign-in as, so gating only sign-in as would make the off default mean nothing.
    - *What off does not do.* An admin can already reach a tenant's files by creating an audited account key, whatever the
      setting is. The docs say so, so off is not read as a guarantee.
    - *Sessions and passwords.* The three ways need an admin session, not an API key. The admin re-enters its own password
      for each sign-in as and each typed password, with the wrong-password limit of `POST /me/password`.
    - *Cookies.* The main session cookie carries the impersonation session. The admin's own session cookie is parked in
      `selfcloud_admin` (`__Secure-` on https, because `__Host-` forbids a path), with the path of the Go back route,
      `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Strict`. The impersonated pages never carry it, and only the Go back route reads it. Go back
      checks the impersonation's CSRF token (the request's `Origin` must be this site), checks that the parked cookie is
      the one the impersonation parked (its hash is in `sessions.impersonator_session_hash`), restores the admin's session,
      and deletes the impersonation. It works after the hour has passed, so the admin can always come back. A restore that
      cannot be made still ends the impersonation and clears both cookies.
    - *Hard limit.* One hour from the start, not renewed: `authenticateSession` refuses an impersonation past its hour at
      once, and a use does not move its expiry. The row stays until the admin goes back, so the restore still works.
    - *Routes.* Each route carries a class (`route.imp` in `server.go`); a zero value is refused, and a test walks the
      table. Refused while impersonating: changing the password, the profile and the sign-in settings; sign-out; keys,
      tokens and webhooks; the account's settings; users (create, change, delete, verify, reset, sign-in links, token
      revocation); label fields; folder, group and grant settings; share links and sharing permissions; access-request
      decisions; ownership transfer; signed links; office editing; and the routes that set a session (sign-in, verify,
      reset, sign-in link). Allowed: reads, file and folder work in the user's reach, uploads, trash, versions, labels on a node,
      signed preview links (capped at the sign-in's end, review F8), and the go-back route. Refused, because each
      records something in the user's name or sends mail: stars, recent, the hidden-folder list, access requests,
      comments, notifications and their settings. The full list is the `imp:` field on each route, and
      `TestImpersonationAllowedWrites` pins the writes that stay open.
    - *Must-change.* A user whose password an admin typed reaches only `GET /me`, `POST /me/password` and sign-out. A
      reset link or the user's own password change clears the flag. An admin cannot sign in as a user with the flag set.
    - *Audit and views.* An audit entry made while impersonating names the admin (`impersonated_by`), and is not made
      private to a personal folder, so the tenant's owner can read it. This relaxes decision 18 for impersonated writes;
      the owner should confirm it. Views made while impersonating are not recorded (Recent and the view records).
      Background jobs carry the mark in their payload, so a zip, a copy or a move that finishes after the sign-in ended
      keeps it (review F5). Both audit viewers, the tenant owner's and the admin's, show the admin's name and that the
      change was made signed in as the user, in all seven catalogues (`audit.viaAdmin`, review F6). The name is the
      admin's display name or email, so a tenant owner can read which installation admin acted.
    - *Webhooks.* An event's payload carries the node and the event type, not an actor (decision 27). An event for an
      impersonated write carries `impersonated: true` and never the admin's ID (the owner's decision, review F6).
    - *Ending.* Going back ends the impersonation. Ending every session of the user (a password change or reset, or a
      disable) ends an impersonation of that user, and removing the admin ends the impersonations it began; each end is
      audited under the admin. Logout is refused while impersonating, so Go back is the only way out.
    - *Scope.* A user is looked up in the account the path names, so another account's user, and an installation admin,
      are not found.
    - *Deviations from the brief, for the owner to confirm.* Office editing is refused while impersonating, since its
      token outlives the session. Signed links are allowed and capped at the sign-in's end (review F8). The session's `GET /me` is open, because the
      change-password page reads its CSRF token from it. An admin cannot sign in as a user whose password must change.
    - *Inbox and comments.* While impersonating, the user's notifications are neither read, marked read nor changed, and
      the notification settings are neither read nor changed; the handlers refuse it too (`ownNotifyCaller`). A comment is
      not written, edited, deleted or resolved in the user's name: a comment sends mention and reply mail as the person who
      wrote it, and that mail would be sent under the user's name for an admin's act, so these routes are refused rather
      than audited. Reading comments stays open. `TestImpersonatedInboxRefused` and `TestNotifyCallerRefusesImpersonation`
      check it.
    - *Review round (2026-10-31, independent security review, F1 to F10).* Each item has its test or a mutation proof.
      **F1:** an installation admin's key is never handed a link to a user that exists (a reset or a resend), whatever
      `admin.tenant_access` says; it may still create a user and mail that user's link, as before. **F2:** turning
      `admin.tenant_access` off ends a running sign-in-as on its next request; Go back still restores the admin.
      **F3:** an admin who changes its password, signs out, has its session ended by five wrong passwords, or is disabled
      or reset loses the sign-ins-as it began, each audited with its reason. **F4:** `POST /nodes/{nod}/access-requests` is
      refused while impersonating. The writes that stay open are listed in `TestImpersonationAllowedWrites`. The open
      writes that send mail or leave a record in the user's name are the unsubscribe link, the anonymous forgot-password
      route, and share open and renew (token-only). **F5:** the job payload carries the mark (zip, copy, move). **F6:** see
      above. **F7:** a reset link from an admin's session needs the admin's own password, as a typed password does, and
      the dialog asks for it. The email reset still needs none, as it reaches the user. **F8:** the viewer's preview link
      is a signed link; the browser step in `adminAccess.mjs` makes, reads and downloads a file while signed in as the
      member, and the link is capped at the sign-in's end. **F9:** while the banner shows, the shell fills the window below
      it and its content column scrolls inside it, so the page does not scroll (the page was 814px in a 800px window, the
      shell's content being 14px taller than the window once the banner took its 48px); `adminAccess.mjs` asserts it on the
      files list and the home page, and prints the heights. The banner text is
      4.63:1 on its background in light (`#B45309` on `#FFF6D1`) and 8.21:1 in dark (`#FECC00` on `#2A363A`), computed from
      the palette in `web/src/theme/tokens.ts`. **F10:** go-back with a wrong Origin is refused by the route and by the
      handler (`TestGoBackWithAWrongOriginIsRefused`).
      **Not changed, for the owner:** an account key still makes a reset link to a user of its own account, as it did
      before this slice (`TestCallersOfTheAdminWaysAreRefused` pins it). The review asked for refusal; a key can already
      make a sign-in link, which the design accepts (section 8), so refusing it here is the owner's call.
    - *Live run (after 2024b97).* The tenant's audit log read the admin's rows as "Someone made a change", and a wrong
      password as a sign-in. The viewers name only the tenant's people, and an installation admin belongs to no account.
      Fixed: the server marks an admin's row (`actor_admin`, and `actor_name`, which is empty for a removed admin, so the
      viewers say "an installation admin"); each sign-in-as, go-back, password set and reset-link action has its own
      sentence in all seven catalogues; a refused password is `admin.password_refused` with its way (`sign_in_as`,
      `typed_password`, `reset_link`), never a sign-in row. A go-back reads with its reason. Setting
      `admin.tenant_access` off writes no end row, so no sentence says it. `TestEveryAuditActionHasASentence` fails for an
      audit action with no sentence unless the action is on the list of older actions that still have none (57 when this
      was written; each reads as "made a change"). The list only shrinks.
      *Closed by slice audit-s1.* Each of the 57 older actions has its own sentence in `web/src/lib/audit/sentence.ts`,
      named from the fields its writer already records (a name, a count, a flag, the outcome); a field the row lacks falls
      back to a generic sentence, never to a raw ID. No server field was added. `noSentenceYet` is now empty, and the test
      keeps its two-way check. The Hebrew and Arabic sentences of this slice are machine drafts, not reviewed by a native
      speaker.
    - *Migration.* `0034_admin_access.sql` (sessions gain the impersonator columns; `users.must_change_password`). It follows
      `0033`, the notifications migration of slice r3, which is on main.
42. **Media viewer, slice s4c** (2026-10-31, built on the owner's request to play video, audio and images in the web interface; the server is unchanged). The faults were reproduced in Chrome on 16b78e4 before the fix: the e2e test `web/e2e/media.mjs` failed there on the double clicks, the tap, the layout, the labels and the playback.
    - *Double click.* The first click selected the item and inserted the selection bar above the listing, so the second click landed on another row. The bar now sits under the listing, sticky at the bottom of the window, so selecting moves no row, in List and Tiles, at desktop and phone width, in English and Hebrew. A double click opens the item the pointer was on, read from its row's ID when the event arrives, whatever was selected before.
    - *Touch.* A finger's tap opens a file or a folder, and a mouse click selects, as a double click opens. The kind of pointer is the pointer event's `pointerType`, read at `pointerdown`, not the window's width: a touch laptop follows each interaction (a finger taps, a mouse or trackpad selects). The list keeps its checkboxes. A tile gets a checkbox when the main pointer is coarse (`(pointer: coarse)`), since a tile has no other way to select on a finger's screen. A pen acts as a mouse.
    - *Names.* The action reads Play for video and audio, View for images and Preview for the rest, in all seven catalogues. A video or audio row, tile, node row and public browse row shows a small play mark with a screen-reader word ("Video" or "Audio"). Enter on a focused row already opened it (`keyAction`), and the e2e test checks it.
    - *Long media.* A signed link ends at its `expires_at` (`ttl` 300 s from the viewer). `handleGetLink` checks the link's end on every request, Range requests included, so the browser's next range after the end is refused with `link_expired` (410). A seek or the next piece of a long file therefore failed after five minutes. The player (`MediaPlayer`) asks for a new link when a media error comes after playback has moved on from the place the current link began at, and resumes at the same place, playing or paused as before. The decision reads no clock (`mediaVerdict` in `lib/files/media.ts`), because the server's `expires_at` and the browser's clock may disagree. The count of links asked for in a row is bounded at three for stalls, and it starts again only once playback has moved on. The TTL is unchanged: the viewer still sends `ttl` 300, and a server with `links.max_ttl` below 300 s refuses that request as before. A link the server ends early is renewed the same way, since nothing depends on how long a link was meant to last (`MediaPlayer.test.tsx`).
    - *Formats.* A media error before playback moves on asks for one new link, since a link that has ended fails the same way. If the fresh link fails the same way with a decode or source code, the file is an unsupported format: the viewer says "This browser can't play this format." and offers Download when the file allows it, and asks for no further link. A network code on a fresh link is an error, not a format. The same player serves the public browse page, which renews through the visitor credential; a refused credential is the page's answer, as before.
    - *Stalls.* A stall while playing waits 4 s, then asks for a link, within the count above. Once the count is spent, the player keeps buffering and shows no error: only a media error reaches the viewer's failure handling. A refused download on a renewal shows the same restricted card as the first load.
    - *Tests.* `web/e2e/media.mjs` (run by the gate): double click on the first and a lower row, in both views, with nothing selected; a tap on a phone for a file and a folder, and the tile checkbox; the layout check; the labels; playback of a video, an audio file and a picture; the long-video renewal, with the browser's next range held until the link has ended; the unsupported file. Unit tests: `lib/files/media.test.ts` (the error mapping, the bounded count, the stale-answer gate) and `components/files/MediaPlayer.test.tsx`.
    - *Same address.* The signed token is `nod|acc|disp|exp` with `exp` in whole seconds and no nonce (`internal/api/links.go`), so two links asked for in the same second are identical. A renewal that returns the failed address is not loaded again by the browser, so no event would follow; the player treats it as the fresh link failing the same way (`MediaPlayer.test.tsx`, "treats a fresh link with the address that failed"). Found by the e2e broken-file step, which waited on a message that never came. The server is not changed.
    - *Review fixes, same slice.* A tap or double click in a rename field no longer opens the item, in List and Tiles (`Listing.tsx`). A player's answer for one file is shown only for that file (`shownState`, `Preview.tsx`). A second tap within 400 ms of a finger's open does not open anything (`tapOpens`, `lib/files/tap.ts`): a double tap on a folder otherwise opened a file inside it, since the folder's rows can be on screen within the tap gap. At phone width the selection bar is one row: the main action, a More menu (antd Dropdown) with the rest, Delete last and marked as destructive, and Clear. Desktop shows every action, as before. The first-load gzip size was measured with `check-dist.mjs`.
    - *Live run, found after the push.* On a real listing of 14 files, the first click of a double click made the sticky bar appear over the lower rows, and the second click landed on the bar: one double click opened "Copy to…", others opened nothing. The test's folder was too short to show it. A new selection bar now lets clicks pass through it for 500 ms (`BAR_SETTLE_MS`), so the second click reaches the row. `web/e2e/media.mjs` uses a short window to put the row where the bar lands, with clicks 100 and 300 ms apart; it failed before the fix, with "opened nothing; dialog Copy to…". It also checks that a settled bar takes a real mouse click.
    - *Not changed.* The server, the link TTL, the no-download rule and the sharing rules. Decisions 40 and 41 are not in this file, and their numbers are not filled in.
43. **Notifications, the mail outbox and the email switch, slice r3** (2026-10-31, built to the owner-approved proposal for slice r (`design-r-proposal.md`) with every recommendation: an email carries the actor's name, the item's name, a count and a link, and no comment text; at most one email an hour and 20 a day per user; a user may switch email off, and an owner cannot force it on; in-app stays on for everyone). Migration 0033: 0031 went to zip errors and 0032 to search (decision 40), which is on main. Built: the notification rows, written in the comment's write; the outbox; the worker; the comment and digest mail in seven languages; the unsubscribe headers and page; the in-app list, bell count and mark-read; the email switch. Not built: shares and requests in the app (r7), the activity pane (r4), who-viewed (r5), the comment webhook (r6), the web interface (r7).

    **Interpretations and deviations, each stated where the proposal is silent, differs or contradicts itself.**
    - *Tables.* `notifications`, `notify_outbox` and `notify_prefs` as the proposal's section 4.2 gives them, with three changes. (a) The budget is in `notify_prefs` (`last_mail_at`, `mail_day_start`, `mail_day_count`) and an index on account and last mail, not in memory: the in-memory limiter of section 7.3 would not hold across a restart or two instances. (b) `actor_id` is nullable and `SET NULL` on user deletion, so a deleted actor reads as gone. (c) A notification carries no name and no text, and a test reads the columns to hold that (`TestNotifyRowsCarryNoText`). The proposal's `mail.notify.*` in-memory buckets are not built.
    - *last_error* holds a fixed code (`user`, `pref`, `comment`, `reach`, `actor`, `smtp`, `render`, `charge`, `hour`, `day`, `account`, `expired`), never the server's text, since an SMTP reply can name an address. The proposal allowed 200 characters of text.
    - *Delivery is at-least-once.* A pass claims rows in one write under a two-minute lease, sends with no transaction open, and records the outcome only while it still holds the lease. A crash after the send and before the record sends the row again once the lease ends; the hour's budget then holds that second mail back for an hour. The Message-ID is `ntf.<lowest outbox id>@<public host>`, so a client can merge a repeat of the same rows. Two passes on one database cannot claim one row (`TestTwoPassesSendOneMail`).
    - *The charge is made before the send, and a failed send keeps it,* as a drop link's count does (`notifyDrop`). A refused mail therefore waits an hour, not a minute.
    - *Budget.* One mail an hour per user, measured from the last charge. Twenty a day, in a day that starts at the first charge and runs 24 hours. At most 200 users of one account charged in an hour (`NotifyAccountHourCap`). A refused row stays pending, with no attempt counted, until the budget allows it. The worker stops charging a user once a row is refused and leaves the row for its next time.
    - *Digest.* One pass claims at most 20 rows of a user (`notifyRowsPerUser`), and one mail covers those that survive the checks. The rest wait for the next mail, an hour on. A digest names up to five items and counts the rest.
    - *Failures.* A refused send counts one attempt and waits the webhook's backoff (`webhook.Backoff`). Eight refusals make the row `failed`. A pass stops after three refusals in a row and leaves the rest pending with no attempt counted, so a server that is down does not hold other accounts for the length of its timeouts.
    - *Send-time checks (section 7.4), per row.* The user is active; email is on; the comment is live (a tombstone or a removed comment is skipped); the user reaches the node through the walk with organisation links (`reachesNode`), which also covers a trashed or missing node; the actor is named. A deleted actor is skipped, because a mail with no name would read oddly. Each check reads the state of the send, and a skipped row builds no text.
    - *Names in mail and the autolink.* `mail.Name` removes format characters (the bidi marks, embeddings and isolates), turns breaks and controls into spaces, and places an invisible non-joiner (U+200C) before each dot and after a colon that a slash follows, so a mail client does not link `example.com` or `https://...` in a name. Readers copy the text with the non-joiner; `mail.UnlinkableName` returns the text without it. The two new templates use it. The share and drop templates still use `mailText` only: the open item "mailText autolink across all mail templates" in `pending.md` remains open for them.
    - *Duplicate display names (review r1, item 3).* Not solved in r3. The inbox row and the mail carry a display name and nothing that tells two people apart, so two people with one name look alike to the reader of a notification. The row keeps `actor_id` internally, and no API answer exposes it (decision 39: no raw IDs in anything a person reads). Slice r7 must decide the disambiguator, for example the e-mail to managers only, or a mark on a shared name. The residual is stated, not fixed.
    - *A reply's notice is about the reply.* The notification's comment is the new comment. A reply whose parent is later deleted still notifies, since the reply is live; the parent's text is in no mail, and the parent is a tombstone.
    - *Mention and reply to one person.* One notification, the mention. A parent's author who is also mentioned gets the mention only.
    - *No mail configured.* The inbox works. No outbox row is written, and a pass does nothing. Rows left from a time when mail was configured wait until the sweep expires them.
    - *Unsubscribe (section 7.4).* The token is the account ID and the user ID sealed with AES-256-GCM, under a key derived with HKDF from the links signing key with its own label, and with `notify.email` as additional data. It opens nothing but the email switch. Every other route refuses it as a bearer token (`TestUnsubscribeTokenOpensNothingElse`). It has no expiry, so an old mail still works, and it opens under the previous key too. A GET shows a confirmation and changes nothing. A POST, from the page or from a mail client (RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`), sets the email off, with no session and no cookie. A valid token for a user who is gone gets the same success page, so the answer does not say whether the person exists. A changed token gets one generic 400. The page is in English and has no script. No `sameSite` check is made: no cookie is read, so a cross-site form has no authority without the token.
    - *Routes.* `GET /notifications` (a page, with the item's name read now), `GET /notifications/unread` (the bell, at most 100 newest unread rows checked for reach, with `more` when it stopped there), `POST /notifications/{ntf}/read`, and `GET|PATCH /notifications/settings`. A signed-in user only: a token of any scope and an account key are refused. No route sets another user's switch, so an owner cannot force email on for a member. The in-app list leaves out a notification whose item the reader no longer reaches, and it is kept, so it shows again when the reach returns. It leaves out a notification of a tombstoned comment too.
    - *Limits, stated.* A write makes at most one reply notice and ten mention notices, so eleven rows and eleven reach walks, all in the comment's write. Notifications per user: 500 (`NotifyPerUser`), the oldest removed in the write that passes the cap, with their mail rows. Notifications kept 90 days, mail rows that finished kept 7 days, and a pending row older than 7 days is expired as skipped (the sweep, every five minutes, in batches of 500). Pending mail: 100,000 rows (`NotifyPendingLimit`); past it a notification is written with no mail queued. Mail per user: one an hour, twenty a day. Per account: 200 users an hour. The unread count reads at most 100 rows. The send checks read the item's name at send time, so a renamed item shows its current name (`TestRenamedItemShowsItsCurrentName`).
    - *Failure of the mail server.* A row is never dropped while it has attempts left. It counts an attempt, waits its backoff, and is `failed` only after eight. The notification stays in the inbox throughout.
    - *Logs.* A log line of the worker holds the purpose, a count or a code, never a comment's text, a name, an address or the send's error text (`TestNotifyLogsCarryNoTextOrAddress`).
    - *Headers.* Every header value is checked for a line break before anything is written (`checkHeader`): the subject, the Message-ID, and the unsubscribe address. The new headers are `Message-ID`, `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post`.

    **Plans and measurements.** `TestNotificationSQLDoesNotScan` reads the plan of every statement the notification path runs, and fails on a scan of `notifications`, `notify_outbox` or `notify_prefs` by table. The claim reaches its rows through `notify_outbox_due`, the list through `notifications_user`, the unread count through the partial index `notifications_unread`, the cap through `notifications_user`, the age prune through `notifications_created`, and the mail prunes through `notify_outbox_done`. The one scan the plans show is of a common table expression (`SCAN due`), which is a sort of the due users and not of a table.

    `TestNotificationsAtScale` (skipped unless `SELFCLOUD_SCALE` is set) was run by hand on the code after the review round, which added the fair claim and the per-account index, with `TMPDIR` on `/var/tmp` at `nice -n 19` and a fifteen-minute limit. The fixture is 1,000,000 comments, 1,000,000 notifications (10,000 users, 100 each, on one node) and 100,000 pending mail rows, all due now, all in one account. Each figure is the median of the runs and the worst run in brackets:

    | Operation | Median (worst) |
    |---|---|
    | Claim: 50 users, 20 rows each, with 100,000 rows due | 174 ms (224 ms) |
    | Unread count: the newest 100 unread rows of one user | 0.75 ms (4.4 ms) |
    | Inbox: first page of 50 of one user (500 kept) | 0.37 ms (0.64 ms) |
    | Pending cap count, capped at 100,000 | 11.2 ms (19.5 ms) |
    | Comment write: one comment, one notification and one mail row, at the cap | 13.6 ms (24.6 ms) |
    | Charge: one user not yet charged | 0.24 ms (0.35 ms) |
    | Age prune, one batch of 500 (no row was old) | 46 ms (56 ms) |
    | Expire, one batch of 500 (no row was old) | 9.9 ms (18.6 ms) |

    The two costs that grow with the queue are the claim, which reads every due row once a minute, and the pending-cap count, which reads up to 100,000 outbox rows in each comment write. At the cap the count is most of the comment write's time. A counter kept in the database would avoid it, but two instances would then race on it; the count is kept as it is, and the number is stated here. These are one run on one machine with a warm cache, and the fixture has one account, so it does not measure a claim shared across many accounts. They show the statements do not grow with the history of a user; they are not a load test.

    **Review round (2026-10-31, independent review of the first commit, and the coordinator's notes).** Each finding is fixed, with a test that failed before the fix or a mutation that the test kills. The review's file is `review-r3.md` in the plans directory.
    - *D1, reach shared across users (high).* The send-time reach was cached by node only, so the first user of a pass decided for every other user on that node. The cache is now keyed by user and node (`passKey`). `TestOnePassChecksReachPerUser` puts two users with mail on one node into one pass, in both orders, with one who lost access and one disabled. Before the fix bob-first mailed the user who had lost access, and carol-first skipped bob for good.
    - *D2, a failed read skipped the row (medium).* A store error, or a cancelled context at shutdown, is no longer a skip. The row goes back pending with no attempt counted. Only a definite answer skips: user inactive, email off, comment gone, item not reached, or too old. `TestTransientReadErrorKeepsTheRow` cancels the context during a send and checks the row is pending with `attempts` at 0.
    - *D3, one account stops mail for all (medium-low).* A new per-account cap of pending mail, `NotifyAccountPendingLimit` = 10,000 rows, sits in front of the global `NotifyPendingLimit` = 100,000, which is now only a backstop. An account over its cap gets no mail queued for new notifications; its in-app items are unchanged, and other accounts are not affected. `TestAccountPendingCapLeavesOtherAccountsMail` fails with the per-account check replaced by the global cap. The claim ranks users by account (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ...)`, as the webhook claim does), so one account's backlog cannot take every slot; `TestClaimIsFairAcrossAccounts` checks two slots go to two accounts. The index that counts an account's pending rows is `notify_outbox_account (account_id, state)`.
    - *D4, an address in place of a name (low).* The mail and the in-app list read names through one helper, `personName` (nodes.go), which applies the rule of the comment page (`peopleNamesSeen`, and the names from `UserNames`). The mail's fallback to the email is gone. A person with no display name is named in the mail by a label in the recipient's language (`mail.ActorLabel`, seven languages, with `TestActorLabelInEveryLanguage` checking each one); the in-app item has no `actor_name` and `actor_gone` stays false. The comment page shows the author with no name in that same case (`author_name` omitted), so the page and the notification agree. The mail's recipient is always a member of the account, so the rule admits every mail recipient; the hidden case is reached only by a principal the routes do not admit, and `TestPersonNameFollowsTheRule` covers it at the helper. `TestActorWithoutNameIsLabelled` checks the subject carries the label and no address.
    - *D5, comments switched off (low).* While an account's comments are off, its rows wait: no mail is sent, the row keeps its place and no attempt is counted (held for 10 minutes at a time). The inbox list and the bell show nothing for that account; the rows are kept. When the switch comes back on, a row older than `notifyMailMaxAge` (48 hours) is skipped as `late`, and younger rows are sent under the usual hour and day budgets, so a long switch-off does not flood. The limit is 48 hours, not 24, because a row that waits for the day's cap can be a day old. `TestCommentsOffHoldsMailAndHidesTheInbox` and `TestOldRowsAreNotMailedWhenCommentsReturn`.
    - *Lease survivors.* The row-level lease check alone is now killed by `TestLeasedRowsAreNotClaimedAgain` (25 due rows, 20 a claim: the second claim must return the other 5 and none the first holds). The user-level check alone is killed by `TestLeasedUserTakesNoSlot` (a user whose rows are all leased must not take the only slot from a user with rows due).
    - *Disabled user (survivor, previously called equivalent).* The reach walk also refuses a disabled user, so the status check was not the only guard. The test now asserts the skip reason `user` for the disabled user's row, so removing the status check is observable.
    - *Retention (`pruneNotifications`).* `TestSweepPrunesNotifications` runs `Sweeper.Once` over a notification past ninety days, a pending mail past a week, and a finished mail row past a week, and checks each count and each row.
    - *Impersonation (not built here).* No impersonation flag exists yet in `auth`. The places that need the check are `ownNotifyCaller` in `internal/api/notify_routes.go` (the inbox, the bell, mark-read and the email switch) and the actor that `commentNotices` takes from `p.UserID` in `internal/api/comments.go`. The slice that adds impersonation must refuse or label both.
    **Mutation proofs (final tree, after the rebase on f7f08dd).** One change at a time, each restored, and the tree checked for residue after the run (only the test change of the sweep check was left, as intended). Killed (the named tests fail on the change): the reach cache keyed by node only (D1, `TestOnePassChecksReachPerUser`); the reach check at send removed (`TestLosingReachHidesAndSkipsMailThenShowsAgain`); the status check removed (`TestEmailSwitchAndDisabledUserSendNothing`, by its reason `user`); a failed read skipping a row (D2, `TestTransientReadErrorKeepsTheRow`); comments off ignored at send, and in the inbox (`TestCommentsOffHoldsMailAndHidesTheInbox`); late rows mailed (`TestOldRowsAreNotMailedWhenCommentsReturn`); an address in place of a label for an actor with no name (D4, `TestActorWithoutNameIsLabelled`); the name rule removed from `personName` (`TestPersonNameFollowsTheRule`); the per-account pending cap ignored (D3, `TestAccountPendingCapLeavesOtherAccountsMail`); the claim not ranked by account (D3, `TestClaimIsFairAcrossAccounts`); the row-level lease check removed (`TestLeasedRowsAreNotClaimedAgain`); the user-level lease check removed (`TestLeasedUserTakesNoSlot`); both removed (`TestClaimLeasesEachRowOnce` with the two tests above); the prune not wired into the sweep, and the keep cut to an hour (`TestSweepPrunesNotifications`); the deleted comment still mailed; the email switch ignored at send; an author notified of their own reply (`TestAuthorIsNeverNotified`); a disabled user mailed (`TestEmailSwitchAndDisabledUserSendNothing`); the hour budget not charged (`TestDigestIsOneMailAnHour`); an address written to the log (`TestNotifyLogsCarryNoTextOrAddress`); a refused server not stopped after three (`TestFailingServerStopsThePassAndLeavesTheRest`); a forged unsubscribe token, and the unsubscribe page changing state on GET (`TestUnsubscribeLinkOfAMail`); a token reading the inbox (`TestNotificationRoutesRefuseTokensAndKeys`); mark-read across users (`TestMarkReadIsOwnRowsOnly`); the hour limit removed in the database (`TestHourAndDayBudget`, `TestBudgetHoldsAcrossReopen`); the day cap raised (`TestHourAndDayBudget`); the account hour cap removed (`TestAccountHourCap`); the per-user cap removed (`TestPerUserCapKeepsNewest`); the autolink break removed (`TestNameBreaksAutolinks`); format and bidi characters kept (`TestNameDropsBreaksControlsAndBidi`, `TestNotificationMailHasNoHeaderInjection`); the unsubscribe address and the Message-ID not checked for breaks (`TestUnsubscribeHeadersAreRFC8058`); the French comment template missing (`TestEveryPurposeInEveryLanguage`); comments writing no notifications (`TestMentionMailsWithoutTextAndListsIt`).
    **Survived, and why.** (1) The global pending cap ignored (`TestPendingCapStopsQueueing`): the test fills one account, and the per-account cap of 10,000 stops it first, so the 100,000 backstop is reached only when ten or more accounts are each near their cap. No test covers that, and the backstop is not proved by a mutation here. (2) The inbox's reach filter removed with the lookup kept: equivalent, because `NodesByID` is called with the kept nodes only, so a node the filter would drop is nil. It is killed when the lookup is widened too (`TestLosingReachHidesAndSkipsMailThenShowsAgain`).
    **Superseded, not run as written.** Five entries of the first list had patterns that no longer match the code after the rework (the reach check, the deleted comment, the email switch, the inbox filter and the pending cap). Each was rerun on its current text: the reach check, the deleted comment and the email switch are killed; the inbox filter is the equivalent case above; the pending cap is replaced by the two D3 mutants. The first list's row-level lease mutant ran only `TestClaimLeasesEachRowOnce`, which has no 25-row user, so it survived; with the two new lease tests it is killed.
44. **File browser toolbar, right-click menu and clipboard keys, slice w1** (2026-10-31, built to the owner-approved proposal for slice w (`design-w-proposal.md`), with its items 1 to 4 and every recommendation, and then to the owner's screenshot of 2026-11-01: "selecting a file should be like in Google Drive, the panel on top, not at the bottom"). The web interface only; the server is unchanged here.
    - *Toolbar.* One row, always on top, under the header (56 px), and it never wraps (`flexWrap: nowrap`). It holds New (a menu, with words), the sort (grid view only: one icon button that opens a menu of the fields and the direction, the current ones marked), and the view toggle (one icon that shows the view it switches to, with its name as the label). Selecting moves no row: the toolbar's row is the same height whether or not something is selected.
    - *Selection panel.* While something is selected, the panel takes the toolbar's row: one full-width rounded bar, tinted with `colorFill`, a grey that shows on the page in light and dark (the primary tint was too faint against the page), at the same height (32 px with a mouse, 44 px on a finger). From left to right, mirrored in Hebrew: X (clears), the count (one line; it shrinks with an ellipsis rather than wrap or push anything), then icons with tooltips and labels: Share, Download, Move, Delete (red), and More for the rest. Only what the role allows is shown (`hidden`). Below 360 px the panel keeps Share and Download and puts Delete, Move and the rest in More. Clearing brings the usual row back in the same place.
    - *No bottom bar.* The phone's bottom bar, its settle timer (`BAR_SETTLE_MS`) and its `pointerEvents` gate are removed. The settle timer existed because the bottom bar could appear under a finger over a row; the panel covers no row, so a double click reaches the row. The double-click check stays (`a double click on a row opens it on a short phone`, `a double click on the lowest visible rows opens that row`).
    - *Share and Copy link.* Share opens the share dialog, which is where links are made. A Copy link action is not built: there is no such action in the app, and one would make links from the panel, which is outside this slice (owner's choice to confirm).
    - *Selected rows and tiles.* A selected row or tile has a 2 px outline in the primary colour and the primary tint. A tile keeps its 1 px border too.
    - *Tiles on a phone.* The star sits in the tile's top right corner as a 44 px target, not in the middle: a tap on the middle opens the file, and a tap on the star stars the file and opens nothing (checked). The tile's middle is the phone test's tap point.
    - *Width.* The toolbar was 512 px wide on a 390 px phone (measured: the page's scroll width, not its content). Its nowrap row held the sort, the reverse button and the view group at a width the row could not hold. Now the row fits: the 390 and 320 px checks pass in List and Tiles, with and without a selection, in English and Hebrew (`a phone window of 390 and of 320 pixels fits its page`). Those checks were shown to fail with a 185 px toggle (scrollWidth 326 at 320 px, Tiles).
    - *Touch.* Toolbar buttons are 44 by 44 on a finger, icon-only ones included (`minWidth` set as well as `minHeight`). Menu items are 44 px: the antd menu's own item height does not reach a dropdown's items, so the height is set on each item (`touchItem`).
    - *Focus.* Clear moves the focus to the listing before it disables itself: a disabled button drops focus to the body.
    - *Pickers.* The hidden file pickers stay mounted while the panel shows, so Upload and New work from either.
    - *Sort arrow.* The active column of the list header shows its direction as an arrow after the label (lucide, `aria-hidden`); the other columns keep an empty 14 px box, so the labels do not move. The header's name stays the label alone. Reads right to left: the arrow sits after the label in reading order.
    - *Keys.* Backspace and Alt+Up go to the parent folder; plain letters and Backspace do nothing in a field, a dialog or a rename, and keys are ignored while a dialog is open.
    - *Clipboard.* Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V act inside the tab over the copy and move routes, so each paste is an undoable transfer job. Cut items are dimmed until pasted or cancelled. The clipboard is cleared on sign-out and account switch by a module subscription, not by the page's unmount. A paste that is still running is not repeated by a held key (`pasting` guard). A partly failed cut keeps the items that did not move.
    - *Menus.* The right-click menu is grouped with dividers and hides what does not fit the selection. A long press (500 ms, a finger that moves less than 10 px) opens it on a finger.
    - *Upload tray.* It folds itself when the last upload ends, and reopens when an upload is added or fails.
    - *English retry.* If the English catalogue cannot be read twice, the page shows an English-only notice with a Try again button. The e2e check for it now answers the file itself (`page.pausedHook`): the run's global listener used to answer first, and the browser's memory cache could serve the chunk without a request.
    - *First load.* 322.6 KB gzip of 330 KB (`check-dist`); the entry is 114.1 KB of 290, the largest other chunk 95.8 KB of 120, the largest language 18.7 KB of 25.
    - *Rebase.* Onto ea14078 (decision 48, the audit log, which has no shared code with this slice), and before that onto 941d9eb (decision 47): the listing takes its order from the server, so the sort menu only sets the sort key and direction the server reads. A failed read of the same sort keeps the rows (decision 47's rule).

End to end: the last full run, `web/e2e/run.mjs`, was 316 PASS and 0 FAIL before the review fixes; the review's e2e changes (items 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8) are written and are checked by the gate run, not by a local run. The run's temporary directories are set under `TMPDIR` on the home disk, because the `/tmp` tmpfs filled (507 from the server).

(4) The sort arrow removed: the two arrow tests fail; the accessible-name and width tests pass.
