45. **Video and audio player and playlist, slice x1** (2026-10-31, built to the owner's request for a player in the web interface, with decision 45 of the design proposal `design-w-proposal.md`; the server is unchanged). Reviewed twice the same day; the findings of both rounds and their fixes are listed below.
    - *Controls.* The bar is the player's own, in place of the browser's: play, a seek bar with the buffered part, time, volume, mute, speed, full screen (video) and picture in picture (video). On a video the bar is a dark scrim over the picture with light icons and no filled buttons, and a dark control set in both page themes. An audio's bar and the playlist panel take the page's colours from the palette, so they follow the theme. The bar reads left to right in every language, and its sliders too: a click on the seek bar seeks to the matching place. Keys: K or Space play and pause, J and L move 10 s, the arrows move 5 s and change the volume, M mutes, F full screen, N and P next and previous. A key typed into a text field is left to the field.
    - *Space.* Space plays and pauses the player, except where the keyboard holds a control whose own Space is what the person asked for: a button, link, box, tab, menu item or list that the keyboard reached (`:focus-visible`, so Tab brings it). A press with the pointer leaves the focus on the control it hit, but that is not keyboard focus, so Space plays or pauses after a click. The viewer does not put the focus on its Close button when it opens, so a Space press on a new viewer reaches the player. A slider does not take Space. A held key acts once for Space, K, F, M, N and P; the arrows and J and L repeat, so a held arrow keeps seeking or changing the volume. A Space the player handled has its keyup cancelled, so a browser does not click the button the pointer last hit; this is checked in unit tests and in Chrome only. Firefox's keyup behaviour is not checked here.
    - *Press to play.* When the browser refuses a play for want of a press (`NotAllowedError`), the bar shows "The browser waits for you to press Play." (`files.media.pressPlay`, in all seven catalogues) until the file plays. Any other refusal shows nothing; the element's own error events report a file that cannot play.
    - *Playlist.* The files of a folder, read a page at a time (50 per page), or the selection, with shuffle, repeat off, all or one, add next, add to end, remove, and reorder by drag, by the More menu (Move up, Move down, Remove) or by Alt with the arrow keys. A row is one line at every width, its name cut with an ellipsis and in full on hover; the file on screen is marked with an icon, the word and its row colour, and kept in view. In a selection the add panel offers only the folder pages already loaded that are not in the queue; its Load more reads the next page, and is the only way the panel reads further. Play selected is one entry of the selection panel's action list, so it is in the More menu and in the right-click menu; a double click opens the player. Later pages of the folder are asked for with the listing's sort, since the server refuses a cursor under another sort.
    - *Limits.* The queue holds 500 files; the folder reader keeps the same 500. When files are left out the panel says so. Playback stops after 10 files in a row that cannot play, and offers Carry on; when nothing can play it says so, and an empty list says it has no video or audio files. A pick (a row, Previous, Next, Carry on) starts the failure run again, and a file that failed may be picked again to retry it.
    - *No-download files.* Playing is not downloading. A no-download file plays in the player on every path (the share page, the viewer, the files page, Play selected and the playlist), as it did on main, because the server gives the player's inline link. Download is shown only where the person may download (`downloadAllowed`), and on the share page the playlist's Download follows the same rule. A download the server refuses shows the downloads-off notice in the viewer, and the same notice under the header in the playlist. Where the server refuses a link (download_restricted) the file is marked restricted and skipped without another request. Interpretation for the owner: whether previews of no-download files are allowed is the owner's open question; this slice does not change main's answer.
    - *Folder pages that cannot be read.* A page that fails is not the end of the folder. The playlist stops with "could not be read past this point, so the list may have more files" and a Try again button, not with "The playlist has ended"; the panel's Load more failure has the same button. Try again reads the same page again. When the playlist has stopped as unreadable, the panel's own failure alert is not shown too: one message, not two.
    - *Shuffle.* Turning shuffle on reads the folder up to the 500 limit first, so the round covers the whole list (no link is asked for by reading a page). A press while the folder is being read does nothing; the round is dealt when the reading ends. The reading stops when the viewer closes, and when a page cannot be read (the round is dealt from the files loaded). The order is the listing's loaded order, then the server's order for later pages.
    - *Races.* A pick made while a page is read wins: the step that was waiting does nothing when the page comes. Two Next presses while a page is read move one file, the second press's; the first is superseded.
    - *Share page.* The playlist plays under the share's credential. A file's refused link (401 or 404) is that file's failure, and the playlist moves on; a link the player cannot renew (401 or 404 after the first) is asked of the share's own check, the same as a first refusal: when the share is gone, the page's expired or gone view shows and the playlist stops. The heading names the file on screen (the playlist's file while one plays).
    - *Kept between files and visits.* The volume and the mute are kept in the browser (`localStorage`, guarded: storage refused leaves the defaults), written only when one of them changes, not on each time update. The speed is kept for the page only.
    - *Phone and touch.* The bar's buttons, the speed list and each slider handle are 44 px on a coarse pointer, and do not shrink in the flex row. The video element has `playsinline`. Where the stage cannot take full screen, the video takes its own (`webkitEnterFullscreen`). **Untested on an iPhone**: there is no device here; the iPhone rules are checked only by unit tests and by the emulated phone in Chrome. The slider handles are drawn 14 px inside a 44 px box, and each slider keeps 22 px margins, so a handle stays inside the bar. The volume block is 220 px on a coarse pointer, so a tablet with touch (768 px) has a volume rail of 128 px; under 600 px the block takes the bar's full width. The e2e step "on a tablet with touch the volume rail is at least 100 px wide" measures the rail (128 px in the local run). Before this change the block was 140 px, which leaves about 48 px of rail after the button and the margins; that figure is arithmetic, not a measurement.
    - *Focus after close.* When the viewer closes, the focus goes to the row of the file on screen at close, else the row that opened the viewer, else the listing itself (`lib/files/focusAfterClose.ts`). A row that has gone is skipped, and the focus is never left on the body. Unit tests cover a gone row and the listing fallback; dropping the listing fallback fails the gone-row test (1 of 5 fails). The page moves the focus on the next animation frame, so the e2e check waits up to 2 s for the focus to leave the body. A diagnostic local run sampled the focus every 100 ms for 2 s after the close: it was on the opening row in every sample, and no dialog was left open, so the dialog does not take the focus back. The failing reads in the runner's gate were taken before that frame. A hidden tab runs no animation frames, so there the focus waits until the tab is shown; it is late, not lost. The focus is not moved from the viewer's after-close callback, because the viewer unmounts on close and has no close animation to hook.
    - *Not built.* Saved playlists (x4), resume (x2), cover art and tags (x3). Restricted playback on a share is unit-tested only.
    - *Review rounds, what was found and what changed.* First round: the bar's icons were white on a white button (1.00:1), so the light-theme video bar had no visible controls; the scrim and the dark control set replace it. The audio panel and the playing row used fallback colours that were white in dark mode; they now use the palette. The Hebrew seek and volume bars ran backwards; the bar's sliders are left to right. The row's three buttons wrapped on a phone; the row is now one line with a More menu. The phone's bar buttons were 43.49 px: a flex row shrank them; they are now 44 px and do not shrink. The viewer had a second scroller over the player; only the playlist scrolls now. Previous and Next below the player repeated the bar; they are gone for a video and an audio, and Download is in the header beside the count. A pick after a stop did not mount the player; it does now. A pending skip could move past the file the person chose; a skip now acts only on the file that failed.
      Second round: the playlist's later pages were asked for without the listing's sort, so the server refused the cursor and the pager stopped for good (fixed: `folderPageReader`). A pick or a Next made during a page read was skipped over (fixed: the superseded step does nothing). A link renewal refused by the server did not reach the share's check (fixed: onFail asks onLost). Shuffle pressed twice ended off, and the reading went on after the viewer closed (fixed). A failed page read ended the playlist with "has ended" and no retry (fixed, above). Media-mode Download dropped the refusal (fixed). A no-download file did not play on a share or in the playlist, which main did (restored, above; the share fixture is back to `no_download: true`). Space closed a fresh viewer, because Close took the focus (fixed, above). The phone's speed list and slider handles were below 44 px (fixed). The volume was written on every time update (fixed). A page appended to a shuffled queue changed the round (fixed). The share heading stayed on the first file (fixed). The selection's add panel offered only the selection (fixed: the folder). Some e2e checks were `check(true)` (replaced with the state read from the page).
    - *Evidence.* Unit tests: 1342 in 158 files (`npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1`, all pass, in the capped scope, on the final tree). Mutation proofs, each applied to the source, run against the named test, and reverted (the tree was compared after each): the pick guard (both guards removed: 2 named tests fail, the pick plays the next file, and the double Next plays the wrong file); a renewal refused without onLost (2 named tests fail); the shuffle second-press guard (1 fails); the shuffle loop without the close check (1 fails: the read after close); a failed page read reported as the end, in the playlist (3 fail) and in the pager (1 fails); a no-download file skipped by the queue (4 fail); a Space press on a button the keyboard does not hold (1 fails); the media-mode Download without the notice (2 fail); Close with autoFocus (1 fails); the share's Download on a no-download file (1 fails); the share heading on the first file (1 fails); the video without `playsinline` (1 fails); no iPhone fallback (1 fails); the volume written on every read (1 fails); the appendPage round mutated (1 fails); the selection add panel from the selection (1 fails); the folder reader without the sort (1 fails). Round 6: the repeat rule removed from the keys (3 fail, on the committed MediaControls); the press-Play note on the committed MediaControls (the note test fails; the AbortError test passes on both, as it asserts an absence); the PublicBrowse no-download notice on the committed code (the explicit and the inherited tests fail); the share heading on the committed code (fails: `a.webm` for `b.webm`); the listing fallback of the focus helper dropped (1 fails); the one-message guard dropped (1 fails: two messages). The first-round mutations are listed in the round's notes. Fail-first: the round tests were written before the fixes for the playlist and share cases.
    - *End-to-end.* The last full run was on the runner (gate x1e; the gate's result is in the report, not repeated here). Local full runs of this round's tree did not come out clean, and none was repeated after the last change: run 1 failed the new press-Play step (the step read the Play button's place while the viewer was still zooming; fixed with the same settle wait playItemUnscrolled uses); run 2 failed `sharePublic.mjs` at the Request-files switch (the step clicked it before it rendered; fixed with a wait, the product is unchanged); run 3 passed the player steps, the tablet step (128 px) and the shots, and failed two w1 steps (`w1.mjs` line 280 checked the listing right after Backspace, while a cached row could still show; the check now waits up to 10 s for the row to leave, and a row that never leaves still fails). The w1 change was not rerun locally, and the machine was loaded. Gate x1e on the runner (1561 s, label x1e, its log `runner-x1e.log`): attempt 1 passed; attempts 2 and 3 failed at the focus-after-close check (BODY); attempt 4 passed; attempt 5 was stopped. The wrapper printed exit 0, but the attempts are the truth: the check was intermittent. The check now waits (above); gate x1f runs the final tree.
    - *Earlier end-to-end (round 4, before the layout and review changes).* `make e2e` (`web/e2e/run.mjs`, which runs `media.mjs` and so `player.mjs`), run once in full on that tree: `e2e passed`, exit 0. Its player steps passed, among them: the playlist of 52 opened from its first page reads its second page (`51 / 52`); Space on a new viewer plays or pauses and keeps the viewer open; Space after a click on the bar still plays or pauses; a button the keyboard holds toggles with its Space; the focus is on the page after the viewer closes (on the opening row); M mutes and unmutes; antd's style tags carry the page's nonce (0 of 40 without); the speed list is 44 px tall and each slider handle 44 by 44 px on a phone. After that run the slider margins were changed (below): the phone step and the screenshot step were rerun and both pass. The player's steps are `check` calls, which the run does not total, so no player total is given.
    - *The 52-track step, the proof.* The step failed in the first full run with the viewer stopped at track 50, and it was the test, not the product. The step opened the viewer with a script's double click, which is not a user gesture; the browser refused `play()` (`NotAllowedError`), so track 50 stopped at 7.82 s of 8.02 s and `ended` never fired. The server was not at fault: the listing's first page answered 200 with 50 items, and a replay of the next cursor with the listing's sort answered 200 with `track-51.ogg`. On the old reader (without the sort) the page's second-page request got 400, `invalid_request`, "cursor is not valid for this sort; start the listing again", and the playlist then showed the Try again notice (not "has ended"). The step now gives the page a real click on the viewer's name, and passes with `51 / 52`.
    - *Test that was wrong, and the proof.* The drag check read the grip's position while the viewer was still zooming in, so its coordinates were stale by about 20 px. The diagnostic run showed the queue's width changing between reads (289 px, then 325 px) and the modal still carrying the appear-animation class after the press. The check now waits for the animation to end; the drag then moves the row to the top in the same run.
    - *Screenshots.* 24 images in the owner's review folder (video, audio and a bright white video, each in light and dark, English and Hebrew, desktop and phone), retaken from the full run and read by the author. The read found one defect, now fixed: at phone width the 44 px seek and volume handles reached over the time beside the seek bar (the handle covered `0:01`) and past the bar's edge. Each slider now keeps 22 px either side, and the phone shots, retaken after the fix, read clean. The volume track is dim over a dark scrim in the video shots, though its handle reads. At phone width the audio bar wraps to three rows (volume on its own row) because its buttons are 44 px; accepted. Desktop shots show no change. Round 6: the 24 images were written by local run 3 (11:59 to 12:00) and the phone ones read again there: `video-phone-light-en` (the bar's seek and volume handles inside the bar, speed and full screen on one row, the playlist readable) and `audio-phone-dark-he` (the Hebrew bar reads left to right, the volume rail visible). No tablet screenshot is taken; the tablet has the rail measurement only.
    - *Not checked.* The reviewer did not reach the listing's play mark, the focus after close, the nonce, IME or key repeat for the player keys. The nonce passed in the e2e run; the focus after close failed in it and was fixed after the run (not rerun). The listing's play mark and IME are not checked. Key repeat is checked in unit tests only. Firefox's keyup is not checked (Chrome only). The iPhone is not checked (no device).
    - *Interpretations for the owner.* The failure-run stop (10) is stricter than "every item". The queue cap (500) is the same for the pager and the queue. Autoplay starts every file the playlist starts, the first file the person opened included. This line said otherwise until decision 52, which corrected it: the first file did not start on open. No-download files play (main's behaviour, kept); the owner may still decide that previews of no-download files are not allowed, which is a server question, not this slice's.

46. **Search over file content, slice q3** (built on the owner's proposal for content search: text extracted from plain text and from office documents through Collabora's converter, and a search that finds the words in it; the owner approved it with words only in the text, substring matching for names, and OCR as a later slice). Migration 0036.
    - **Mechanism.** `search_texts` holds one row per file blob that content search reads. Its ID is the rowid of `search_text_fts`, a contentful FTS5 table of the text in search form (`names.SearchForm`: marks removed, case folded), with `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2` and words only. Names keep the trigram table of decision 40; the text does not. A row is queued by the write that gives a file its blob (`InsertNodeNoIndex`, and `UpdateNodeHeld` when a new version arrives), so a copy shares its blob's row. A blob with no node and no version has no row. `DeleteOrphan` removes the full-text row in the same write, before the blob, because a cascade does not reach the full-text table (`TestOrphanDeleteRemovesTheFullTextRowInTheSameWrite`).
    - **Where the text is kept, and who may read it.** The extracted text is stored in `search_text_fts` and in its FTS shadow tables. It is user data, like the file: it is in every backup, and it is deleted with its blob, its node or its account. Account deletion removes its rows (`TestDeletingAnAccountRemovesItsContentText`). Deleting the text overwrites the freed pages of the database file, and the full-text tables are set to secure-delete; what that does not reach is listed under review S2 below.
    - **Sizes.** `search.fulltext_max_bytes` (50 MiB, the largest source read) and `search.text_max_bytes` (1 MiB, the most text kept per file, cut at a rune boundary) are both settable. Source bytes above the first limit are refused as too large, and that refusal is a permanent skip. The text is validated over the whole source, not the first megabyte, so a file that is text for its first MiB and binary after it is not text (`TestReadTextValidatesTheWholeSource`). A NUL byte or invalid UTF-8 refuses the file. A byte order mark at the start is dropped. Measured: one 1 MiB cut text adds 1,167,360 bytes to the database (one run, one machine).
    - **Families.** The first bytes decide the family (`SniffFamily`), never the name: a ZIP-based office file and a plain ZIP are told apart by their contents, so a `.docx` that is a ZIP of two text files is not a document (`TestSniffFamilyDecidesFromBytesNotName`). Only plain text is read in this process. Documents go to the converter, and only when `office.enabled` and `search.office_text` are both on (`search.office_text` defaults to off, review S4). A document queued while `search.office_text` is off is skipped with the reason "office text search is off" (`TextErrOfficeTextOff`) and no request is made. A document queued while the converter is off is skipped with the reason "the converter is off" (`TextErrConverterOff`). When `office.enabled` is turned on, the server releases those rows to pending (`ReleaseTextSkipped`, at start), so they are converted without a re-upload.
    - **Converter.** A document is converted to `txt` (`office.Formats["txt"]`, added here: `text/plain`, not an export or a preview format). The worker's classes follow decision 37, as revised by review S4: an outage (the converter unreachable, a dial error) is not an attempt; the worker pauses, the wait doubling from one minute to five, and probes the converter once per pause; a failure in flight is counted, is retried at one and ten minutes, and after the third try waits for a new converter key; a time-out is counted the same way and, after the third, is sticky under the converter key, as a refusal is (review round q3c, item 3; it was sticky for a day before); a refusal or a bad output is sticky until the converter key changes (it was sticky for a day before the review), with a fixed message. The preview converter pool and the bulk converter slot are separate, so bulk work does not delay a preview. The queue wait for the bulk slot is neither counted as time against the limit nor as an attempt. The converter's true file type is sent, not a guessed one (`TestDocumentKeepsItsTrueType`). Messages are fixed strings, never the converter's text. Tests: `TestConverterOutageIsRetriedAndNotCounted`, `TestConverterTimeoutCountsThreeTriesThenWaitsADay`, `TestConverterRefusalIsStickyWithAFixedReason`, `TestConverterOutputOverTheLimitIsCutAndMarked`.
    - **Live run, `txt` against Collabora (one disposable container, removed after the run; the LAN test site was not touched).** The image is `collabora/code` at digest `sha256:c7415b963e32eb0986a562583f154d36d3d7a461e1ddfb660a95e87094328acb`, productVersion 26.04.5.2. Results:
      - `txt` gives text for `.docx`, `.odt` and `.rtf`. Hebrew with niqqud and Arabic came through exact. The output starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark, which `ReadText` drops. CRLF input comes out as LF.
      - `.xlsx`, `.ods`, `.pptx`, `.odp` and `.pdf` are refused by the converter with `savefailed` (HTTP 500). Spreadsheets and presentations are therefore not searchable through `txt`. They open in the converter (`xlsx` to `csv`, `pptx` to `pdf`, `pdf` to `png` all return 200), so a later format could search them; this slice does not add one. A PDF is not searchable at all in this slice.
      - A ZIP of text files is refused (`faileddocloading`), as is a ZIP sent as `pdf`.
      - A file of random bytes named `.docx` or `.bin` is not refused: the converter returns 200 with a few kilobytes of valid UTF-8, which the worker stores as text. Its words are noise, and a search can match them. This is a known gap: the converter accepts the input, and the worker has no check beyond UTF-8 that could tell this from text.
      - A 2,000-paragraph `.docx` (366,896 bytes of text) converted in about 1.6 s.
      - To connect, the probe needed the container's process namespace shared with the host (`--pid=host`), because the rootless container could not mount `/proc`. This weakens the isolation of that disposable container. It was used for the run only, and it is not part of any committed setting.
      - The probe pinned the converter's certificate, which carries a name but no alternative name. Go refused it under normal verification, so the probe compared the leaf byte for byte with the PEM it generated. The probe is not committed. The gated test `internal/search/live_test.go` runs only when `SELFCLOUD_LIVE_COLLABORA` (and `SELFCLOUD_LIVE_COLLABORA_CA`) is set; the measurement tests run only when `SELFCLOUD_MEASURE_CONTENT` is `1`.
    - **Content hits.** A content search needs `q` and finds files only (`kind` is `file`). Each hit carries `snippet`: a window of up to 12 tokens (FTS5's count) around the first matched words, in search form, as plain text with the byte ranges of the matched words (`[start, end)`). Markup in a file is text, never markup. A snippet is read only for a hit the caller may read, after the access check. A file the no-download rule binds for the caller (a viewer, or a commenter, rank at most commenter) gets no content hit at all: a hit it cannot read would show what the file says (`TestContentPrivacyFollowsTheReachAndTheNoDownloadRule`, `TestNoDownloadHitLooksLikeNoMatch`, so a viewer's search answers the same as for a word that is not there). A share-link visitor is refused by the route, as before.
    - **Privacy.** A word found in text needs the same reach as the file's name: the candidate read joins the node, and the reach check runs per hit. Staged copies never match (`TestStagedContentRowsNeverMatch`, which runs the candidate read alone; the API's reach check would also drop a staged copy, so the staged filter is the guard that the candidate test isolates). Labels, restricted labels and the folder filters apply to content hits as to names. Cursors are sealed as for names, and a content cursor holds the text row and the node position, 16 bytes, so two nodes sharing one blob page correctly (`TestContentPagingWithSharedBlobs`).
    - **Ordering and plan.** A content search has no `ORDER BY`. A sort over a full-text match sorts the whole match set on each page, which costs as much as the matches. The candidate order is the plan's: the full-text table outermost, then rows in rowid order. `TestContentQueryPlanSortsNoMatchSet` pins the plan, so a change of plan fails.
    - **Lifecycle.** Versions, restore, rename, move, trash, delete, copy (small and bulk) and account deletion are covered by the store writes that queue or drop rows (`TestFinishTextKeepsNothingForAnUnusedBlob`, `TestNewBlobOnAnUpdateQueuesItsRow`, `TestFileNodeQueuesItsContentRowOnce`). A move changes no row. A trashed file keeps its text, as it keeps its blob, until the file is purged; search does not show trashed nodes, so it does not match in the meantime.
    - **Load.** The worker is one bounded background job (`search.workers` is not built: the worker is one per process). Claims are round robin across accounts, FIFO within an account (`TestClaimIsRoundRobinAcrossAccounts`). Writes are short. Backfill on upgrade is bounded in batches of 1,000 blobs, resumable from a cursor (`search_text_backfill`), and yields between batches (`TestBackfillIsBoundedAndResumes`). Not verified at scale: the backfill and claim were run on up to 20,000 blobs, under the 200,000-row limit for the local machine; a run at the production scale of 100,000 files was not done (`SELFCLOUD_SCALE` was not run).
    - **Repair.** `SearchCheck` counts the content rows that are missing (`TextMissing`) and whether the full-text table disagrees with its rows (`TextFTSMismatch`). The sweep repairs a missing count and logs a mismatch, and does not repair a mismatch (decision 40). `admin search-rebuild` clears the text in the same write as the name index, and queues the backfill again. `SearchRepair` repairs both.
    - **Security review of ade087c (S1 to S5), fixed on this slice.** The review found no direct disclosure of content, and five weaknesses, each fixed with a test that failed first or a mutation proof.
      - **S1, a confirmation oracle (medium).** An unreadable match used to count against the scan budget and could return a page with no items and a cursor, so a viewer could tell that a hidden file held the word. The budget is removed. The search stops on emitted items only, and the cursor appears only when the limit is reached. Trashed rows are excluded in the candidate SQL (`n.trashed_at IS NULL`, in the content and name candidate queries). Failing first (`TestSearchAnswerDoesNotRevealAnUnreadableFile`, run with a budget of 50 before the change): "the answer tells an unreadable match apart: with the word: {"items":[],"next_cursor":...} without: {"items":[]}". The two-worlds test runs the same query with and without the hidden match and requires byte-identical answers. `TestSearchPassesUnreadableMatches` pins the first page: one item, no cursor. The reach check is still per batch in Go, not in the candidate SQL. Not done in this slice (see "Not done" below).
      - **S1, timing residue (measured, not closed).** `TestMeasureUnreadableMatchCost` (gated by `SELFCLOUD_MEASURE_CONTENT=1`): 5,000 unreadable matches for a word the caller cannot read, answer `[]`, 503 ms; the control with no match anywhere, 1.3 ms. The cost is linear in the matches (about 0.1 ms each, by this one run). Extrapolated, not measured: near 20,000 matches the 2 s deadline (`search.timeout`) answers `unavailable`, which a caller can tell from `[]`. This is a visible difference that the answer bytes do not show, and it stays open.
      - **S2, deleted text on disk (medium).** `PRAGMA secure_delete` is on in the common pragmas, and FTS5's `secure-delete` option is set on `search_words`, `search_trigram` and `search_text_fts` at store open (`secureDeleteFTS`). Failing first: `TestDeletedTextLeavesNoBytesInTheDatabaseFile` (a marker absent from the database file after `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`) and `TestVacuumIntoCopyHoldsNoDeletedText` (a `VACUUM INTO` copy holds no deleted text); both passed after the fix. Write cost (`TestMeasureSecureDeleteCost`, 2,000 files of 1 KiB, each deleted in its own write): both mechanisms on (shipped) 18.577 ms per delete; pragma on, FTS5 off 0.821 ms; pragma off, FTS5 on 19.533 ms; both off 0.806 ms. Each write of a file costs about 0.8 ms. So the FTS5 option is the cost, about 18.7 ms per deleted file, and a purge of N files costs about 18.6 N ms in writes. This is an owner choice (below).
      - **What secure delete does not reach (residue, stated plainly; revised in round q3c, below, which adds the write-ahead log: deleted words stay in the `-wal` file until the hourly truncating checkpoint).** The blob file on disk is removed by unlinking it, and the blocks it used are not overwritten by this store. The page cache may hold the text until it is reused. On an SSD, wear levelling may keep old flash pages. A backup taken before the deletion keeps the text, as it keeps the file. The database's freed pages are overwritten by the pragma; the full-text shadow tables are overwritten by the FTS5 option.
      - **S3, index growth (medium).** No extraction runs for a blob that only an old version holds (`TestFinishTextDiscardsAVersionOnlyBlob`). A blob that stops being current loses its text when no node holds it (`TestReplacedBlobLosesItsTextWhenNoNodeHoldsIt`). The sweep's catch-all (`DropUnusedText`) drops text no node holds (`TestDropUnusedTextIsTheSweepsCatchAll`). Restoring a file queues its text again through the same queue. Caps: `search.max_text_per_account` (default 64 MiB) and `search.max_text_total` (default 1 GiB), counted in `search_text_usage` per account and in total; a file that does not fit is skipped with "the account's text limit is full" or "the installation's text limit is full" and waits for room (`TestPerAccountCapStopsOnlyTheFullAccount`, `TestInstallationCapStopsEveryAccount`, `TestCappedRowsWaitForRoom`). Measured growth (`TestMeasureTextGrowth`, four files of 1 MiB of random words, about 4 MiB of text): the database grew 3.03 bytes on disk per byte of text. So the defaults are justified as follows: 64 MiB of text is about 194 MiB on disk, and 1 GiB is about 3.1 GB on disk, against 11 GB free on the owner's main server when the review was made (a full installation cap would use about 28% of that). **No quota charge:** text is not charged to the account's storage quota. The cap is separate and is the only bound on text. Usage shows the text bytes, the cap and the skipped count.
      - **S4, the bulk converter (medium).** `search.office_text` defaults to off, and README says so (`TestOfficeTextOffMakesNoRequest`). A trashed document is not sent until it is restored (`TestTrashedDocumentIsNotSentUntilRestored`). A version-only blob is not sent. A refusal is sticky until the converter key changes, not until the next day (`TestConverterDailyRefusalIsNotResent`). The true type is sent (`TestDocumentKeepsItsTrueType`). An unreachable converter is not counted, and it pauses the worker (`TestUnreachableConverterIsNotAnAttempt`, `TestOutageIsOneProbePerPause`). A failure in flight is counted, and after three tries waits for a new key (`TestConverterFailureInFlightIsCountedThenSticky`). Bulk work has its own slot, so previews are not delayed (`TestBulkUsesItsOwnSlot`), and the time in the bulk queue is not counted as time or as an attempt (`TestBulkQueueTimeIsNotCounted`).
      - **S5, prefix cost across tenants (low).** `TestMeasurePrefixAcrossTenants` (gated): 150,000 rows of 20 words for one tenant, 10 rows for another, one full-text table. The prefix `ab` on the small tenant took 19.1 ms (the first query of the run; the cause of the difference from the second was not traced); `ab` on the large tenant 2.5 ms; `abc` on the small tenant 0.9 ms. There is no minimum prefix length. The fix is a per-account rate limit on top of the per-caller one: `search.account` allows ten times the per-caller rate for an account (`TestSearchAccountLimitHoldsAcrossCallers`, 11 users in one account at a rate of 1: ten requests pass, the eleventh gets 429).
      - **Tests the review asked for, and where they are.** A restricted label with content hits (`TestContentRestrictedLabelMatchesOnlyAManager`). A no-download token capped at viewer (`TestContentNoDownloadHoldsForATokenCappedAtViewer`). A content cursor replayed under another identity or another query (`TestContentCursorIsRefusedUnderAnotherIdentityOrQuery`). A personal folder (`TestContentSearchOfAPersonalFolderFollowsItsOwner`). A disabled or deleted user (`TestContentSearchEndsWithADisabledOrDeletedUser`). An impersonating admin (`TestContentSearchForAnImpersonatingAdminIsTheUsersOwn`). The scan-budget property (`TestSearchAnswerDoesNotRevealAnUnreadableFile`, above). Residue (`TestDeletedTextLeavesNoBytesInTheDatabaseFile`). No daily PDF resend (`TestConverterDailyRefusalIsNotResent`). Slot starvation (`TestBulkUsesItsOwnSlot`). The usage count of skipped text (`TestUsageShowsTheSkippedTextCount`).
    - **Mutation proofs.** One change at a time, each restored and the tree checked after the run. Killed, with the first failing test: the orphan delete without the full-text drop; account deletion without its rows; claim without the account cursor (round robin); the no-download rule not applied to content hits; the commenter not restricted; a result kept for an unused blob; an update not queuing the new blob; an insert not queuing the content row; NUL not refused; invalid UTF-8 not refused; the whole source not validated past the cut; a converter outage counted as an attempt; a time-out not counted; a refusal retried at once; a full converter output not marked truncated; snippet ranges dropped; the cursor without the node position; the backfill cursor not kept; text kept unfolded (Hebrew niqqud and case); office documents told apart from ZIPs by name; the full text over the source limit not refused; a content row inserted for a copy; a retry released before its wait; a third time-out not sticky; truncated text cut in the middle of a character. Killed by the new test `TestStagedContentRowsNeverMatch`: the staged filter removed from the content query (it survived the API test, because the API reach check also drops the copy; the candidate test isolates the SQL guard). Killed after a fix to the mutant: the byte order mark kept (the mutant first failed to compile, which proves nothing; rerun with `&& false` in the condition, `TestReadTextDropsControlsAndTheByteOrderMark` fails).
    - **Not built.** The converter's build-key retry when the converter changes (a changed converter is not re-read until a blob gets a new row). Spreadsheets, presentations and PDF text (refused live, above). OCR. A web interface for content hits (q4). The `search.workers` setting. Tests that run `SELFCLOUD_SCALE` above 100,000 files. Not verified: whether a PDF can ever yield text through `txt` (the converter refused it in the run).
    - **Mutation proofs for the review (S1 to S5), one change each.** Each mutant is applied, the named test run, and the tree restored. Killed by the first failing test named:
