53. **My files is the landing page, and there is no Home page** (2026-11-01, the owner's decision: "users do not need a home. it should go directly to files."). Web interface only; the server is unchanged. Built as follows, and each point is a choice the owner may want to confirm.
    - *The root.* `/` for a person who is not an installation admin is replaced by `/files`, with a replace, so Back leaves the root. An admin's root stays `/admin/tenants`. A sign-in goes to `homeFor(user)` (`web/src/lib/routes.ts`): `/files` for everyone but an admin, in one step, with no second navigation (`lib/next.ts`, `lib/signin.ts`). Deep links are unchanged.
    - *Removed.* The Home page (`pages/HomePage.tsx`, its test and `lib/home.ts`), the Home entry in the sidebar, and the catalogue keys only Home used (`nav.home`, `home.recent`, `home.starred`, `home.shared`, `home.sharedOn`, `home.seeAll`, `home.waiting` and its plural forms) in all seven languages. The logo opens My files. The Recent, Starred and Shared with me pages keep their own lists.
    - *The storage notice* moved to My files. It shows in the person's own folder and its subfolders only, below the toolbar, so the toolbar does not move. It shows from 80% of the person's own limit, with its link to Storage and the usage meter (`components/storage/StorageNotice.tsx`; `storageNoticePercent` is in `lib/storage/logic.ts`). Its catalogue keys keep their names, `home.storageNotice` and `home.storageLink`.
    - *The requests count.* A person with requests waiting sees the entry and its count in the sidebar, as before. Home read the count on each visit, so the sidebar now reads it again when the person comes to the files area (`components/Shell.tsx`), and a request that came in while signed in still shows.
    - *No personal folder.* `/files` shows the not-found page when the person has no personal folder (`loadPlace`, `pages/FilesPage.tsx`). The server makes a personal folder with each user, and at start-up gives one to each existing user who has none (`internal/store/personal.go`), so a member or an owner does not reach it.
    - *Not changed.* The end of a forced password change still goes to `/`, which the gate replaces with `/files`.
    - *Proofs.* The tests were broken on purpose one at a time, and each failed: the root's target (`routes.ts`), the replace (`App.tsx`), the Home entry (`Shell.tsx`), the 80% threshold (`logic.ts`), the own-folder gate (`FilesPage.tsx`), the redirect of a missing folder (`FilesPage.tsx`), and the count's re-read on arrival (`Shell.tsx`).
54. **Search web interface, slice q4** (2026-11-01, built to the owner-approved proposal for slice q (`design-q-proposal.md`), section 4 and questions 11 and 12, with every recommendation). The web interface only; the server is unchanged. Each point is a choice the owner may want to confirm.
    - *Where it sits.* The top bar has one box (on a phone, one button that opens the page). The box is `ShellSearch`, a native input and one button, the only search code in the shell. The page is the lazy route `/search`, a chunk of 5.3 KB gzip. Its own strings are a separate catalogue (`web/src/i18n/search/`), loaded when the page opens, so the seven main catalogues do not grow. The first load measured 322.5 KB before the slice and 323.6 KB after, of the 330 KB budget (`npm run build`, the same tree, with the slice's Shell change).
    - *The address is the state.* The words, `in=content`, type, extension, modified, size and label values are in the address, so a search can be reloaded and walked with Back and Forward. A change replaces the entry. The words are written after 300 ms of no typing, or at once on Enter. The box keeps the letters typed while a write is pending, so an echo of the write does not clear them (`useDraft`).
    - *The words are checked before a request.* At most 200 bytes of UTF-8 (a Hebrew letter is two bytes), 8 words, 64 bytes a word, and two letters or digits a word; a text search needs a word; a label value is checked by its field's type. A query that fails a check is not sent, and the page says why in a sentence.
    - *Requests.* Each change of the address sends one request. An answer or a failure for an older address is dropped, so a slow answer cannot replace a newer one (`SearchPage.test.tsx`, "only the answer to the latest address"). Load more uses the clock of the first page, because the server's cursor covers the modified-after time (`Load more asks with the same window`).
    - *Failures.* A failed first answer shows its error, and no "nothing matches" text. A failed Load more keeps the list and shows the error above it, with a Try again button. A new search clears the previous results: they belong to another search, so they are not a list being refetched. The server's codes map to sentences: rate limited, invalid, took too long, search off, and the file errors for the rest. The rate-limit sentence names no minutes, and the page does not read `Retry-After`.
    - *No counts.* The page never says how many matches there are. A page with a cursor says "More results may follow." A page with no hits and a cursor says that nothing on this part matched.
    - *Snippets.* Shown as text. The server's ranges are UTF-8 byte offsets, so the text is cut by bytes and each piece is decoded on its own (`snippetParts`). Matches are `mark` elements. The text is the server's search form (lower case, marks removed), and the page says so under the results: the server keeps no original case.
    - *Chips.* Type (files, folders, shortcuts), extension (a fixed list of twelve, up to eight), modified (7, 30 or 365 days), size (under 1 MB, 1 to 100 MB, over 100 MB) and label values (text prefix, number and date ranges, choices by their names). Each chip's close button removes its filter alone; "Clear filters" removes all. A text search offers no type chip, since it finds files only. A label chip names its field, never its ID. The user label type is not offered in v1.
    - *Not built, and open for the owner.* (a) A scope chip: the API takes `scope`, but the page has no folder picker, and the listing (`FilesPage.tsx`, shared with other slices) was not changed. (b) User-valued label filters. (c) The "/" shortcut (feature parity, section 7, row k). (d) The text search is a second mode, not one box for both: the API takes one `in` at a time, so the box searches names, or text, and a button switches. (e) Restricted labels match only for managers, so the page says so under the label row, and does not show a count of what it hides. (f) Reading `Retry-After`: the rate-limit sentence names no minutes, and the page does not read the header.
    - *Languages.* English, Spanish, French, Portuguese and Russian are written for the slice. Hebrew and Arabic are machine drafts, and a speaker should read them before release.
    - *Tests.* Unit: `web/src/lib/search/*.test.ts` (the address, the checks, the snippets, the seven catalogues), `web/src/pages/SearchPage.test.tsx` (the requests, the failures, the answers, the chips, the snippets), `web/src/components/search/ShellSearch.test.tsx` (the box). Browser: `web/e2e/q4.mjs`, run with `SELFCLOUD_E2E_ONLY=q4`: real key presses; one request for a burst of letters; a name search; a text search with its mark; a chip that removes itself; an empty answer; a Hebrew search in a right-to-left page; the phone layout with no sideways scroll; a failed connection; and the server's limit, past sixty searches a minute. `SELFCLOUD_Q4_SHOTS` saves eight pictures (desktop and phone, English and Hebrew, light and dark) and one of a text search.
    - *Mutations, each run and reverted.* Removing the latest-address guard of the first answer fails "only the answer to the latest address is shown". Reading the clock for Load more fresh fails "Load more asks with the same window". A debounce of 0 fails four tests, including the one request for a burst. Cutting snippets by characters instead of bytes fails both Hebrew snippet tests.
    - *Found while the browser checks were written.* The results list's label is translated, so the test finds it by a test id. The top bar's box is re-mounted when the width changes, so the check waits for it and confirms the focus before it types. The server's search limit refills one token a second, so the check sends its burst while the page's own search is still waiting out its pause.
    - *Review fixes (2026-11-01), each with its test or its mutation.* (1) On a phone the filter fields are 44 px high: a `(pointer: coarse)` rule in `index.css` sizes `.search-filter` the way the repo's media-speed rule sizes its selects. The browser check "at phone width every search filter field is at least 44 px high" reads the heights; the rule under `pointer: fine` gives 32 px and fails it. (2) Contrast: a result name uses the theme's link colour, and "Clear filters" is an antd link button. The browser checks measure each against the colour behind it, in light and dark, and require 4.5 to 1 (measured: name 5.47 light, 4.55 dark; Clear filters 4.79 light, 5.15 dark). With the link on the tertiary text token the check reads 3.71 to 1 and fails. (3) The page heading is the main catalogue's `shell.search.open`, so no raw key shows before the search catalogue loads. A failed catalogue shows its error with a Try again button (`files.retry`). `SearchPage.loading.test.tsx` and `SearchPage.retry.test.tsx`; the heading on `search.title` fails the loading test. (4) A label chip names its field. While the field list loads, the chip is the neutral word "Label" and the request waits. A label whose field is gone, or whose choice is not live, is dropped from the address and from the request, and a failed field list drops every label (`resolveLabels`, four tests in `query.test.ts`, and the page tests "neutral label chip while fields pending", "unknown field not sent", "crafted choice not sent", "fields failed, labels not sent"). No ID is shown. (5) A write still pending from the box's pause is cancelled when the place changes, so a nav link clicked during the pause stays where it went (`useDraft`, `ShellSearch.test.tsx`; removing the scope effect fails it). (6) On a phone the top bar's button opens the page with its box focused on arrival (`focusSearch` in the link state; "focus on arrival" test; removing it fails the test). (7) An unavailable shortcut in a result is a link to its own address, `/n/<shortcut id>`, and not dead text (`HitRow.test.tsx`). The listing does not link an unavailable shortcut: it opens the access dialog on the shortcut. `/n/<shortcut id>` opens the shortcut's folder with the shortcut selected, from where the person can open it or ask for access, so the link is the closest match. The target's ID is never shown. (8) A text search has no type: `?in=content&kind=dir` drops the type from the address and from the request (`stateFromParams`, `a text search has no kind`). (9) Markup: a file whose name and text are `<img src=x onerror=...>` shows as literal text. The browser check finds no img element in the results, `window.__pwned` stays undefined, and the tag is on the page as text. (10) The limit is per principal: the server counts a search per user (kind and ID) at 60 a minute and per account at 600 a minute, and does not read `Retry-After` (not built). The check's flood runs as the member, so it empties that member's allowance for about a minute. The only other search requests in the suite are in `adminAccess.mjs`, which runs its own server in a temp directory, so no later step of `run.mjs` is affected. The flood's 150 requests were refused 150 times in the last run, and the page's own search then shows the sentence.
    - *Server fix, found by the gate (run q4a, five runs).* A member's name search past many names the member cannot reach answered 503 `unavailable` ("the search took too long") after the 2 s deadline, so the page showed the error and no results. Cause, in `internal/search/search.go` `candidateSQL`: the name candidate query made `search_names` the outer loop, so SQLite ran the trigram or word MATCH once per name row of the account, and every batch re-ran it. `ORDER BY sn.id` then sorted every match after the batch's position before the first row came back, so a batch cost all the matches that follow it. The content query had the same shape and was fixed in decision 46; the name query was not. Fix: the full-text table is the outer loop (`CROSS JOIN`, as the content query does), the position is its rowid (`sn.id` is that rowid), and the term path has no `ORDER BY`, because the match yields rows in rowid order. Measured on this host, unreadable names of one word: 5,000 names, the handler 43.0 s before and 0.68 s after. The candidate walk (51 batches) over 5,000 names: 3.1 s with the new loop order and the sort still there, 0.41 s with the sort removed. Over 2,000 names the walk was 16.9 s before the fix. The gated measurement is `TestMeasureNameSearchUnreadable` (`SELFCLOUD_MEASURE_NAMES=1`). Tests, each failing first: `TestNameSearchPastUnreadableMatchesWithinTheDeadline` (1,500 unreadable names, a 2 s deadline) answered `503 unavailable` after 2.005 s with the old query and 200 with the fix; `TestNameQueryPlanMatchIsTheOuterLoop` fails on the old plan (`SEARCH sn USING INDEX search_names_account`) and passes on the fix (`SCAN search_trigram VIRTUAL TABLE INDEX 0:M2>`). Both were reverted to the old query for the red run and restored. The gate's own database was not inspected; the figures are from seeded volumes.
    - *What is left.* The cost is still per unreadable match: each one is read and checked in Go, and the reach check is not in SQL (decision 46, "Not done"). The scan budget stays removed, because a page cut short by a budget would show that a hidden file matches (review S1). So a member whose search matches very many files they cannot reach can still reach the deadline, and then gets the 503 as before. A person can hit this on a real drive: a common word matches files in folders they cannot see, and each upload adds matches.
    - *Recovery.* The page does not retry by itself. A failed first answer shows the error with a Try again button (`search.err.retry`), which sends the same search again; typing sends a new search as well.
    - *Not built, as the review asked, and left out on purpose.* The scope chip, a user-valued label filter, the "/" shortcut and reading `Retry-After` for the rate-limit sentence. Each is named above in the not-built list.
    - *Not covered.* The server's two-second search deadline is not reached from the page (the "took too long" sentence is tested with a stubbed answer). No screen-reader pass was made. Scope is not in the page. A full run (`make e2e`) runs the q4 checks after w2, as w2 is run, so they upload four files into Team A (three, and the markup file) and use the member's search allowance for about a minute.
55. **Web interface for comments, activity and who-viewed, slice r7a** (2026-11-01, built to the owner-approved proposal for slice r (`design-r-proposal.md`), section 1, section 8.2, section 9.2 and question 21, with every recommendation). The web interface only, with one server change: a reason on the who-viewed refusal (below). Not built, as slice r7b: the bell with the unread count, the notifications page, and the notification email settings. Each point below is a choice the owner may want to confirm.
    - *Where it sits.* The tabs (Comments, Activity, and Who viewed for a manager) are at the foot of the file details drawer, below the existing actions, in `web/src/components/comments/CommentsTabs.tsx`. A shortcut has no tabs (decision 39). The tabs are a lazy chunk with their own texts, so the first load stays under its budget: 324.6 KB gzip of the 330 KB budget after the build (it was about 323 KB before), and each language chunk is under its 25 KB budget.
    - *The texts are a separate catalogue.* The main catalogues are close to the language budget (Russian is 22.2 KB gzip before this slice), so the r7a texts are in `web/src/i18n/comments/` (one file per language, namespace `comments`), loaded with the panels. The `search/` catalogue the brief named is not on main (q4 is not merged), so no pattern was copied from it. `catalogue.test.ts` checks that the seven catalogues have the same keys, that every literal key the panels use has a text, and that no key is left unused. The Hebrew and Arabic texts are machine drafts, to be read by a speaker. The other five are written by hand.
    - *Comments.* A commenter and up may write, reply and resolve; the author edits and may delete, and a manager deletes any comment (decision 39). The composer and the reply box show the rule that refuses a body (2,000 characters, 50 lines, 10 people) before the server is asked. A send the server refuses keeps the typed text. A body is shown as text in a `bdi` element with white space kept: no HTML is made from it and links are not made clickable. A thread shows its first 50 replies, and "show more replies" reads the rest with `?parent=`, oldest first, paging by cursor.
    - *The mention picker.* It reuses the combobox reducer and the debounce of the sharing dialog (`lib/sharing/combobox.ts`), so an answer to an old query is dropped and a search waits for the typing to stop. It asks `GET /nodes/{nod}/people`, never the directory, and it shows names only. The reference the answer gives is sent, never an ID. A name is added to the text as `@name`, and a person whose name the author removed from the text is not sent. A rate limit is said in words.
    - *Refusals are read by their reason.* `comments_off` hides the Comments tab (the server's answer is the signal, not an error), and a note says why. `role` and `rate_limited` have their own texts. `limit`, `author` and `reply_to_reply` have their own texts (the review fixes below). Everything else is the common text for the code, and the server's English is never shown.
    - *Activity.* The route's entries are shown with the audit page's sentences (the same catalogue keys), through an adapter in `lib/comments/logic.ts` that gives the sentence the one name it needs. A gone person reads "former member"; an installation admin's act names no one. A page that comes back empty with a cursor is followed to the next page, for up to 20 empty pages, and "show more" follows any cursor left (`followEmpty`, decision 50 point (e)). The pane has no kind filter in r7a; it shows what the server lists for the caller.
    - *Who viewed.* The tab is shown to a manager of the file only, and only once the list answers. The list carries the note that it is a convenience and not evidence (decision 51). A name is shown while the person reaches the file, "former member" when the person no longer does, and "name not shown" past the server's bound of 40 people, where nobody was checked. No ID is shown. Turning the switch on begins a new period, which the settings page says.
    - *One server change: a reason on the who-viewed refusal.* A manager cannot read the account's switch (the route is the owner's or the key's), so the list's refusal while the switch is off carries `reason: who_viewed_off`, as the comments refusal carries `reason: comments_off`. The change is one line in `internal/api/viewers.go`, and `TestViewersOffByDefaultAndOnForManagers` checks the reason.
    - *The owner's switches.* Two switches sit on the owner's Overview page beside the switch for links (`web/src/components/comments/SharingSwitches.tsx`): comments (on by default) and who-viewed (off by default). Each is saved on its own, with the same `PATCH sharing-policy` the links switch uses (`setSharingSwitches`). The installation admin's page does not show them.
    - *Not built, named.* (a) The bell, the notifications page and the notification email settings: r7b. (b) The notice on the file for people who cannot read the switch (question 12): a non-manager cannot read the switch, so the notice cannot be shown to them without a new read route. (c) The installation admin's allowance per tenant (question 12, first half; decision 51). (d) The duplicate display names disambiguator (decisions 39 and 43 say r7 must revisit it): the people list still shows two people with one name alike. (e) Comment search and assignment (questions 13 and 14). (f) The comment webhook (r6). (g) A kind filter on the Activity tab.
    - *Tests.* Unit: `web/src/lib/comments/logic.test.ts` (permissions, mention text and references, the body limits at their edges, `followEmpty`, the activity adapter, the three who-viewed states, the refusal reasons, and the times), `catalogue.test.ts`, and `web/src/components/comments/comments.test.tsx` (the composer's send and its kept text, the refused send, the limit before a send, the hostile body, the role-dependent actions, delete with its question, resolve, the first load's error, a failed refetch keeping the list, the reply paging, the tab rules for the switch and for a manager, the empty-page follow, the gone actor, the mention debounce, the stale answer, the rate-limit text, and the owner's two switches). The server test is `TestViewersOffByDefaultAndOnForManagers` in `internal/api/viewers_test.go`.
    - *Review fixes (after the review of 624a1c5).* (1) An edit, resolve or delete refused as gone or off reads the list again, and a delete refused that way closes its confirm. (2) A send refused as off keeps its text and does not reload the panel: the panel is read on its next read, so the text survives the refusal. A send refused as gone or as a reply under a reply reads the list now; a reply under a reply has its own text. (3) Every write also refreshes the Activity: the tabs keep a visited pane mounted, so it would otherwise go stale. (4) A failed catalogue load shows the main texts' error with a Reload button. The button reloads the page, not the section: a browser keeps a module that failed to load, so a retry in the page cannot succeed. A chunk that does not load is caught by a boundary around the tabs in the drawer, so the rest of the drawer stays usable; the page's own error boundary would replace the whole page. (5) The name picker: Enter or a click returns the focus to the box; `aria-controls` is set only while the list is open. Escape closes the open list. With a name typed in the picker, or text in the composer, Escape stops at the composer and does not reach the drawer, so the draft stays. With both empty, Escape closes the drawer as before. (6) A refusal for an old search does not put its note on the newer search. (7) The replies: the rest is shown as loading while it is read, and a failed read is shown even when the first page had no reply. (8) The composer stays editable during a send, a second send is refused while one is in flight, text typed during a send is kept when the send succeeds, and a failed send leaves the focus in the box. (9) On a coarse pointer the name picker's box is 44 px high, checked at phone width by `web/e2e/r7.mjs`. Tests: run against the previous component files, 13 of the new tests failed (the edit, resolve, delete, activity, switch, send focus and in-flight, replies, picker keyboard, Escape, old-search note, and the chunk boundary and catalogue-failure views); the two fault-mapping tests failed against the previous `logic.ts` and `faults.ts`. The tests that pass on the previous files are guards of behaviour that already held (a failed edit keeps its text, a second send is refused, who-viewed leaves the tab mid-session). Item 5 (the 44 px box) is checked only by the end-to-end run, which measured it at 44 px; it was not run with the rule removed.
    - *Browser checks.* `web/e2e/r7.mjs`, wired into `run.mjs` by `SELFCLOUD_E2E_ONLY=r7`, beside w2. It runs as the owner, then as the member, in one browser: the owner names the member by typing and picking, posts a body with markup (which makes no image and runs no script, and is shown literally), has a refused send keep its text, resolves, and reads the activity; the member replies and edits, and sees no Edit on the owner's comment and no Who viewed tab; the owner deletes the reply as a manager; the owner turns comments off and on, and turns who-viewed on, from the owner's page. The pictures (with `SELFCLOUD_R7_SHOTS`) are taken at desktop and phone width, in English and Hebrew, in light and dark. A Hebrew check reads the right-to-left direction and the Hebrew tab names. Each check compares a value the page shows; none is a constant.

The server change is checked by `TestViewersOffByDefaultAndOnForManagers`, which fails without the reason.

The line is shared with the other slices and was left as it is. Two harness facts came up: a press made while the drawer slides in lands beside its target, so the checks wait for the slide to end; and Chrome does not select all on Ctrl+A sent as a key, so the edit field is emptied through the page's input.

56. **Cover art and tags from audio files, slice x3** (2026-11-01, built to decision 45's x3 line of `design-w-proposal.md`: "Cover art and tags from audio files (read on the server by the derived-files pipeline): title, artist, album, duration", with the owner's answer "queue first, saved next (x4 follows as its own slice, with cover art and tags)"). Migration 0041 (`audio_tags`). Built as follows, and each point is a choice the owner may want to confirm.
    - *Dependency: none added.* The readers are in `internal/audio`, hand-rolled. The module proxy was reachable, and `github.com/dhowden/tag` was not taken: it gives no duration, it allocates each frame at its declared size, and it would have been one more licence to check (BSD-2, compatible) in a parser that reads files anyone may upload. Duration needs the container headers either way. `golang.org/x/text`, already required, provides the NFC normalisation.
    - *Formats.* MP3: ID3v2.2, v2.3 and v2.4 (text frames, APIC or PIC, unsynchronisation, the extended header, compressed or encrypted frames skipped), ID3v1 for what the v2 tag left empty (Latin-1). Duration from the Xing, Info or VBRI header of the first frame, else estimated from the bitrate and the audio's bytes (a variable-rate file with no header may be off). FLAC: Vorbis comments, the PICTURE block, duration from STREAMINFO. Ogg Vorbis and Ogg Opus: the comment packet (`METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE` for a cover), duration from the last page's granule (Opus less its pre-skip, at 48 kHz). MP4 and M4A: `moov/udta/meta/ilst` (©nam, ©ART, ©alb, covr), duration from `mvhd`. Not read: ID3 in other containers, raw AAC (ADTS), WAV, AIFF, WMA, APE, and Ogg streams other than Vorbis and Opus.
    - *Bounds.* Each read takes at most 16 MiB (`maxRead`). A tag value keeps at most 256 characters. A picture is at most 8 MiB (`MaxPicture`); a larger one is no cover. ID3: 512 frames a tag, and a frame whose declared size passes the tag's end stops the tag there. FLAC: 256 metadata blocks, and a block past the end stops the walk. MP4: 4096 boxes a level; a box whose size is under its header or past the file is corrupt; `moov` over 16 MiB is refused as too large. Ogg: 512 pages read at the head (a picture of several megabytes spans more than 64), a 64 KiB window at the tail for the granule, a packet at most 16 MiB, 1024 comments, a granule at most 2^40. The tags child writes at most 8 KiB of JSON, and the parent checks it again (a value over 256 characters, a control or format character, a bidirectional override, a newline, or a duration over a week is given up and stored as 0, the title and artist being kept). A header that is malformed refuses the file (`ErrCorrupt`); a tag block that is malformed or cut short keeps what was read before it. A panic inside the reader is recovered as `ErrCorrupt`.
    - *Text.* Each value is NFC-normalised. Control characters and format characters (bidirectional controls included) become spaces, except the zero-width joiner and non-joiner, which Arabic and Persian need. Runs of white space become one space. The client shows the values as text nodes, with `dir="auto"` where the page places them. Nothing is rendered as markup.
    - *The size rule, the one departure from the thumbnails.* A thumbnail refuses a source over `derived.max_source_bytes` (50 MiB). An audio file is read by seeking to its head, its tail and the `moov` box, not whole, so a file is refused by `derived.audio_max_source_bytes` instead (100 GiB by default; the validator allows up to 1 TiB). The child's stdin is the file itself, so it can seek; a non-seekable input is read whole up to the image cap, which the parent never sends. The pool sniffs the first 12 bytes to choose the limit, and the route checks the stored type the same way.
    - *Routes.* `GET` and `HEAD /api/v1/nodes/{nod}/tags`: the node's state, `ready` with the values, `none` (a read that failed, or a file with no tags the reader could use), `pending` with `202` and `Retry-After`. A folder, a shortcut and a file of another type are `not_found`. `GET /api/v1/media/tags?ids=` answers up to 100 nodes at once; a node the caller cannot read, or that is not audio, is left out, and is `pending` while queued. A cover is not a new route: an audio file's `/thumbnail` is its cover, through the same pool, cache, budget and content-origin redirect as an image's, and `has_thumbnail` is true on it when it has one (so the grid's tiles show a cover for an audio file). The listing carries `tags` on audio files whose read has finished, in the same query shape as `has_thumbnail`; a link visitor gets none, and the tags route refuses a link visitor as it refuses a thumbnail (`link_route`); the web reads tags through the batch route with a session.
    - *Access.* `nodeAccess` runs first on each route, as for a thumbnail, so a caller who cannot read a node gets the same answer as for a node that does not exist. A tags read is viewing, not downloading: the no-download rule does not refuse it, as decision 33 for thumbnails. The read queues through the thumbnail pool (its workers, queue and per-account share) and its own limiter, `tags.enqueue` (300 a minute per caller).
    - *Pipeline.* A tags read is a derived row of kind `audio_tags` (converter `tags-go-1+<hash of the source limit>`, `TagsVersion`), with the state, retry and sticky rules of a thumbnail, and its values in `audio_tags` in the same transaction that marks the row ready. A row holds no file and counts no bytes, so the budget never evicts it; the values go with the blob (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), so a replaced file, a deleted file and an account's deletion drop them with the rest. A cover is an ordinary thumbnail row, so the existing eviction, orphan sweep, blob removal and start-up recovery apply to it unchanged. `EncoderVersion` is unchanged: no audio was thumbnailed before this slice, so no old row exists to be served.
    - *Failure messages.* A file the reader refuses is sticky for its key: corrupt tags, not an audio format the server reads, over the source limit, or no cover picture the server can show (exit 68: no picture, or a picture the thumbnail decoder does not accept, JPEG, PNG or GIF). A host fault (time limit, stopped child, out of memory) is retried as for a thumbnail.
    - *Tests.* `internal/audio/audio_test.go`: the seven fixtures (ffmpeg made, under `testdata`, Hebrew title and PNG cover in ID3v2.4 and v2.3, ID3v1 added in the test to a tagless file, FLAC and M4A with covers, Ogg Vorbis and Opus), each read with its expected values; every truncation of each fixture; 400 seeded random damages of five fixtures; a declared frame size of 0x0FFFFFFF; a tag declared at 256 MiB; a picture past the cap and without a description end; FLAC blocks past the end and a short STREAMINFO; MP4 box sizes below the header, past the file, and a `moov` over the cap (a file of zeros that names 20 MiB, so no memory holds it); an Ogg granule of 2^62; `cleanText`; `Sniff`. `internal/derived/tags_test.go`: a read marks the row ready and a second request queues nothing; the source limit refuses sticky; not-audio refuses sticky; a corrupt header refuses sticky; the child's JSON is checked value by value; the output limit cuts at one byte past. `internal/api/tags_test.go`: the real child process reads the fixture, the single route, the listing, the batch and the cover (JPEG from the thumbnail route); a file with no tags answers `none`; a corrupt file answers `none`; another account gets `not_found` and is left out of a batch; a folder and an image are `not_found`; the batch refuses bad IDs.
      Mutations (each applied to the source, the named tests run, the source restored byte for byte): `cleanText` without the format-character strip (`TestCleanText` fails: the override kept); the ID3 frame bound removed (`TestID3FrameDeclaredPastTheFileIsRefused` fails: the file is refused); the value check removed from `checkedTags` (`TestCheckedTagsRefusesWhatTheChildMustNotSend` fails on the bidirectional override, the newline, the control character and the over-length value, among others).
    - *Review round (the coordinator's security review of this commit).* Fixed: a batch whose budget of new reads runs out answers `pending` for those nodes and `200` for the rest, instead of `429` for the whole request; the web client retries a failed request with a doubling back-off (2 s, capped at 30 s, six tries), and a pending node after a fixed wait (six asks). The derived row and the values agree on one converter: `AudioTagsFor` joins the row in state `ready` under the current converter, so a value from an older reader is not shown on any route or listing. The converter key includes `audio_max_source_bytes`, so raising the limit does not keep refusals made under the old one. The tags child is given a 1 MiB input cap, so a non-seekable input is never read whole. Every file's reads are capped at 64 MiB in all (`maxTotalRead`); a tag declared over 16 MiB is skipped whole, a v2.3 extended header counts its own four bytes, and a UTF-16 description's terminator is searched at an even offset. Text: the Hangul fillers (U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0) and the braille blank (U+2800) are blank, and a run of combining marks keeps two. A cover changes with its node: the web shows no previous file's picture on the first frame of a new node. The reader's `Read` no longer hides a panic (the test calls the inner reader, so a bounds check removed is a panic seen by the test). Fuzz targets `FuzzRead` and `FuzzFormats` (`internal/audio/fuzz_test.go`) run their seeds with `go test`; a short fuzz run found no crash. Not changed, for the owner to decide: a no-download viewer still gets covers and tags (a tags read is viewing, as above).
    - *Second review round.* (a) The batch's requests are limited per caller by `tags.batch` (120 a minute): each request walks up to 100 nodes for access, and the read budget `tags.enqueue` (300 a minute) counts only the reads a request queues, so the limit is on the requests themselves. A refused request is `429` for the whole request, with `Retry-After`; a read the budget cannot queue is still `pending`. Test `TestTagsBatchRequestsAreLimitedPerCaller` failed first (200 where 429 is due). (b) The web's retry stays inside `tags.batch`. A 500-track queue is 5 batches of 100. Each retry round sends at most 5 more requests. Pending reads are asked at most 6 times, so the queue asks at most 5 + 5 x 6 = 35 times; failed requests are retried at most 6 times, again at most 35. The two are not added for one node, since a node is pending or failed in one answer; the worst mix is 65 requests over the whole retry, and at most 60 in any 60 seconds (the back-off spaces the failed rounds at 2, 6, 14, 30 and 60 s). One queue load is therefore 65 requests against 120 a minute; two loads at once can exceed it, and a refused request backs off. Tests `asks no more than 35 times for a 500-track queue...` pin the 35. (c) The playlist row's playing mark is an icon, its word in screen-reader-only text, so it no longer takes the room a title needs. Before: the mark sat 4 px from the More button, the short title's box was 68 px and the artist 59 px; after: 8 px, 84 px and 62 px (the e2e `rowFit` measures, which failed first). The mark's word stays in the row's text content. The title and artist are in `title` attributes, so a cut name reads in full on hover. A title keeps a floor of 6em, so a long artist gives way first. Not reproduced: the clipped "Playing" label that was reported. The measured label text stayed inside the row at every size; what the screenshot showed was the label touching the More button, which the 8 px gap now fixes. Known limit: a title mixing Hebrew and English can cut its ellipsis mid-title, a bidi effect of `dir="auto"`.
    - *Not built here.* Firefox and Safari were not checked. The lock screen's artwork was not seen on a device. Saved playlists (x4) and transcoding (x5) are not built. A read of a 100 GB file's head and tail has not been timed on the server. The Hebrew and Arabic strings in the web interface are machine drafts, as in earlier slices.

57. **Bell, notifications page and email switch, slice r7b** (2026-11-01, built to the owner-approved proposal for slice r (`design-r-proposal.md`), section 1 items 3 and 8, section 7.1, section 7.2 and questions 9 and 10, with the routes as the server has them today). The web interface only: the server is unchanged, and no migration. Each point below is a choice the owner may want to confirm.
    - *Where it sits.* The bell is in the top bar, beside the language choice, in its own chunk (`web/src/components/notifications/Bell.tsx`, loaded from `Shell.tsx`). It is drawn for a person of the drive only: not for an installation admin, and not while a person is signed in as another (the server refuses the inbox in both cases, `ownNotifyCaller`). There is no sidebar entry: the bell is the way in.
    - *The count.* It reads `GET /notifications/unread` when the bar appears, once a minute while the tab is shown, and again when the tab comes back (react-query's window focus). Nothing is read while the tab is hidden (`pollInterval`, tested). A failed read keeps the count on the screen and shows no error. The count is in a polite live region, so a screen reader hears "3 unread" or "No unread notifications", and the button's name carries it too. A count of 100 or more, or the server's `more` flag, shows as 99+. The server reads at most 100 unread rows (`notifyUnreadScan`).
    - *The routes as built, where the proposal differs.* The proposal's `POST /notifications/read` with `{ids}` or `{all: true}` is built as `POST /notifications/{ntf}/read`, one notification per call, as decision 43 built it. **There is no "mark all" route, so the page has no "mark all" button and no loop that would send one call per line.** The count route is `GET /notifications/unread`, answering `{count, more}`; the proposal named no count route. Nothing on the server changed.
    - *Opening a line.* It marks the line read (only when it is unread) and goes to `/n/{nod}?details=comments`. `NodeLinkPage` keeps the request through its redirect (`linkQuery`, tested), and `FilesPage` selects the item and opens its details drawer, whose Comments tab holds the thread. The node ID is checked for its shape before it is used in an address; a line whose ID does not pass says it has no file to open and goes nowhere. **Not covered:** a file the person reaches only on its own (its folder listing is out of reach, so `/n/` shows the preview alone). It opens with no comments, because the details drawer needs the folder listing. The line still marks read.
    - *What a line says.* "{actor} mentioned you in {item}" or "{actor} replied to your comment on {item}". A former member reads "A former member", a name the server does not give reads "Someone", and an item with no name reads "an item". No ID is printed (the browser run checks the page's text for `nod_`, `ntf_` and `usr_`). The item name and the actor name come from the route. The comment text is never on the page.
    - *Email switch.* It is on the notifications page, saved by `PATCH /notifications/settings`. The switch shows the value the server last gave; a refused or failed save leaves that value, so the switch goes back, and a message says it could not be saved. A saved choice is still there after a reload (browser run).
    - *Texts.* A separate namespace, `notifications`, in seven catalogues (`web/src/i18n/notifications/`), loaded with the bell, as r7a did for comments. Hebrew and Arabic are machine drafts, to be read by a speaker. The placeholders take single braces and are not called `count`: the main i18next instance reads `count` as a plural selector, and a count in a plural-less text came out raw in the first run.
    - *Budget, measured.* Before the review's fixes the first load was 327.1 KB gzip over 38 files (r7a stood at 324.6 over 33). The bell is not the cause: with the bell taken out of the shell the figure was still 327.0. The rise came from antd's modal, skeleton and rc-util's `useId` being preloaded by the entry. One change in `web/vite.config.ts` puts those three into one shared chunk, `antd-shared`: the first load is now 323.7 KB over 25 files, and `check-dist` passes. That shared chunk is 119.8 KB gzip against its 120 KB budget, so the next addition to it breaks the build; the owner should know that. The `zoom` helper the review named is not one of these modules and is not moved.
    - *Review fixes (the independent review of ef285cb).* (1) The page's Show more, Try again and Reload buttons are 44 px on a finger. (2) A failed bell chunk, or a bell that throws, renders nothing where the bell was (`BellBoundary.tsx`), and the rest of the bar stays. (3) The shell's negative guard tests wait for the lazy bell to settle, then check that no unread read was made. (4) A failed next page says so in its own message, in all seven catalogues. (5) When the server stopped counting (`more`), the badge, the button's name and the live region all show 99+, including with no reachable count. (6) While the person is signed in as another, the page says so and reads no inbox; a failed email read has a Try again. (7) A bell that mounts in a hidden tab makes no request until the tab is shown.
    - *Shell change.* One lazy import and a block of five lines in the top bar. `Shell.test.tsx` wraps its render in a `QueryClientProvider`, since the shell now reads a query: the app already had one.
    - *Not done.* The duplicate display names disambiguator that decision 43 asked slice r7 to decide: two people with one name still look alike in the list. Left open, as decision 55 left it.
    - *Tests.* Written first and seen to fail (missing modules and functions). Unit: `web/src/lib/notifications/logic.test.ts` (polling, the count's text and cap, the sentences, the former member and the someone rule, the address and its refusal, the paging helpers), `catalogue.test.ts` (seven catalogues, the same keys, a text for each, every literal key used), `web/src/components/notifications/Bell.test.tsx` (the count and its announcement, the zero state, a failed read keeps the count, the press opens the page), `bellShown.test.tsx` (not for an admin, not while impersonating), `web/src/pages/NotificationsPage.test.tsx` (the first-load error, the list as sentences with no ID, a failed refresh keeps the list, the next page, the mark and the address, a bad address, the switch saved and refused), and `web/src/lib/files/nodeLinkDetails.test.ts` (the query the address carries).
    - *Mutation proofs.* Four changes, made together and restored byte for byte: the polling read while hidden (`logic.test.ts` fails); the bad address opened anyway (`NotificationsPage.test.tsx` fails); the bell drawn for an admin and while impersonating (`bellShown.test.tsx` fails, two tests); the switch shown as the typed value after a refused save (`NotificationsPage.test.tsx` fails). After the review, eight more, each restored: the hidden-tab gate removed (`Bell.test.tsx`); the boundary passing errors through (`BellBoundary.test.tsx`); the admin and impersonation guard removed (`bellShown.test.tsx`, two tests); the impersonation check off on the page (`NotificationsPage.test.tsx`); the next-page message off (`NotificationsPage.test.tsx`); the touch size 32 px (`NotificationsPage.test.tsx`); the email Try again doing nothing (`NotificationsPage.test.tsx`); the 99+ badge dropped at zero (`logic.test.ts`, `Bell.test.tsx`).
    - *Browser run.* `web/e2e/r7b.mjs`, wired into `run.mjs` by `SELFCLOUD_E2E_ONLY=r7b`. The owner names the member in a comment; the member's bell reads one more on the next load, with its name and the screen reader's text; the notice reads as a sentence with "Unread"; the email switch goes off and stays off after a reload, and goes back on; opening the notice shows the file on its Comments tab and the bell returns to its earlier number; at phone width there is no sideways scroll and the bell and the switch row are 44 px on a finger; Hebrew sets the page right to left and names it. The pictures are saved in the plans folder, not in the repository. A 403 from the who-viewed route is filtered out, as r7 does, because a member who does not manage a file is refused it on purpose.
58. **Saved playlists, slice x4** (2026-11-02, built to decision 45's x4 line of `design-w-proposal.md`: "Saved playlists, on the server: named, ordered, per user; entries that were deleted or lost show as unavailable; never reveal a file the user cannot reach. API routes, migration, audit", with the owner's answer "queue first, saved next"). Migration 0042 (`0042_playlists.sql`): `playlists` and `playlist_entries`. Built as follows. Each point is a choice the owner may want to confirm.
    - *Who may use them.* The signed-in user only, as media resume and the recent list are: a delegated token, an account key, and an installation admin get `forbidden`, and every playlist route refuses impersonation (`impRefuse`, on the GET too, since a playlist is the user's own). Stars allow a read through a token; playlists do not, on purpose.
    - *Routes* (`internal/api/playlists.go`): `GET`/`POST /api/v1/playlists`; `GET`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/v1/playlists/{pls}`; `POST /api/v1/playlists/{pls}/entries` (append one file); `PUT /api/v1/playlists/{pls}/entries` (replace the list with the nodes given, in order); `DELETE /api/v1/playlists/{pls}/entries/{ple}` (remove one, reachable or not); `PUT /api/v1/playlists/{pls}/order` (the entry IDs in their new order, each once). Rate limits `playlist.read` 120 and `playlist.write` 60 a minute, per user.
    - *Bounds, refused by code.* 100 playlists a user (conflict, reason `limit`); 500 entries a playlist, the queue's own cap so a saved queue always fits (conflict on append, invalid_request on replace); a name of 1 to 120 characters after trimming, with no control characters (invalid_request); a node listed once in a replace (invalid_request).
    - *Reach, checked on every read.* Each read asks `reachRoles` for all of the playlist's entries in one query, and reads a node only for an entry the caller reaches. An entry the caller cannot reach, whose node is trashed, purged, not a file, or of another account, is `{entry_id, position, node_id, unavailable: true}` with no node: no name, size, type, role, tags or cover. The four causes answer alike (the test diffs the shapes). The node ID stays, because the caller put it there and the web needs it to remove or keep the entry. Tags and covers come from the existing batch route, which checks reach itself (decision 56).
    - *Adding a file.* The reach is checked inside the write, before anything else, and an unreachable, missing, trashed, another account's or non-file node answers the same `not_found` with the same body (the test compares bodies with the request ID removed). The check runs even when the playlist already holds the file, so the answer does not change with its history.
    - *Replacing.* A node the playlist already holds is kept with no reach check, so an unavailable entry can still be kept, reordered or removed; a node new to the playlist must pass the same check, and one refusal refuses the whole write. Entries kept keep their IDs.
    - *No-download files.* The queue plays a no-download file (its own comment: playing is not downloading, decision 45 x1), so a playlist accepts it and lists it as playable. The proposal's "rules that stay" say a no-download file "does not join a playlist and shows as restricted". Those two readings conflict. This slice follows the queue, as the brief asked. The owner should decide; the change would be one check in `addableIn` and one in the read.
    - *Deletion.* `playlists.account_id` and `playlists.user_id` cascade from accounts and users; `playlist_entries.playlist_id` cascades from playlists. `node_id` has **no** foreign key, so a node that is purged leaves its entry in place, which then reads as unavailable (the brief's "deleted shows as unavailable"); the user removes it, or the playlist goes with its account. A trashed node is unavailable, because the reach check reads the trash on every read; that it reads as playable again after a restore follows from the same check and is not tested. Account deletion needs no code of its own: `DeleteAccount` removes the account row and the cascades do the rest (`TestPlaylistAccountDeleteCascades` counts the rows left, which is zero). A user's deletion is left to the same cascade; it is not tested here.
    - *Audit.* `playlist.create`, `playlist.rename`, `playlist.delete` and `playlist.entries` (the last with `change` add, remove, replace or reorder, and `count`). No name, no node ID, no entry ID appears in an entry. Each is private to its user (`PrivateUserID`), so the account's owner does not read them, as a personal folder's entries are not read by the owner. The web sentences are `audit.playlist.*` in all seven catalogues.
    - *Cost of a read.* The largest playlist is 500 entries. `TestPlaylistReadCost` builds one under a user with a reach on the top folder and times the GET in process: 51 ms on the development machine (one run, `go test -run TestPlaylistReadCost -v`). The test's bound is 5 s. This is the reach query plus the node read, with no network and no response encoding of the file bodies (there are none).
    - *Web.* The player's queue panel gains a "Saved playlists" section (`components/files/MediaPlaylists.tsx`, the `saved` slot of `MediaQueue`, shown in the signed-in player only: a share page has none). Save the queue (name, then the queue's files in order), open one to replace the queue (its first playable file starts, since the file that was on screen is not in the list; `replaceEntries` in `lib/files/queue.ts`), rename, delete after a Popconfirm, and edit: remove and move entries. An unavailable entry is the mark `unavailable`, a row that reads "Unavailable", is never played, and is not counted as a failure, so a run of them stops nothing (`queue.playlist.test.ts`). A failed refresh keeps the list; a failed first load shows an error with a retry (`MediaPlaylists.test.tsx`). Buttons are 44 px on a touch screen, and stay so under the pointer and when focused (e2e `touchSizes`).
    - *Catalogues.* The 28 `files.playlists.*` keys and the four `audit.playlist.*` keys are in the main catalogue. Russian is 22.8 KB gzip against 25 KB, so no lazy namespace was needed; the build reports the largest language at 21.9 KB, the first load at 323.6 KB of 330, and the largest other chunk at 95.8 KB of 120. Hebrew and Arabic are machine drafts. The file count is a plural (`files.playlists.count_one` and `_other`; Russian and Arabic have the fuller sets), as the other counts are; see "Review of slice x4" below.
    - *Tests.* Go: `playlists_test.go`, 13 tests, one per access case in the brief (another user's playlist, an entry whose access was removed, a trashed entry, a purged entry, an entry of another account, a token, the account key, identical answers for unreachable and missing). Two route-wide guards pass: `TestRoutesMatchSpec` (every route documented) and `TestNodeKindComparisonsAreReviewed` (the two new comparisons reviewed in `kind_guard_test.go`). `TestEveryAuditActionHasASentence` passes. Mutation checks, run and reverted: taking out the read's reach check fails `TestPlaylistAccessRemoved` and `TestPlaylistTrashedAndDeletedEntries`; taking out the add's reach check fails `TestPlaylistUnreachableAddIsIndistinguishable` and `TestPlaylistReplaceKeepsUnavailableEntries`. The tests were first written against the code and failed on their own harness (a request ID in every body, a node ID that differs by design); those were corrected in the tests, not in the code. Web: `queue.playlist.test.ts` and `MediaPlaylists.test.tsx` pass, with the existing 297 player, queue and i18n tests. Those web tests were not shown to fail before the code existed, and they say so. e2e `x4.mjs`, run with `SELFCLOUD_E2E_ONLY=x4`: passes on a local build, covering save, the unavailable row after a trashed file, rename, entry removal, delete after a confirmation, and the touch sizes in English and Hebrew, light and dark.
    - *Not covered.* Impersonation is covered by the route table's refusal flags and the route-wide impersonation test, not by a test that signs in as another user and tries these routes. The rate limits have no test of their own. A user's deletion is not tested. Firefox and Safari were not checked. The no-download question above is open. Transcoding (x5) is not built.

    *Review of slice x4* (the owner's reviewer's findings, each with a test that failed first, except where stated):
    - *A saved playlist ends at its own end.* A queue that came from a saved playlist is not continued with the folder's next page (`fromSaved` in `MediaPlaylist.tsx`; `MediaPlaylist.saved.test.tsx`). Checked by breaking the guard: the test fails with "called 1 times".
    - *Opening a saved playlist plays it.* The file that was on screen is not in the playlist, so the player would show nothing; the first playable file now starts. This changes the rule above, which said the on-screen file keeps playing.
    - *Saving makes one playlist.* The create takes the files in the same write (`POST /api/v1/playlists` with `nodes`, optional), so a refused file leaves no playlist and a retry makes the only one (`TestPlaylistCreateWithEntriesIsAtomic`, failed first: the server ignored `nodes`). The save dialog ignores a second Enter or click while a save runs, with a ref (`MediaPlaylists.test.tsx`: the one-call test fails first with two calls).
    - *Moves and removals run one at a time.* The editor's buttons are disabled while an edit runs, and a second press does nothing, so no order is built from rows an edit in flight is about to change (`sends one move when its button is pressed twice`, failed first with two calls).
    - *The newest Play wins.* A read that answers after a later Play is dropped (`the newest Play wins when the earlier one answers last`, failed first).
    - *An unavailable entry cannot be picked.* `choose` refuses it as it refuses a restricted file (`queue.playlist.test.ts`, failed first: the mark became `ok`).
    - *An editor's first-load error has a retry* (`an editor whose first read fails can be read again`, failed first: no button).
    - *Migration 0042 (edited in place; not shipped).* `playlists_account` indexes `account_id`, which account deletion scans. `playlist_entries_node` is dropped: nothing reads entries by node (`TestPlaylistIndexes`, failed first on both).
    - *The count is a plural.* One file reads "1 file" and "1 קובץ"; the keys are `files.playlists.count_one` and `_other` (`playlists.plural.test.ts`, failed first for en, es and he at one file). The three-file forms passed from the start, as they were the base text.
    - *The buttons of a saved row have a gap.* Play, Edit, rename and Delete have 6 px between them, the gap the queue's own button row has. The e2e `rowGaps` check read 0 px before the fix and passed after.
    - *Not changed, as the owner asked.* The no-download question stays open, above. Bidi characters in names are left as they are.
    - *Verification.* Web: `queue.playlist.test.ts`, `playlists.plural.test.ts`, `MediaPlaylist.saved.test.tsx`, `MediaPlaylists.test.tsx`, and the existing player and queue tests (`MediaPlaylist*.test.tsx`, `queue*.test.ts`), 83 of 84 passing in one run; the one failure was `MediaPlaylist.review.test.tsx` "after the failure run stops, a pick plays again", which timed out at 20 s under the parallel load and passed when its file ran alone (23.9 s, 6 of 6). Go: `TestPlaylist*` and the store's `TestPlaylistIndexes`. e2e: `SELFCLOUD_E2E_ONLY=x4`, see the commit.

59. **Document previews and exports in the web interface, the failed state of a conversion, slice s4b** (2026-11-01, built to the owner-approved proposal for slice s, section 9, with every recommendation (a) that applies, and to decisions 37 and 38). Decisions 54 to 58 belong to other branches. Migration: none. Decision 10 holds: no converter runs in the server, and the document goes to Collabora.
    - **The fault, and the fix.** A failed conversion answered `404` on the ID's first read, and its reason came only from a repeat `POST`, which answered `415` with the reason `failed`. The page could not tell a failure from a missing file. The smallest honest fix is one answer for a refused conversion, `415` with the reason `failed`, given by every read: the preview `GET` and `HEAD`, the export `GET` and `HEAD`, and the repeat `POST` (`convertFailed` in `internal/api/exports.go`). `404` stays for a row that does not exist, and a preview `HEAD` with no row is still `404`. A failure the server expects to clear (an outage, or a counted time-out) keeps its `503` with `Retry-After`. Tests: `TestFailedExportAnswersItsReasonOnTheFirstRead` and `TestFailedPreviewAnswersItsReason` (both answered `404` before the fix), and `TestConverterRefusalIsStickyAndItsTextIsKept`, which asserted `404` and now asserts `415`. The OpenAPI text for the preview, the export and `features` is updated to match.
    - **Office signal.** `GET /api/v1/info` lists `office_convert` in `features` while `office.enabled` is on, and an empty list while it is off (`TestInfoNamesTheConversionWhileOfficeIsOn`). The page reads the list at start-up into `officeConvert` (`lib/files/convert.ts`).
    - **Preview, in the viewer.** An office document opens in the viewer while the feature is on, and its card offers a Preview button; opening the file does not start a conversion. The Preview button makes one request that queues the conversion, then `HEAD` requests until the answer is final (`watchPreview`; `HEAD` starts no work, decision 37). A `303` from the content origin is read as ready (`redirect: "manual"`), and the frame loads the preview's own address, so the browser follows the redirect. The PDF is shown in an `iframe` with no `sandbox` attribute, as the existing PDF viewer shows one (design section 10). The states are: asking, converting, ready, failed (by its name), not convertible, unavailable (with a retry button), too large, and slow (after 90 waits, with the text "taking longer than expected", not an endless spinner). Leaving a file while its preview is being made stops that watch. Coming back to the file shows the Preview button again, and starts nothing by itself: the card does not resume the old wait (the choice here: no resume, since a fresh request is the only thing that can say the state now). The reset is in `Preview.tsx` (the effect on the node ID), tested by `Preview.office.test.tsx`, "returns to a file left mid-conversion with the Preview button, not a stale wait" (failed first: it showed the making text with no button).
    - **Export, in the viewer.** An Export menu in the viewer header lists PDF and the formats of the document's family: `docx` gives PDF, DOCX and ODT; `xlsx` gives PDF, XLSX and ODS; `pptx` gives PDF, PPTX and ODP; a legacy `doc`, `xls` or `ppt` gives PDF only. Cross-family conversions are not offered, because the live converter fails them (decision 37, item 9). Choosing a format opens `ExportDialog` (its own lazy chunk), which queues the export, polls its ID with `HEAD`, and starts the download when the export is ready, through the existing download link. The dialog shows a spinner and text, not a percentage, since the server reports no progress. Closing the dialog stops the watch; the server finishes the export, and no download starts. Two ends are not success. (a) A download that cannot start (the request rejects, or the download returns false) shows the error text "Something went wrong. Try again." and a Download again button, and never the ready text; the button starts the download of the same link again (`ExportDialog.tsx`, `ExportDialog.test.tsx`, "shows an error, not the ready text, when the download cannot start, and retries it", failed first: the ready text showed). (b) An outage the server names (`503` with `Retry-After` on the export `HEAD`) shows "The converter is not available right now. Try again in a minute." with a Try again button, which asks the server again: the export `POST` is repeated and returns the same row, then the watch starts over. The choice here: a retry button, not continued polling, to match the viewer's preview, where a person waits for the answer rather than the dialog. A refused conversion (`415` with `failed`) has no retry, since the server keeps that refusal for a day. The export is in the viewer only, not in the file toolbar or the row menu, so the toolbar is unchanged.
    - **Refusals by name.** The text of each failure is chosen by status and reason (`failureOf`, `failureKey`): a 403 is the no-download text, a 413 is too large, a 415 with `not_convertible` is not convertible, a 415 with `failed` is the conversion failed, and a 503 or 429 is the converter unavailable. The server's English is never shown.
    - **No-download.** The Preview and the Export are not offered to a viewer whose downloads are off, and the server refuses both (decision 37). A `403` from the preview is shown as the no-download text.
    - **Office off.** No feature, no button, and nothing asked of the server. Covered by Go and vitest only: Go, `TestInfoNamesTheConversionWhileOfficeIsOn` (the `features` list is empty with office off) and `TestConversionRoutesAreOffWhileOfficeIsOff` (`internal/api/exports_test.go`, every conversion route answers not_found) and `TestConvertedLinkIsNotFoundWhileOfficeIsOff`; vitest, `Preview.office.test.tsx`, "shows no preview button and no export menu while the server does not offer conversion" (`fetch` is never called). **There is no browser run with office off**: the e2e configuration has office on for every section, and no run has shown the page with office off. The page's office-off behaviour is therefore unit-tested, not seen in a browser.
    - **Languages.** Twelve keys in the seven catalogues (`files.convert.*`; 1,356 keys in each file). Spanish, French, Portuguese and Russian were written here. **Hebrew and Arabic are machine drafts, to be read by a speaker.**
    - **Touch targets.** The preview and export buttons carry the class `convert-btn`, which is 44 px tall on a coarse pointer (`index.css`). The e2e measures them at rest, under the pointer and focused, on a coarse pointer, at desktop and phone width: 44 px in each state (`touchTargets` in `web/e2e/s4b.mjs`).
    - **Tests.** Go: the three tests above, and the existing export, preview, refusal, outage and info tests in `internal/api` (narrowed run: all pass). Web: `convert.test.ts` (20 tests), `Preview.office.test.tsx` (8 tests, the stale-wait test added in the review round), `ExportDialog.test.tsx` (2 tests, new). Review round, narrowed vitest run of those three files: 30 tests in three files pass (`vitest run src/components/files/Preview.office.test.tsx src/components/files/ExportDialog.test.tsx src/lib/files/convert.test.ts`). Before the fixes the same three files gave 3 failed, 7 passed (the stale-wait test, the download-failure test, the outage-retry test). The earlier full run of 159 tests in six files passed before the review round and was not repeated. E2e rule: `node --test e2e/refusals.test.mjs` passes 5 of 5 (before the fix: it failed to load `refusals.mjs`). `tsc --noEmit` passes after the review round. `tsc --noEmit` passes. `check-keys`, `check-source` and `check-licences` pass. `npm run build` with `check-dist` passes: first load 324.1 KB of 330, largest language 21.8 KB of 25.
    - **Proofs (each broken on purpose, then restored).** The Go preview's failure answer made `404`: `TestFailedPreviewAnswersItsReason` and `TestConverterRefusalIsStickyAndItsTextIsKept` fail. The web failure reader made to answer `notConvertible` for every `415`: six tests fail. Not broken on purpose, so not proven: the touch CSS rule (the e2e measurement would catch its removal, but that was not run), and the watch's other states beyond those tests.
    - **End-to-end (`SELFCLOUD_E2E_ONLY=s4b`, the browser named by `SELFCLOUD_E2E_BROWSER`, server built after the web bundle).** The run starts a fake Collabora conversion interface on 127.0.0.1 over HTTPS (`web/e2e/convertFake.mjs`). The server trusts the fake's certificate through `SSL_CERT_FILE`, set for the server process only. The e2e configuration now has `office.enabled` on for every section, so a full run runs with office on; the other sections were not re-run that way, and the owner should know. The checks (37 PASS, `only s4b: passed`): the feature in `/info`; the Preview button; the frame's address; the PDF's status, type, `nosniff`, sandbox policy and magic bytes; the format menu; the ODT export downloaded as `letter.odt`; the converter asked for ODT from the DOCX; the failed export's dialog with no spinner and no English; a refused preview; an old binary file that is not convertible; the touch targets; no horizontal scroll at 375 px; the dark theme; Hebrew on the phone and the desktop. Screenshots: the folder named by `SELFCLOUD_S4B_SHOTS` (desktop and phone, light and dark, English and Hebrew, the card and the failed export), taken after the transitions settled. The fake's PDF is a fixed one-page file and its ODT a fixed ZIP header; no pixels are asserted.
    - **Security review of slice s.** Checked: every new answer runs the existing access checks (`nodeAccess`, the no-download rule at the request and at the download) and the blob check of decision 37; the export format is validated server-side against the fixed list before anything is queued; the failed answer carries a fixed message and a reason only, so no converter text reaches the page or a row; `/info` reveals one boolean; the served files keep their headers through the existing `writeConverted`; no new route and no new dependency; no string is built into SQL or a shell command (the fake's `openssl` call uses fixed arguments); the page shows no ID. Not checked: whether Collabora sandboxes macros, external links and embedded objects (decision 37, item 11); whether Chrome's PDF viewer honours the sandbox policy on the frame; a live Collabora against this build (the e2e uses the fake); a race of two conversions against the budget; the node ID is not checked for shape on the client before it goes into a path (it comes from the server); and the window between the second access check and the install write (decision 37, stated and not closed).
    - **Review round (the coordinator's five items).** (1) Returning to a left file shows the Preview button, not a stale wait (above). (2) A failed download shows an error with Download again, never success (above). (3) The e2e "conversion refused" entry is scoped: `refusedOnPurpose` in `web/e2e/refusals.mjs` accepts a 415 on a preview or export URL (including the bare export `POST`) only when the node is in the set the section filled. s4b adds `letter.docx` before its refused export, `broken.docx` before its refused preview and `old.doc` before its not-convertible preview; `run.mjs` passes the set into `s4bChecks`. Any other 415 on a preview or an export now fails the run. (5) An outage on the export `HEAD` has a Try again button (above). The e2e run for s4b was not repeated after these fixes: the unit tests cover them, but the browser has not seen the new dialog states.
    - **Choices the owner may want to confirm.** The export is in the viewer only. The formats offered are the family and PDF. A failed preview answers `415`, not the `404` that section 3 of the proposal named. The preview starts with a button, not on opening. A legacy binary format exports to PDF only.

60. **Pictures open in a lightbox** (2026-11-01, the owner's request with a picture of the viewer they mean: "the images should be shown like this", "I mean like how claude code display em"). Web interface only.
    - *The look.* The page stays behind, dimmed to 90% black in both themes. The picture sits in the middle with rounded corners, no larger than the window and never enlarged. The way out (X) and Download are at the top's end. The name is at the bottom's start on a wide window, and centred above the steps on a phone. The steps ("1 of 2" between two arrows) are in the bottom's middle, and only when there is more than one picture.
    - *The steps count pictures.* A text file between two pictures is not a step here. PDFs and text keep the full viewer and its steps through every file.
    - *Closing.* The X and Escape. A click outside the picture does nothing. The picture the owner showed closes on an outside click, and this project's rule is that a click outside a dialog never answers it (`check-source`). The rule stays until the owner says otherwise.
    - *Keys and touch.* The arrows step, mirrored in right to left. A swipe of at least 40 pixels steps, mirrored too.
    - *Two faults found in the browser, both also in the PDF and text viewer.* A step to the last file turned its own button off, and the focus fell off the button, so Escape and the arrows did nothing until the next click: the viewer now takes the focus in that case (`useKeysAfterStep`). And antd puts the focus on its own frame as a dialog opens, outside the stage that reads the keys, so the arrows did nothing until something was clicked: the viewer takes the focus once it has opened (`afterOpenChange`).
    - *Proofs.* Two pictures, one far larger than the window and one tall, at desktop and phone width, in English and Hebrew, in light and dark: the dimming, the corners, the picture in the window and centred, the count, the way out and the steps clear of the picture, 44 pixel buttons at rest and with the focus, and no overflow (`web/e2e/media.mjs`).

61. **A Play media button** (2026-11-01, the owner's request: "I want a button \"play media\" to play all the audio/video filels."). Web interface only; the player and its playlist are the ones of decisions 45 and 52.
    - *Where.* On the toolbar when nothing is selected and the listing holds audio or video, and in the menu of the empty space, for the folder on screen. In the right-click and More menus of one selected folder, for that folder. A phone shows the toolbar's button as a 44 pixel icon.
    - *What it plays.* The folder's audio and video files, in the listing's sort, from the first of them. The playlist reads further pages as it needs them, like the one a double click opens, so a large folder is not read at once.
    - *Subfolders are not played.* Only the files directly in the folder. This is a choice of the build, stated for the owner: walking a tree of folders costs one read per folder and has no natural order.
    - *A folder from a menu.* Its pages are read until one holds audio or video, so a folder whose first page has none still plays. A folder with none says so, and a failed read says that instead, never that the folder is empty. A move to another address, a change of sort, or opening anything else drops the answer. There is no limit on the pages read; a folder of very many files with no media is read until the person does one of those. A later page of any playlist shows the space's no-download rule as the first does, which it did not before this slice. The toolbar's button shows only for what the listing has read, so a folder with media only past its first page shows it after Load more.
    - *Proofs.* `pages/FilesPage.test.tsx` and the browser step in `web/e2e/media.mjs`: both entry points, the playlist's contents, nothing but media in it, the empty folder, the phone's button at 390 and 320 pixels in English and Hebrew.
62. **The drive's layout: the folder tree in the sidebar, drive-style tiles, slice d1** (2026-11-01, built to the owner's words: "The drive should look like this. This my file part is not good and take half of the screen. the subfolders should be under my file on the sidebar.", with a screenshot of Google Drive beside one of ours). The web interface only; the server is unchanged; no migration. Colours, the 4 px corners and the sidebar blue with its yellow pill are kept. Built as follows, and each point is a choice the owner may want to confirm.
    - *The tree.* The second column (the 240 px aside `folder-tree` and its PanelLeft toggle) is removed. The folders are one tree in the sidebar, above the menu: My files first (the person's own space, with its folders under a chevron), then the team spaces, each with its folders under its own chevron. The current folder carries the yellow pill, on the files pages only. Each row keeps the drop attributes, so a dragged item drops on any row (`elementFromPoint` in `useGestures` reads the sidebar too). A long tree scrolls in one region (`.shell-scroll`), so the rail toggle at the bottom stays in reach. The tree is a lazy chunk, loaded by the sidebar (`components/files/FolderTree.tsx`). The first load measured 324.0 KB of 330.0 (323.5 before the slice).
    - *The place crosses from the page to the sidebar* through a small store, `lib/files/treePlace.ts` (`userWritable`, cleared at a change of person): FilesPage writes the space, the folders on the way and the top folder a person was given, and the sidebar reads it. The store keeps the last place when the person leaves the files pages, so a person given only a folder below a space's root still sees that folder elsewhere; the marks show on the files pages only.
    - *refreshTree needs no store.* `refreshTree` (`lib/query.ts`) invalidates the `tree` reads on the one query client that the app shares, and the sidebar's branches are those reads, so a create, rename, move or delete reads the open branches again from the sidebar. The test "a refresh reads again the open folders that the change touched, and no other" proves it.
    - *The open state* is the person's own, under `selfcloud.tree.<id>`, as before. The stored `open` flag (the old column's show-or-hide) is no longer read; a state written before this slice still loads.
    - *Team rows* keep their options menu (Hide or Show, Space settings) and their hidden tag. They now sit in the tree, above the menu, where the team list was under it; this is a move of the teams' place in the sidebar. The "Team spaces" heading is removed (its key `nav.teams` is removed from the seven catalogues).
    - *The phone.* The drawer holds the tree (it is mounted only at phone width). A folder chosen in it closes the drawer. Admin navigation has no tree. The folded rail (88 px) shows no tree: My files is an icon in its menu.
    - *The listing* takes the whole width beside the sidebar: 1656 px at 1920 wide, 1016 px at 1280 (the sidebar is 264 px, the page padding 28 px each side).
    - *Tiles.* Folders come first, in their own band of one-line chips (40 px, 44 on a finger): folder icon, name cut with an ellipsis and in the title, a star and a ⋮ button. Then the files, in a band of their own, as cards: a header (type icon, name on one line, ⋮), then a preview of a fixed 120 px. The preview shows the thumbnail where there is one (the tiles' existing `Thumb`, which takes a height now and keeps 96 by default), else a 48 px type icon on a tinted area. The star is a button in the preview's top corner; the play mark stays on the preview's bottom corner (`KindMarks`). Every card is one height, whatever its name. Size no longer shows on a tile; the list view keeps it, and so does the Details panel.
    - *The column width is 260 px, not 200.* The owner asked for about five columns at 1920 and a minimum tile width of about 200 px. At 1920 the listing is 1600 px, so a minimum of 200 gives seven columns and five needs a minimum between 254 and 323 px. The grid uses `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, 260px), 1fr))` for both bands, so a 320 px window still fits one column. This is a deviation for the owner to confirm.
    - *Arrow keys.* Up and Down in the tile view move to the tile one row away on the screen, read from the tiles' places (`lib/files/grid.ts`, `nextRow`), not by a count of columns: the folder band and the file band are two grids, so a count of columns is wrong across them. `keyAction` is unchanged (its tests pin the deltas), and the page replaces the Up and Down delta in the tile view only. The list view moves by one row as before. There is no column count any more: `rowStep` (`lib/files/grid.ts`) gives the step, and a tile of the order that is not on the screen gives a step of 0, so the focus stays put rather than jump (the review of this slice removed the earlier column-count fallback).
    - *The gutter.* The tile view keeps 12 px of padding inside its listing, the place a rubber band starts from (the w2 check "a band from the tile grid's padding selects tiles").
    - *What the tiles keep.* Click, Ctrl and Shift selection; a checkbox on a finger; the rubber band; a double click plays or opens (`rowAttrs`); the right-click menu, and the ⋮ button opens the same menu at the button; the drag; the arrow keys; touch targets of 44 px on a finger at rest, on hover and on focus (sizes set inline, so a hover does not change them).

The other choice, lifting the drawer state into the viewer, was not taken: the state stays in `MediaPlaylist`, and the slot is one prop. The empty row above the screen is gone. The drawer is a plain element with a CSS transform, inside the screen; antd's Drawer was not used, because it adds its own mask and portal, and the brief asked for no mask.

It closes by its toggle, by its X, and by Escape. Escape closes the drawer first and the viewer on the next press: a window capture listener stops the event before the viewer sees it. In order: (1) the file's embedded art; (2) an image named `cover`, `folder`, `front` or `album` (case-insensitive, without its extension); (3) an image whose name equals the album tag, equals the folder's name, or is contained in the folder's name; (4) the folder's only image, when the whole folder was read; (5) two or more images and no match: no cover. A large folder whose first page has no match shows no folder cover; the rule reads the first page only. The listing (second review round, fix 4): up to 5 pages of 50 entries (250 in all) in the server's default order, following `next_cursor` (`readFolder`, `PAGES_MAX`), and the walk stops at once when an image named `cover` is found, since no later entry can beat it. The server's default order is by name key, the same on every page (`children_sort.go`). A good listing is kept for 5 minutes (`LISTING_TTL_MS`), so a picture uploaded later appears; a failed read is not kept, so the next track asks again. So the rule is one listing per folder per 5 minutes, not one read per folder. A folder over 250 entries with no match gets no folder cover, and step (4) needs the whole folder read. The upload tray was the largest part that most visitors never need: its antd card, with antd's tabs and their styles, sat in the first load for every visitor, though most never upload.
