The first load is now 313.0 KB over 29 files, 15.0 KB less, and the budget stays at 330 KB. Measured again on the base it landed on, with decisions 60 and 61: 329.7 KB over 31 files before, 314.9 KB after.

65. **The installable web app, part 1: install, fast start and the offline page, slice pwa1** (2026-11-02, owner: "Please add a slice for pwa". Approved as part 1 (this decision) and part 2 (the share target, slice pwa2, later). Offline files and push notifications stay out.)
    - *What was built.* `GET /manifest.webmanifest` is built per request from `ui.brand`: the name, a short name of at most twelve characters, the accent as `theme_color`, the light page colour `#EDF0F6` as `background_color`, `start_url` `/files`, `display` `standalone`, `scope` and `id` `/`. Four icons sit under `/brand/`, which is reserved for the server's own files: `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `icon-512-maskable.png` (the glyph inside the central circle of radius 40% of the size) and `apple-touch-icon.png` (180 pixels). The server draws them (`internal/web/pwa.go`, `pwa_glyph.go`) from the accent and an analytic glyph: three circles and a rounded rectangle, anti-aliased by a 4 by 4 sample grid per pixel, with no bitmap. On a plain icon the glyph is 60% of the width. Each icon's ETag is a hash of the accent, the glyph's shapes, the icon's path and its size, so a repeat request gets 304. `/sw.js` is the service worker (`web/public/sw.js`, a classic script at the root, served `no-cache`). The Vite build writes a build identifier into it, a hash of the built file names, the offline files and the worker's own source, so each build has its own cache, and a change to the offline page reaches installed workers. The worker keeps the cache of the previous build, and removes the others on activate. The sign-in page links the manifest and the apple icon, and gives the browser's bar a light and a dark theme colour. The light colour follows the accent when the brand is known (`brand.ts`); the dark colour is `#071531`. The policy adds `manifest-src 'self'` and `worker-src 'self'` and nothing wider.
    - *The worker's rules.* It caches a same-origin 200 `basic` GET of a file under `/assets/`, cache first, and only when the answer was not redirected, came from the path asked for, has one of the build's media types, and has no query string and no `Range` header. A path with a percent sign, a backslash, a double slash or a dot segment is never stored, and the server answers such a path with 404, not a redirect. It answers the offline page's own four files (`/offline.html`, `/offline.css`, `/offline.js`, `/favicon.svg`) from its cache, and fetches them at install and again at sign-in. A navigation goes to the network first, and the offline page is answered only for a document navigation outside `/api`, `/wopi`, `/s`, `/brand` and the manifest, and only when the network fails; a navigation's own answer is never stored. Nothing else is stored: no API answer, no office endpoint, no share page, no brand file, no signed link, no range answer, no answer from another origin. The unit tests (`web/src/lib/pwa/sw.test.ts`) run the worker in a stub of its scope and prove each refusal.
    - *Sign-out and sign-in.* Sign-out deletes every cache whose name starts with `selfcloud-`, then writes a marker into `selfcloud-state`. While the marker is there the worker stores no app file, so a visit to the sign-in page after sign-out leaves none behind. Sign-in lifts the marker (`setSignedIn` and the page's boot, `lib/pwa/cacheState.ts`), and asks the worker to fetch the offline page again only when the marker was there or the page is missing from the cache. Every message to the worker carries a sequence number, and the worker ignores one older than the newest of its kind, so a late sign-out cannot write the marker back after a sign-in. No user content is cached at any time, so the app's own files are the only thing a shared computer can keep, and sign-out removes them.
    - *The update.* A new worker that waits behind the one in control is offered: "A new version is ready", with Reload. The offer shows only while the tab is idle: no file plays (the playback's media is playing and not ended) and no upload is queued, uploading, paused, waiting, in conflict or waiting for a name. The offer sits at the inline end of the content area, in both directions, and does not overlap the sidebar (measured in English and Hebrew). Reload first asks the other tabs of the browser over a `BroadcastChannel` whether any is busy; if one is, the offer says it is waiting for other tabs and the update is not applied. Otherwise the waiting worker takes over, and each tab reloads once it is idle, through one `controllerchange` listener per page. Each open tab checks for a new worker when it becomes visible and every hour. A closed offer stays closed for that worker.
    - *Install.* The account menu offers "Install app" only after the browser fired `beforeinstallprompt`, and only once per offer. On an iPhone or an iPad outside standalone mode it offers "Add to Home Screen", which opens three steps in a dialog that cannot be closed by a click outside it. The entries are not shown to a person who is viewing as another person, nor in the installed app.
    - *What was not done.* Offline files (feature parity: later, with its own design for storage limits, encryption at rest and the no-download rule). Push notifications (Web Push goes through Google's, Apple's or Mozilla's servers, against "depends on no other system"). The share target (part 2). A custom logo as the app icon: the icons are the accent with the glyph, for every installation.
    - *Choices the owner may want to confirm.* (a) The icons are drawn from the accent and a built-in glyph, not from `ui.brand.logo_file`. (b) The offline page's words are in `offline.js`, in seven languages, because the worker cannot load the catalogues; its Hebrew and Arabic words are machine drafts, to be read by a speaker, as are the Hebrew and Arabic words added to the catalogues for this slice. (c) The offline page takes the brand name from the server, filled in when the page is served, so the cached copy carries it. (d) The browser's bar takes the accent in the light theme and a fixed dark colour in the dark theme. (e) The marker cache `selfcloud-state` stays after sign-out, holding one entry and no app file. 67. **Sizes and names read right in Hebrew and Arabic, slice b1** (2026-11-02, a display fault found in the d2 screenshots: the sidebar's storage line drew "MB 3.1" for "3.1 MB" inside a Hebrew sentence, and the size cells of the listing did the same).
    - *The fault.* A size is digits and a Latin unit ("MB"). Inside a right-to-left paragraph the bidi rules order them the wrong way, so the unit lands before the digits. A Latin name or number in a Hebrew or Arabic sentence can move the same way, with its neighbours (`files.newFolder.created`, "נוצרה התיקייה {name}."). Arabic's "3.1 م.ب" was already right and stays right.
    - *The fix.* `isolate` (`web/src/lib/i18n.ts`) wraps a value in FIRST STRONG ISOLATE (U+2068) and POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE (U+2069) when the interface language is right to left (he, ar). The isolate takes its direction from its own first strong letter, so "3.1 MB" keeps its order in Hebrew and "3.1 م.ب" keeps its order in Arabic. Two places use it, once each: `formatBytes` (`web/src/lib/files/format.ts`) wraps the size it returns, which covers its roughly 25 call sites and `formatRate`; and the formatter of `t()` and `tp()` (`formatValue`) wraps every placeholder value and the count. A left-to-right language gets the text unchanged, byte for byte. A value that is already isolated (a size passed to `t()`) gets a second isolate, which is harmless.
    - *Where it applies.* Only the right-to-left languages. No key, no wording and no server change.
    - *Checks that read through the isolates.* `format.test.ts`: the byte unit in full now expects the marks in he and ar. `playlists.plural.test.ts` (the Hebrew and Arabic count of a saved playlist), `e2e/x4.mjs` (the one-file count), `e2e/media.mjs` (the picture viewer's count) and `e2e/adminAccess.mjs` (the button labels and the text wait) strip U+2066 to U+2069 before they compare, so they check the same words as before.
    - *Tests, each run both ways.* Unit, first run before the fix: `format.test.ts` and `i18n.test.ts`, 3 tests failed, 19 passed; after: 22 of 22 pass. Browser (`web/e2e/d2.mjs`, `SELFCLOUD_E2E_ONLY=d2`): the sidebar's storage line, a file's size cell and the Storage page's figure are read in Hebrew at 1440 wide, and each draws its digits left of its unit; the English line does the same; the Arabic line keeps its right-to-left order (digits right of the unit). Mutation proofs: with the `formatBytes` isolate removed, the Hebrew size cell fails; with every isolate removed, the Hebrew sidebar line fails and draws "MB 3.1". The unstripped `x4`, `media` and `adminAccess` checks fail in Hebrew on the fixed build, and pass once they strip the marks.
    - *Sections run in Hebrew or Arabic, on the final build.* Each passes on its own (`SELFCLOUD_E2E_ONLY`): `d1`, `d2` (61 PASS), `media`, `pwa`, `q4`, `r7`, `r7b`, `s4b`, `w2`, `x2`, `x3`, `x4`, `x6`; `adminAccess` in he (24 of 24). `w1` fails only at its step 22, the known artifact of a run alone. `media` and `x4` failed before their check was stripped, and passed after.
    - *Budgets.* `npm run build` prints: entry 91.2 KB of 290.0; largest other chunk 119.8 KB of 120.0; largest language 22.6 KB of 25.0; first load 322.8 KB of 330.0 across 37 files. These are the figures decision 66 records for this base. The change adds one small function and no chunk.
    - *Not tested.* Arabic is checked on the sidebar line only, not on a listing or a Storage page. Hebrew and Arabic speakers have not read the rendered text. With only the `formatBytes` isolate removed, the sidebar's Hebrew line still passes, because the `t()` formatter isolates the size it is given; the cells and the Storage page get their isolate from `formatBytes` alone.
    - *Text on the yellow highlight (same slice, separate commit).* The sidebar's current item sits on the yellow pill (`SIDEBAR.active`), and its text is `SIDEBAR.onActive`, but two places drew white on it. The current folder's row and its arrow in the tree (`FolderTree.tsx`) were white, 1.52:1. The Storage block (`SidebarStorage.tsx`) forced the sidebar's text on its title (1.52:1) and its caption on the figures (1.21:1), and its track (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)`) was 2.33:1 on the yellow, with the yellow fill 2.33:1 on that track. The fix: the current tree row takes `onActive`. The Storage block takes a `selected` prop, which `Shell.tsx` sets on `/storage`. Selected, its title is `onActive` (10.55:1 on the default palette), its figures are `onActive` at 75% (5.88:1), and its track is `onActive` at 80% (6.73:1). The track has a 1px ring of `onActive` outside it, because an inset ring sat under the yellow fill, which is the row's own colour, and the fill was then invisible. With the ring the fill reads as an outlined block. The fill stays the accent yellow: 6.73:1 against the track. The warning fill is 5.34:1 and the danger fill 3.68:1 against it. Not selected, the block is as it was. Tests, each run before the fix and after. Unit: `FolderTree.test.tsx` (the current row and its arrow take `onActive`, a row that is not current keeps `text`) failed 2 of 16 before, and 16 pass after; `SidebarStorage.test.tsx` (selected title and figures, the track and its ring, not selected) failed 2 of 10 before and 10 pass after. Browser (`web/e2e/d2.mjs`, `SELFCLOUD_E2E_ONLY=d2`): nine contrast checks, computed from `getComputedStyle` with any alpha blended over the row, fail before the fix at the measured values above (name 1.52:1, arrow 1.52:1, Storage title 1.52:1, figures 1.21:1, track 2.33:1, fill 2.33:1, Arabic title 1.52:1 and figures 1.21:1, dark name 1.52:1), and pass after (70 PASS, 0 FAIL). The bar's edge check was added after the fix and was not run before it. The e2e install has a custom accent, so its on-active is black there (name 13.85:1, figures 8.20:1); the ratios above are the default palette. Sections on the final build: `d1` 46 PASS, `w2` 106 PASS. The screenshots are in the plans folder (`shots-c1`): the tree's selected folder in light and dark (the sidebar is the same blue in both modes), the Storage sidebar in English with its bar, and in Arabic, where the install had no limit, so there is no bar. Not done: the warning and danger bar colours on a selected row are not measured in the browser (the checks use 61%), and the bar's edge check is not checked before the fix. Found when reading the screenshots: a team's options button (the "···" at the end of its row, `Shell.tsx`) kept the sidebar's white on the current row. It now takes its row's ink (`color: inherit`), so it is `onActive` on the yellow and the sidebar's text elsewhere. Unit: `Shell.test.tsx` ("draws the current team's options button in the row's dark ink…") failed before the change (the button was `rgb(255, 255, 255)` on a row of `rgb(13, 33, 66)`) and passes after; the shell's 36 tests pass.
    - *Exactly one unit in Hebrew (found in the d3 screenshots, separate commit).* The Hebrew data writes exactly one of a short Latin unit unit-first: `Intl.NumberFormat('he', {style: 'unit', unit: 'megabyte'}).formatToParts(1)` gives "MB", a right-to-left mark, then "1". Inside the isolate that drew as "MB1". The fix: in a right-to-left language, when the unit comes before the number and is Latin letters, `formatBytes` puts the size back together as the number, a space and the unit, then isolates it. Every other size is as before; a left-to-right language skips the new step and gets the text unchanged. Hebrew's byte word ("1 בייט") and Arabic ("1 م.ب") already put the number first. Unit: `format.test.ts` ("writes one kB, MB or GB digits first in Hebrew") failed before the change (received "kB", the mark, "1") and passes after; the 45 test files under `lib/files` and `lib/i18n` pass (431 tests).

(10) A keyboard press then focus keeps the tooltip hidden after the press (the menu or the action has opened), until the pointer leaves or the focus does. Kept, and stated here.

    - *antd's colours as CSS variables.* 127 uses of `var(--ant-...)` in 40 files (the stylesheet's drop and tree-hover states, and inline styles such as the secondary text of the audit and management pages) painted nothing: antd's own CSS variables are off (the `ConfigProvider` sets no `cssVar`), and nothing else defined them, so secondary text took the main text colour and some split lines and hover bands were missing. `theme/antdVars.ts` names every string token of antd's computed theme as `--ant-<kebab-case>`, and `ThemeProvider` writes them on the root element for the mode in effect, as it already wrote `--link-colour`. Tests (`antdVars.test.tsx`): every `var(--ant-...)` the sources read is defined in both modes with the token's value, and the root element carries them in each mode (red before: the root had none). Choice: the variables are written from JavaScript, not antd's `cssVar` mode, which would change how antd writes all of its styles and the first-load size.

73. **The office editor in the web interface, WOPI rename, and the lock marks, slice l4** (2026-11-03, built to decision 72's l4 line and the coordinator's correction that this decision is 73, not 72; the owner's proposal for the editor, decision 37's Collabora host, and the lock rules of decisions 31 and 32). Scope as briefed: (1) WOPI RenameFile; (2) read-only and no-download properties in CheckFileInfo; (3) "Open in editor" and "Open in viewer" from the file menu and the preview, a full-window editor page at `/edit/{nod}`, the token posted into a hidden form whose target is a named iframe, and `postMessage` from the editor read only from its origin and its own window; (4) the lock mark in the list, "Being edited" with the holder's name in Details, and the manager's "End the editing session" with a confirmation; (5) the README's `office.*` settings and the CSP note. Blank documents and a live Collabora run were out of scope.

    - *WOPI RenameFile* (`internal/api/office_rename.go`, `internal/wopi/utf7.go`). The override `RENAME_FILE` reads `X-WOPI-RequestedName` as UTF-7 without the extension (RFC 2152; a non-ASCII byte, an empty shift and a lone surrogate are refused); the file keeps its extension. The answer is `{"Name": base}`. A name that is invalid or already taken in the folder is refused with 400 and `X-WOPI-InvalidFileNameError`; the server does not invent a name. A locked file takes the rename only from its holder (the lock ID must match; a missing ID on a locked file is 409 with `X-WOPI-Lock`). The write goes through `UpdateNodeHeld` with the holder's lock, so the store's lock rule (decision 32) applies, and it is audited as `node.rename`, which the webhook reports as `file.updated`. A folder or a shortcut is refused as not found after the token check.
    - *CheckFileInfo.* `SupportsRename: true` and `UserCanRename` equal `UserCanWrite`: a read-only token cannot rename, and the editor is not told it can when it cannot. The no-download rule (decision 31) binds viewers and commenters only, so an editor's token is unchanged.
    - *The 501 test.* `TestWOPIUnimplementedOverridesAnswer501` used `RENAME_FILE` as its example of an override not yet built. It now loops over `PUT_USER_INFO` and `PUT_RELATIVE`, which are still unbuilt.
    - *The editor page* (`web/src/pages/OfficeEditPage.tsx`, its own lazy chunk, 1.79 KB gzip). It asks `POST /api/v1/nodes/{nod}/office` for the editor's address and a token, builds a hidden form whose target is the named frame, and submits it once the form is in the page. The token is in the form's body only: not in the address, not in a log line, not in the page text. Messages are read only when their origin is the editor's origin and their source is the frame (`isTrustedEditorMessage`): `UI_Close` returns to the folder the file was opened from (`from`, else the file's folder), and `App_LoadingStatus` with `Document_Loaded` clears the wait. A failed open shows the reason by its status (404 not found, 403 forbidden, 400 and 413 and 415 not supported, 429 and 503 unavailable, otherwise failed), never the server's text.
    - *Why the page reads its node from the address.* The app mounts every page under one catch-all route (`lib/router.ts`), so `useParams` is empty there. The first e2e run showed "Page not found" for every open; the unit test had mounted the page under a `/edit/:nod` route, which production does not do. The page now reads `nod` from `location.pathname`, and its test mounts it under `*` as production does.
    - *Layer and direction.* The page is `position: fixed` with `zIndex: 1000`. Without the layer, the app's top bar drew over the page's own header and hid the back button and the "Editing" label (seen in the first l4 screenshots). Its back arrow uses the `icon-dir` class, so it points the right way in Hebrew and Arabic.
    - *Feature.* `/api/v1/info` lists `office_edit` (`featureEdit` in `health.go`) while office is on, next to `office_convert`. The file menu and the page both read it: with it off, no editor entry is offered and `/edit/` is the not-found page. The test `TestInfoNamesTheConversionWhileOfficeIsOn` now expects both names.
    - *Lock marks and Details.* `nodeJSON` gains `editing` and `editing_by`, both `omitempty`. `withEditing` reads the account's live locks once per listing (`LiveLocksOf`) and marks each item held by an editor. The holder's display name is shown only when the caller may see people's names (`peopleNamesSeen`); otherwise the mark says that someone is editing, without a name. Details shows "Being edited" with the name, and a manager (owner or manager role, not an editor) gets "End the editing session" behind a confirmation ("the editor's next save will be refused; unsaved changes in the editor may be lost"). It calls `POST /api/v1/nodes/{id}/unlock`; 404 and 409 are shown by name.
    - *Choices.* (a) The holder's name is hidden from people who cannot see names, as the people list does. (b) A clash on rename is refused, not renamed, so the editor's save stays exact. (c) `office_edit` is a separate feature name, so a client can tell the editor from the converter. (d) No Compose file and no image: the README gives the `office.*` settings, the CSP note, and the reachability rule, and nothing else.
    - *The rule the e2e found.* The run also showed that the editor's own frame posts its form after the page is up, so its record arrives later than the file name; the check now waits up to 15 seconds for the fake's record.

    - *Tests.* Go: `gofmt -l .` is empty; `go vet ./...` is clean. `go test -race` (with `-gcflags='modernc.org/...=-d=checkptr=0'`) passes for every package: `internal/api` passes alone in 2089 s (the full run's 30-minute limit was too short for it on this loaded machine, so it ran alone with a 60-minute limit), `internal/store` passes in 329 s, the rest passed in the full run. Three guard tests needed the new code declared: `TestNodeKindComparisonsAreReviewed` (`office_rename.go` has one reviewed comparison, a refusal that grants nothing), `TestEveryNodeWriteIsClassified` (`office_rename.go UpdateNodeHeld` is a holder write, `lockHolder`), and the info test above. Web unit: `vitest run` passes on the final code, 234 files and 2176 tests (`evidence-l4/42-vitest-final.txt`).
    - *Fail-then-pass.* RenameFile's UTF-7 vectors, its refusals, and the CheckFileInfo properties were written red first (`evidence-l4/01-utf7-red.txt`, `02-rename-red.txt`, `02b-rename-folder-red.txt`, `03-feature-lock-red.txt`); the web pieces red first (`05-web-red.txt`).
    - *Mutation proof, the postMessage origin rule.* `isTrustedEditorMessage` was changed from `origin === expected && source === frame` to `||`. Two tests failed (`evidence-l4/40-mutation-origin-broken.txt`: 2 failed, 12 passed). The file was restored; `cmp` showed it identical to the saved copy, and the two files pass again (14 tests, `41-mutation-origin-restored.txt`).
    - *Budgets* (`npm run build`, final). Entry 93.0 KB of 290.0; largest other chunk 119.8 KB of 120.0; largest language 23.1 KB of 25.0; first load 325.4 KB of 330.0 across 39 files (324.2 KB on main). The editor page is its own lazy chunk (`OfficeEditPage`, 1.79 KB gzip). The Go binary builds.
    - *E2E, by section, on the final build.* Section `l4` (`web/e2e/l4.mjs`, after `l1`) passes with 39 checks (`30-e2e-l4.txt`), and its run is part of the tail run below (`49-e2e-tail.txt`, 443 checks from `x2` to `pwa`, 0 failures). The screenshots were read: the menu entry, the editor page (back, name, "Editing"), the Hebrew phone layout, the list's lock mark, Details with "Being edited" and the end-session button, and the confirmation. `adminAccess.mjs` passes in English (24 checks) and Hebrew (24 checks) (`43-admin-en.txt`, `44-admin-he.txt`). Section `s4b` with `media` passes (412 checks, `39-e2e-s4b-media.txt`). Section `w2` passes on its rerun (107 checks, `48-e2e-w2-again.txt`).
    - *The full e2e run has not been green in one pass.* Intermittent failures, each not reproduced on the next run of its section: run 31 failed at the base suite's small upload (a row never appeared) and run 32 passed that step; run 37 had one player check fail ("Space plays and pauses the player, after a click on its bar too") and it passes in `media` alone and in `s4b` then `media`; `w2` failed twice with different checks (the Hebrew drag, `45-e2e-after-media.txt`; the band over a scrolled tile, `46-e2e-w2.txt`), passed on the rerun, and passed once on `main` (`47-main-w2.txt`). The machine's load average was up to 7.8 during these runs. Run 32 also stopped in `w1` with three checks: the long press passes alone (`33-e2e-w1.txt` has only check 22 failing), and check 22, "a failed English catalogue shows a retry", fails on `main` as well (a detached `main` worktree: `36-main-w1.txt`), so it is not this slice's. This check was not changed here.
    - *Not verified.* (a) A live Collabora run: its `postMessage` ids (`App_LoadingStatus`, `UI_Close`) and its RenameFile calls were checked only against the fake (`convertFake.mjs`), which signs WOPI proofs with its own key and locks the file itself. (b) Real proof keys from the live server's discovery. (c) The Hebrew and Arabic strings for the 21 new keys are machine drafts for a native speaker to check; the other five catalogues are drafts too.
    - *Known outside this slice.* `internal/web` builds the PWA icons per test server, which is slow under the race detector, and the `w1` retry check described above. Neither is changed here.
    - *Review fixes* (an independent review of the commit; each with a test that failed first or a mutation proof, the runs in `~/.local/share/selfcloud-plans/evidence-l4review/`). (a) *Ending the session.* After a break, an editor whose session still held the file's current content could take a new lock at once and save, so "the editor's next save will be refused" did not hold. The break now clears the served tag of the file's editing sessions (`ForgetServedContent`, in the break's transaction), and Lock and a save already refuse a session without one (decision 32), with the same 409 and no lock. A viewer's session is not changed. The sessions are not revoked: that would turn decision 32's 409 answers into 401. `TestBreakLockEndsTheEditingSession` (red: the LOCK answered 200). (b) *The token form.* The hidden form stayed in the page after it was posted, with the token in it; it is removed after the submit, which has already read it. `OfficeEditPage.test.tsx` (red: the input was still in the page); the `l4` browser section shows the editor still receives the post. (c) *The mark for visitors.* A share link's visitor was told that a file is being edited, without the name. The mark is now left out for a visitor, who cannot open the editor; `TestVisitorSeesNoEditingMark` (red). (d) *Tests that missed a broken rule.* UTF-7 padding (non-zero bits, a whole character beyond the padding, a shift with no unit, the empty name); a change of case only, which renames the file to its own name; the audit's `from` and `to`. Each was shown to fail on a mutation of the rule it guards.
    - *Not changed after the review.* (a) A lock is held by its ID, not by a person (decision 32): an editor whose token names the file may read the lock ID and rename or save with it, as for any co-editor. Binding a lock to a user would be a change of decision 32. (b) Names reserved on Windows (`CON`, `NUL` and the like) are taken, as everywhere in the drive; a rule for them would belong to `names.Clean` for every write, not to RenameFile. (c) The UTF-7 decoder refuses a name that holds U+FFFD itself, since it reads the decoder's replacement for a lone surrogate; such a name is not expected from an editor.
    - *Gate fix.* The full browser run's last check, "every request is same-origin", failed on the gate in three runs: the editor's page (`/browser/.../cool.html` on the fake editor's origin) counted as a request to another origin. The editor is another server by design, so `run.mjs` now lets such a request through only when it is under the editor's `/browser/` path and its `WOPISrc` names this server's `/wopi/files/` address. Any other foreign request still fails the check. The section runs alone skip this check, which is why it was not seen before the gate.

74. **Follow-ups of 2026-11-03, server part, slice fu2** (the owner: "Let's finish all the open follow ups too"). A read-only triage of the plans list found the server items below still open on main. Each needed no product decision, except where it says so. Each has a test that failed first, or, where the behaviour already held, a mutation proof: the code broken, the test shown to fail, the file restored and checked with `cmp`. The red and green runs are kept outside the repository, with the other plan evidence. No migration. Web interface for items 5 and 6 only. No setting changed, so the README is not touched.
    - *Rate limits by the /64 of an IPv6 client (item 1).* Every per-address limit now uses `addressKey`, the key the link guard (decision 23) uses: login, verify, forgot password and its mail charge, reset, change password, the sign-in link redeem, the link download (`links.serve`), and the share open and drop limits, which already did. `clientKey` had no callers left and is removed. Red before: in each of the six routes tested over HTTP (verify, login, forgot, reset, sign-in link, link download), a second address of the same /64 got a fresh budget. Tests: `TestPerAddressLimitsCountAnIPv6PrefixTogether` (the six routes) and `TestPerAddressLimitsKeepIPv4AddressesApart`. Not tested over HTTP: the change-password limit, which sits behind a session; it is the same one-line key change, and it is checked by the diff only. Known limit: clients behind one NAT64 gateway (`64:ff9b::/96`) share one /64 budget.
    - *Signed links under an impersonation (item 2).* One helper, `signedLinkLife`, gives the longest life a signed link made by the request may have: the least of what its delegated token, its visitor's credential and its impersonation have left. `handleCreateLink` uses it, and so do the thumbnail redirect and the preview and export redirect on the content origin, which minted links with the default TTL. The thumbnail and preview links now also stop at the token's and the visitor's end, not only the impersonation's: the same rule, the one helper, and a change the owner may want to confirm. Red before: a thumbnail link made with 3 minutes of impersonation left took the 5-minute default and outlived it (`TestThumbnailLinkLivesNoLongerThanTheImpersonation`). Not tested over HTTP: the preview and export redirect, which needs a converter; they use the same helper.
    - *Deleting an account ends its sign-ins-as (item 3).* Not moot, as first read. While the account is `deleting`, the sign-in-as's session row still existed, so an admin's Go back restored the admin, while the member's own requests were refused with a bare 401 (`authenticateSession` refuses a deleting account), and the web signs out on such a 401. Decision 41 ends a disabled user's sign-ins-as at once, so the deletion now does the same: `handleDeleteAccount` ends each sign-in-as of a member in its write, audits the end under the admin with reason `account_deleted`, and the audit entry goes with the account at the job (decision 48). Red before: the session was still live after the deletion began (`TestDeletingAnAccountEndsItsSignInsAs`). After the job the session row has gone by cascade (`sessions.user_id`), so Go back answers 401 with the session-ended message and clears both cookies, and the admin's own session is untouched; `TestGoBackAfterTheAccountIsDeletedAnswersCleanly` passed before this change as well and passes after it. An admin whose sign-in-as is ended by a deletion signs in again, as after a reset. The end is also written at installation level, as `account.delete` is: `account_id` NULL, the account's name as the target, reason `account_deleted`. The account's own rows go at the job, so this copy is the one that survives it; `TestDeletedAccountsSignInAsIsRecordedInstallationWide` runs the job and counts the row (red: 0 rows, green: 1). When a deletion ends a member's sign-in-as, the member page's next request gets 401 `unauthenticated` with no reason, and the web signs the browser out. That is the answer a disable gives, and the deletion already matched it: no code change was needed. `TestDeletionAndDisableAnswerTheMemberTheSameWay` pins the match.
    - *A mail is audited before it is sent (item 4).* The audit log is append-only, so one mail makes two rows and neither is changed later. `deliver` first writes a `verification.send` row with outcome `attempted`, and sends only after that write succeeds. If the write fails, nothing is sent and the answer says `sent: false`. After the send, a second `verification.send` row records the result: `ok`, or `failed` when the send failed. A mail that left therefore always has its attempted row before the send, and the result row says how it went. The forgot-password path already audited in its transaction and is unchanged. Red before: the row count at the send was 0 (`TestVerificationMailIsAuditedBeforeItIsSent`; evidence `review1-mail-red.txt`, green `review1-mail-green.txt`). The failing audit write is a SQL trigger in the test, with no hook in production code.
    - *Verify and reset ask before they switch (item 5).* The verify and reset routes answer `409 signed_in_as_other` when the browser holds a session of another user, with the same names as a sign-in link, before anything is written, so the link stays live for the second answer; `confirm: true` accepts the switch. A verify or reset that signs in now ends the browser's previous session, as a password sign-in and a sign-in link do (before, the old session row stayed live). The pages use the prompt SignInPage shows, moved to `components/SwitchPrompt.tsx`; the text is the sign-in link's, which reads for a link. No new text, so no catalogue changed. Tests: `TestVerifyAsksBeforeSwitching` and `TestResetAsksBeforeSwitching` (red: 200 where 409 is due), `switchPrompt.test.tsx` (two pages; the verify page's mutation makes it fail, and the file is restored with `cmp`).
    - *A folder made by parent ID (item 6).* `POST /folders/{fld}/directories` takes `{parent, name}` as well as `{path, parents}`; giving both forms, or `parents` with the parent form, is `invalid_request`. The parent is a directory of the folder in the URL, found by its node ID, with contributor needed, and the check is repeated in the write. A parent in the trash, or of another account, or in another folder than the URL's, is `not_found`; a file is refused; a name must be one path element. The web uses the parent form for a folder made inside a directory (`NewFolderDialog` and the files page's toolbar). **The web keeps the path form at a folder's root**, because the places the web holds do not carry the root's node ID, and the root cannot be renamed or moved, so the race cannot happen there. The owner may want the root on the parent form too. Tests: `TestMkdirByParentFollowsARename` (red: the parent form was an unknown field), `TestMkdirByParentRefusals`, `TestMkdirPathFormIsUnchanged`; web `mkdirIn.test.ts` and the dialog test (the mutations make each fail). The openapi document describes both forms.
    - *Missing tests (item 7), each with a mutation proof.* The audit entries that name a change: `user.update` with `quota_bytes` (mutation: the key renamed), `account.storage_policy` (the action renamed), `node.appearance` (the action renamed): `TestAuditEntriesNameQuotaPolicyAndAppearance`. A label value is kept while its node is in the trash, comes back with a restore, and goes with a purge: `TestLabelValuesSurviveTrashAndGoOnPurge` (mutations: the trash deletes the values; the purge keeps the row). The choice limit on PATCH: `TestLabelChoicesLimitHoldsOnPatch` (the limit lifted, which breaks POST too). `store.Colors` against the 0019 CHECK: `TestColorsMatchTheMigrationCheck` (one colour renamed). The global pending cap when ten or more accounts are each under their own: `TestGlobalPendingCapHoldsWhenEachAccountIsUnderItsOwn` (11 accounts, 100,000 pending rows, a twelfth account's mail not queued; the global check removed, and the test fails). All these behaviours held, so each test passed before its mutation was made.
    - *Decision 35, the zip job (item 8).* A zip reads each file from the blob its snapshot named. A file whose blob is purged after the snapshot and before its entry's turn cannot be read, so its entry fails and the whole zip fails with "a file's contents are missing"; the zip does not leave the file out. This is a divergence from decision 35's statement that a node deleted after the snapshot is still in the zip: that holds only while its blob exists. Test: `TestZipFailsWhenAFilesBlobIsPurgedBeforeItsEntry` (it holds as built; mutation: the missing blob skipped, and the test fails). Decision 35 carries the sentence.
    - *Browser checks changed (item 5).* `e2e/adminAccess.mjs` opens the emailed reset link and the admin's reset link in a browser still signed in as the admin, so the new prompt appears there. Both steps now accept the switch with the dialog's primary button (`acceptSwitchIfAsked`), since the step is the member's own link. The first full run stopped at the first of them, before the change; the rerun of `adminAccess` in `en` and `he` passed (48 checks, none failed). `run.mjs` passed (1133 checks) on the first run, which the switch does not touch.

The Go race tests pass for `internal/store` and `internal/api` (after the two guard counts were updated: `TestEveryNodeWriteIsClassified` and `TestNodeKindComparisonsAreReviewed`, each reviewed in its file).

Each is fixed in this slice, in plain words: (1) the mail audit writes an attempted row before the send and a result row after it (item 4 above); (2) the end of a sign-in-as that a deletion ends is also kept at installation level (item 3 above); (3) the token and visitor branches of `signedLinkLife` have tests in `link_life_test.go`, and each capped branch was removed in turn, its test failed (`review3-M-token-mutant.txt`, `review3-M-visitor-mutant.txt`), and the file was restored byte for byte; (4) the parent form refuses a viewer and a share-link visitor (`mkdir_refusals_test.go`), and with the contributor check lowered the viewer test fails (`review4-M-role-mutant.txt`); (5) this decision names no local path, and the rate-limit line above records the NAT64 known limit; (6) a deletion ends a member's sign-in-as the way a disable does (item 3 above; verified, no change).

75. **Keep me signed in, slice ks** (2026-11-03). The owner, on the sign-in page: "there is no "remember me"". Asked how it should work, the owner chose: "Box, off by default". Unticked, the session ends when the browser closes, and after 12 hours unused even when the browser restores its tabs. Ticked, the session lasts 30 days, as every session did before. The browser remembers the last choice. Web interface and API; one migration (`0043`); one new setting, `sessions.short_idle_timeout`.
    - *What changed.* The sign-in page has a box, "Keep me signed in", under the password field and above the button, unticked on a fresh browser. A session made with the box unticked has a cookie with no Max-Age and no Expires, so a browser that closes drops it, unless the browser restores its last session and keeps the cookie; the server then ends the session `sessions.short_idle_timeout` after its last use. An unticked session used at least every 12 hours still ends at `sessions.max_age` at the latest. The server ends such a session `sessions.short_idle_timeout` (unset, the shorter of 12 hours and `sessions.idle_timeout`) after its last use, and its absolute limit, `sessions.max_age`, still applies. A kept session is as before: its cookie lasts `sessions.max_age`, and it ends `sessions.idle_timeout` after its last use. `POST /api/v1/auth/login` takes `remember`. Left out, the session is kept, so API clients keep their behaviour; the web page always sends it. The session row records its kind in a new column, `sessions.short` (migration `0043`; existing rows are kept sessions). The browser keeps the box's last choice in `localStorage` under `selfcloud.keepSignedIn`; a storage that cannot be read or written leaves the box unticked for the page, and the choice still applies to that page.
    - *Which sessions take the box.* The password sign-in takes the box. A verification link and a password-reset link do not: the person chose nothing there, so their sessions are browser-session ones. A sign-in link that an application mints keeps today's lifetime: the application decides. A password change replaces the session and the new one keeps the old one's choice. A sign-in as (an installation admin's sign-in as a user, decision 41) keeps its one-hour limit, and takes the admin's choice of box: an unticked admin's sign-in as, and the admin's parked cookie that Go back restores, are browser-session cookies too.
    - *Why.* Every web session lasted 30 days, and a browser that the owner closed kept its sign-in. The owner's words are quoted above. The short limit is server-side, so a browser that restores its tabs does not keep a session nobody has used for 12 hours.
    - *Startup check.* `sessions.short_idle_timeout` is optional. Unset, the effective value is the shorter of 12 hours and `sessions.idle_timeout`; set, it must be more than 0 and not more than `sessions.idle_timeout`, and a negative value is refused. The effective value is one method, `SessionsConfig.ShortIdle`, which start-up and the session expiry both read. (Review fix 1 replaced the first version, which took 12 hours as a required setting and refused an installation whose idle timeout was under 12 hours.)

The red and green runs are in `~/.local/share/selfcloud-plans/evidence-ks/`. The browser section `ks` was written after the box, so it has no red run of its own.

76. **Web follow-ups of 2026-11-03, slice fu3a** (the owner: "Let's finish all the open follow ups too"). Each item of the brief was checked against the code first. Where it held, a mutation proof or a browser check is the record; where it did not, a test was written first and failed. The runs are in `~/.local/share/selfcloud-plans/evidence-fu3a/`. Web interface only, no migration, no server change.
    - *1. A request that hangs.* `api()` had no time limit, so a hung call kept a busy dialog open. `api()` now ends a call after `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, 60 seconds (`lib/api.ts`), covering the headers and the body. The value is 60 s because a call here is small JSON that the server answers in well under a second; a minute with no answer means the server or the network has stopped. Uploads and downloads do not use `api()` (`tus.ts`, `Preview.tsx`, `MediaDock.tsx` and the thumbnail and zip fetches have their own `fetch`), so they have no limit. A timeout is `timeout` with `details.write`: `error.timeout` ("may or may not have been saved") for a write, `error.timeoutRead` for a read. A busy dialog can be cancelled: `lib/flight.ts` holds the request the dialog has out, and Cancel or Escape aborts it and closes the dialog. The page says "Cancelled. The change may or may not have been saved; check the list before you try again" (`common.cancelledMaybe`) on dialogs that make a write. Covered: Invite (`InviteDialog.tsx`), the group and team-space name dialog (`NameDialog.tsx`, called from `GroupsPage.tsx` and `SpacesPage.tsx`), the removal confirmation (`RemoveDialog.tsx`, through a new `oncancel` on `Confirm.tsx`), New key (`NewKey.tsx`), New tenant (`NewTenant.tsx`), the admin form and the admin removal (`AdminsPage.tsx`), and the label dialog (`LabelDialog.tsx`, `LabelsPage.tsx`). The write functions in `lib/manage/api.ts` and `lib/labels/api.ts` take the signal. Two old tests asserted that Cancel does nothing while busy (`NewTenant.test.tsx`, `TenantKeys.test.tsx`); they now assert the new behaviour, which the brief asks for.

A cancel that comes after the server has already saved the write leaves the page with no record of it, which is why the message says the change may or may not have been saved.

        1. *A cancel during the body read.* A cancel while the answer's body was still arriving resolved as success with no body, so a caller could read fields that were not there. The body read now ends at a timeout or a cancel as a failure (`lib/api.ts`). Test: `api.timeout.test.ts`, "a cancel during the body read ends as cancelled" (red: the call hung, `fu3a-r1-red-body-cancel.txt`).
        2. *A save whose re-read failed.* The page reported a network error with the old value, though the server had kept the save. The save is now reported as saved, and a failed re-read is a softer warning that the value shown is the saved one (`PersonDialog.tsx`). The dialog's own warning is hidden while that note shows, so the message is not said twice. Test: `PersonDialog.test.tsx`, "a kept limit whose re-read fails is reported as saved" (red: no saved notice, `fu3a-r6-red-reread-note.txt`).
        3. *A write's timeout read as the network.* Five places mapped any status 0 to the network text: the share dialog, general access, the request-files dialog, the drop page, and the request-access outcome. One helper, `statusZeroKey` (`lib/errors.ts`), now gives the timeout text for a write that timed out, the "did not answer" text for a read, and the network text otherwise. A timed-out request is a new outcome, `unsure`, so the request-access page does not say it failed. Tests: `errors.statusZero.test.ts` and `sharing.test.ts` (red: `fu3a-r3-red-status-zero.txt`).
        4. *Lock keys.* Some keys were shared by two actions or two parents: the member key had no group, and the add and the delete of a group shared one key, and the open and delete of a space shared one. Each key now names its kind and parent (`lib/manage/locks.ts`, used by the people, spaces, groups and links pages). Test: `locks.test.ts`, which checks two actions on one row, one user in two groups, and one action on two rows (red: the module did not exist, `fu3a-r7-red-lock-keys.txt`). The test is at the key level; the page-level cases are not driven in a browser.
        5. *The session clear.* The clear now runs with the "store the previous value in state" pattern (`components/admin/hooks.ts`), so a dropped render drops the state and the clear together. The committed-render test is kept and passes.
        6. *The default limit.* A call with no time given is now checked on fake timers: it is cut at 60 s and not before. Mutation proof: with the default changed to zero, the test fails (`fu3a-r5-mutation-default-limit.txt`); the file was restored and `cmp` confirmed it byte for byte.
        7. *The upload commit.* A commit of a large file assembles the pieces on the server and can take minutes; under the minute limit it would have marked the upload failed while the server might still finish it. The commit has its own limit of ten minutes (`COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `lib/files/api.ts`). Ten minutes is a judgement: long enough for a large file's assembly, short enough that a stuck commit is reported. Test: `api.commit.test.ts` (red: `fu3a-r2-red-commit-and-default.txt`).
        8. *The Cancel check in the browser section.* The section said Cancel sent nothing; it checks only that the dialog closes. The words now say that (`web/e2e/fu3a.mjs`).
        9. *A cancelled write refreshes the lists.* After a cancelled write, the dialog now reads the lists again, so a write that did happen shows. Invite, name, removal, new key, new tenant, labels, and the admin form and removal all do it. Tests: the refresh is asserted in the invite, name and removal cancel tests (red: `fu3a-r8-red-refresh-invite-locks.txt`); the other dialogs share the same code path and are not asserted one by one.
    - *Checks after the review fixes.* `tsc`, `check-source`, `check-licences`, `check-keys`: pass. Full vitest: 253 files, 2,261 tests passed (`fu3a-r10-green-vitest-full.txt`). Build: entry 91.1 of 290 KB, largest other chunk 119.8 of 120, largest language 23.3 of 25, first load 323.8 of 330 (`fu3a-r11-build.txt`). E2E: `fu3a` 24 PASS, 0 FAIL (`fu3a-r12-e2e-fu3a.txt`); `adminAccess` en 24 PASS and he 24 PASS (`fu3a-r12-e2e-adminAccess-*.txt`).

Fix: the list is one table with its header (`components/files/Listing.tsx`: no `sticky` prop, `tableLayout="fixed"`), and the header cells are pinned with CSS at `--sc-list-top`, set from the toolbar's place (`index.css`, `.files-list .ant-table-thead > tr > th`). The header and the rows share their columns in every frame by construction. Tests: `Listing.test.tsx`, "the list's column header (fu3b, item 1)" (two tests; red before, `evidence-fu3b/red-item1-single-table-unit.txt`, green after, `green-item1-single-table-unit.txt`); `components/files/listHeader.test.ts` (the pin rule, red when the rule is removed, `red-item1-css-unit.txt`). Fix: the place query keeps the previous place (`placeholderData: keepPreviousData`). While the next place or listing is read, the last listing stays on screen inside a wrapper with `aria-busy="true"` and `inert`, and the toolbar is inert; the shortcuts and drag and drop do nothing while the place is pending. A failed read still shows its error, and the first folder of the page still shows the loading notice. The check read the buttons during that zoom. A read early in the zoom gives about 9 px (the "9 px at rest" flake of item 8 was this). A read late in the zoom gives 43 px, as the gate logged. It also means no box around a button in an antd motion (a class such as `ant-zoom-appear`), no animation on or around a button that has not finished, and no scaled box around it.

Made to always pass, it failed four runs of four with "rest 9,9" (`lead-s4b-mutant-nosettle-1..4.log`, restored byte for byte, checked with cmp).
            - The gate (fu3stackb) still read 9 px twice. antd attaches the zoom paused at its first frame, so the second try counted any animation not finished, and any scaled box. That still failed two runs of four here, with "rest 9,9" (`lead-s4b-settle2-1..4.log`). A diagnostic at the read (`lead-s4b-diag9-*.log`) showed why. The buttons were laid out at 44 px, the dialog had `ant-zoom-appear ant-zoom-appear-active` and a scale of 0.2, and its zoom was running. antd's motion begins with a step that has no transform and no animation: the wait had passed in that step, and the zoom started after it.
            - The third try adds the motion class. antd puts the class on the dialog from its first drawn frame and removes it when the zoom has ended. With it, s4b passed six runs of six, 12 measures, every one 44 px (`lead-s4b-motion-1..6.log`). The second try's failures are the red for this check: the same wait without the motion class.
            - The §14 rows are left alone until the gate passes.

    - *The cause.* The folder tree's rows were 32 px on a mouse and 44 px on a finger, with no inline margin and the radius `borderRadiusSM`. The sidebar's menu items were antd's default: 40 px (`controlHeightLG`) on a mouse and on a finger, a 4 px inline margin (`marginXXS`) and the radius `RADIUS`. The menu's icon column also came from antd's inline indent (24 px, a Menu prop), which the stylesheet's `--sc-icon-col` could not change, because antd sets the indent as an inline style. On a finger the menu's rows were 40 px, not the 44 px every sidebar row should be.

The folder tree's rows in the sidebar take them (`components/files/FolderTree.tsx`, `side` only); the sidebar's Menu takes the same values through its ConfigProvider, and its `inlineIndent` (`components/Shell.tsx`). A tree row has no gap between its arrow and its icon and no start padding at the top level, so its icon sits where the menu's icon sits: 28 px from the sidebar's content edge on a mouse, 48 px on a finger. The outside tree (the move and copy picker and the rest, with `side` off) keeps its own rows.

83. **Comment webhook events, slice r6** (2026-11-05, the owner's answer to the design: "Yes, IDs only"). Decision 39 left the comment webhook (r6) to be built; this is it. Built: five events, `comment.created` (a top-level comment or a reply), `comment.updated` (an edit), `comment.deleted`, `comment.resolved` and `comment.reopened`, in `webhook.Events`, which the endpoint routes validate against; migration 0044 rebuilds the two event tables so their CHECK accepts the five names. Each route writes its event in its own write transaction, with `tx.EmitEvent` after the change and before the audit entry, so a refused or failed action queues nothing. The payload is `store.CommentEvent` (`webhook.Comment`), with `id` (the comment), `reply_to_id` (null for a top-level comment), `node_id`, `folder_id`, `author_id`, `mentions`, plus `actor_id` only when someone other than the author made the change, and `tombstone` on `comment.deleted` only. The names follow the other payloads (`id`, `folder_id`, `parent_id`, `upload_id`). The comment's own ID is `id`, as the other payloads give their subject's ID, so the node that holds the comment is `node_id`, not `id`. The example:

```json
{"id":"evt_…","type":"comment.created","time":"2026-11-05T16:50:34.664Z",
 "account":{"id":"acc_…","external_id":null},
 "data":{"id":"cmt_…","reply_to_id":null,"node_id":"nod_…","folder_id":"fld_…",
         "author_id":"usr_…","mentions":0}}
```
    - *No text, ever.* The payload holds IDs and a count. Neither the body, an author's or a mentioned person's name, nor an address is in it, as decision 43 keeps comment text out of mail. An event outlives the comment in the outbox and reaches every endpoint the account subscribed, and the account's external systems are not the people the comment was for. The receiver reads the text through the API, where the reader's rights are checked.
    - *The switch.* The routes check the account's comment switch inside the write, as they did before, so with the switch off no change is made and no event is written. The test proves it.
    - *Interpretations.* `author_id` is null once the author's user is deleted, as the comment is then shown as a former member; a manager who resolves or deletes such a comment gets `actor_id` set and `author_id` null, tested through the route. Repeat resolve is pinned: resolving a comment that is already resolved answers 200 and queues a second `comment.resolved`, as the audit records a second entry (`TestResolvingAResolvedCommentQueuesAgain`). A refused action queues nothing, and so does an action answered `not_found`: an unknown comment, a tombstone (edit, resolve, or a second delete) and a comment on a shortcut (`TestNotFoundRefusalsQueueNothing`). A viewer's refused delete and refused resolve queue nothing (`TestViewerRefusedDeleteAndResolveQueueNothing`). `mentions` is the number of people the request named (the count the audit records); an edit, a delete, a resolve and a reopen name no one, so they carry 0. A resolve of a comment that is already resolved, and a reopen of one that is open, still write their event, as the audit does for them. The event type is `comment.resolved` or `comment.reopened` by the value sent.
    - *Migration.* 0044 rebuilds `webhook_endpoint_events` and `webhook_events` with the five names added, keeping their rows, indexes and the outbox ID counter, as 0021 did. It runs with foreign keys off, so `TestRebuildMigrationIsMarkedForeignKeysOff` now lists 44 as well. `TestMigration0044KeepsRowsAndAcceptsCommentEvents` (`internal/store/migration_0044_test.go`) runs the runner's `applyMigrations` up to 43 on an empty database, since `migrate` has no stop-at-version option, then seeds an account, an endpoint with two subscriptions, an event and its delivery (and one deleted row, so the counter is ahead of the largest ID). After 44 alone it checks the row counts of the five webhook tables, that the delivery still names its event, that `sqlite_sequence` carried over, that `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` is clean, that the five comment names are accepted in both tables, and that an unknown name is still refused.
    - *Tests.* `internal/api/comments_events_test.go`: the payload's keys and IDs for a top-level comment, a reply, a mention (`mentions` 1), an edit, a removed comment and a tombstone, a manager's delete (with `actor_id`), a resolve and a reopen by someone else, the refused actions and the switch-off each write nothing, a subscriber to `comment.created` gets one delivery and a `file.created` subscriber gets none, and the five names are accepted while an unknown name is refused. `internal/webhook/comment_payload_test.go`: the five names are listed and sorted, and the key set of the two payload shapes. `internal/store/comment_event_test.go`: `actor_id` only for another person, a null `author_id` after a user's deletion, `reply_to_id` and `mentions`. Every outbox test has a subscriber, since the outbox holds only events some endpoint takes: a test without one passes whether or not the route emits. The delete handler takes one timestamp for the tombstone and the event.
    - *The first red run was not a valid red.* The first run of the event tests had no subscriber, so the outbox was empty whatever the routes did. The subscriber was added to each test (`subscribeComments`) before the code was written. The red evidence is therefore the mutation proofs below.
    - *Mutation proofs, each restored with an Edit and checked with `cmp` against a copy made before the change.* (1) The resolve and reopen names swapped: `TestResolveThenReopenQueueTwoEvents` fails ("events written = [comment.reopened], want exactly [comment.resolved]"). (2) The actor named for the author's own change too (`actor != c.AuthorID` removed): `TestCommentCreatedPayloadIsIDsOnly` fails on the key set (`actor_id` present), and `TestCommentEventNamesTheActorOnlyWhenNotTheAuthor` fails. (3) The comment's body put in the payload as `text`: `TestCommentCreatedPayloadIsIDsOnly` and `TestCommentEditedQueuesUpdated` fail on the key set. (4) An event written in a separate transaction before the permission and switch checks of create: `TestRefusedCommentActionsQueueNothing` ("refused actions wrote 2 events") and `TestCommentsSwitchOffQueuesNothing` ("comments switched off wrote 1 events") fail. Each file was restored byte for byte. The second round, with the new tests: (5) migration 0044 without `comment.reopened` in the outbox's CHECK: `TestMigration0044KeepsRowsAndAcceptsCommentEvents` fails ("constraint failed: CHECK constraint failed"). This caught a gap in the first version of that test, which inserted only `comment.created` into the outbox; the test now inserts all five. (6) migration 0044 with the row copy removed: the test fails, since the migration's own `foreign_key_check` refuses the dangling delivery and the migration is rolled back. (7) the repeat resolve skipped when already resolved: `TestResolvingAResolvedCommentQueuesAgain` fails ("events written = [], want exactly [comment.resolved]"). (8) `author_id` always set, even when the author's user is gone: `TestDeletedAuthorResolvedByManagerThroughTheRoute` fails. (9) an event written before the create checks: `TestNotFoundRefusalsQueueNothing` fails ("wrote 1 events"). (10) an event written before the resolve checks: `TestViewerRefusedDeleteAndResolveQueueNothing` fails. (11) the comment's `id` tag renamed to `comment`: `TestCommentPayloadKeys` fails on the key set. The tests that pass on the existing code are guards, and their proofs are (7) to (10). The delete handler's single timestamp has no mutation proof: it is a structural change, checked by reading the diff.
    - *Not proved.* A failure after an emit inside one transaction rolling back the event: the routes have no step after the emit that can be made to fail from a test, so this rests on the transaction, the same rule as the file events (decision 27), not on a test of the comment routes.
    - *Gate.* The full `./internal/...` run passed (21 packages, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean) before the mutation proofs; the sources were restored byte for byte afterwards. The race run is the gate's.
84. **Fixes from the security review of 2026-11-05 (slice sec1)** (2026-11-05; 82 is pwa2, 83 is r6). Three read-only reviewers read main at 87fd326 (findings in the review's notes, not in this repository). No critical or high finding. The owner chose "1-11 plus admin hardening". Not taken: TOTP, a consent step for ownership transfer, node-count caps. Each finding, its fix, its test, and what was decided against:

    - *1. Sign-in and reset lockout.* The per-email bucket was keyed on the email alone and charged before the password check, so a few tries from one address kept the user refused from anywhere. Fix: the per-email buckets (`login.email`, `forgot.email`) are keyed on email and client address (`emailAddressKey`). Online guessing from many addresses is bounded by `login.failed`, 30 failed sign-ins an hour per email. Device cookie (the OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet's device-cookie approach, "Slow Down Online Guessing Attacks with Device Cookies"): a successful sign-in or password reset sets `selfcloud_device` (`__Host-` over https), `userID.nonce.issued.expiry.mac` (issued in milliseconds, covered by the MAC; review F9 below), HMAC-SHA256 under an HKDF key with its own label from the links signing key, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax. A sign-in with a valid cookie for that email's user skips `login.failed` and spends `login.device` (10 an hour per cookie, given back on a match); a spent cookie stops being trusted. Without a trusted device the cap applies, with one answer for known and unknown emails, pointing at Forgot password or a device used before. Reset is not refused by the cap and sets a cookie. Decision 90 changes the cookie's scope: it names one user, its budget covers that user's password only, and the other users with the email stay under the cap. Tests: `TestGuessingFromOneAddressDoesNotLockOutTheUserElsewhere`, `TestGuessingOneEmailFromManyAddressesIsBounded`, `TestDeviceCookieSignsInWhileTheCapIsSpent`, `TestNoDeviceCookieIsRefusedWhileTheCapIsSpent`, `TestForgedOtherUsersAndExpiredDeviceCookiesAreNotTrusted`, `TestDeviceCookieThatFailsItsOwnBudgetStopsBeingTrusted`, `TestResetWorksWhileTheCapIsSpentAndSetsADeviceCookie`. *Decided against:* a per-email cap that refuses before the check with no device exception, because a correct password from the user's own address would be refused while an attacker holds the cap. *Residual, stated plainly:* a user with no device cookie who signs in from a new device is refused for up to an hour while the cap is spent by an attacker; Forgot password still works. The mail budget `mail.forgot.target` stays keyed on the recipient by design (anti-spam), so an attacker can use up a victim's reset mail for the hour; the 202 answer is the same either way. Commits 9dee205, 91e6c7b, c70d663.
    - *2. One-request writes and the disk.* `POST /folders/{fld}/files`, `PUT /nodes/{nod}/content` and WOPI PutFile wrote the body before any disk check. Fix: `writeBlob` checks the disk (the tus rule, `diskUsable` and `checkDisk`, with the body as the bytes to hold) and the quota on the declared length before reading a byte (`checkOneRequestRoom`); a body with no Content-Length is counted as the cap, since the blob writer stops at the cap, so the write cannot pass what was checked. Limiter `write.one_request`, 300 a minute per caller (60 refused ordinary bulk creation in the test suite). *Decided against:* 411 for unsized bodies, because the clients may send chunked bodies and the cap-count is safe without refusing them. Tests: `TestOneRequestWriteIsRefusedWhenTheDiskIsBelowMinFree`, `TestOneRequestWriteIsRefusedByQuotaBeforeItIsWritten` (counts body reads; red under a mutation that skips the pre-check), `TestOneRequestWritesAreRateLimitedPerCaller`, `TestChunkedWriteIsCheckedAgainstTheCap`, `TestChunkedWriteIsCheckedAgainstTheQuota`. Commits c64c11b, dc4260f.
    - *3. Deadlines.* `decodeJSON` sets a read deadline (`jsonBodyTimeout`, 15 s). A download's deadline follows its progress, and the kernel's sendfile path is kept (CLAUDE.md requirement 6). The response is `progressWriter` (`internal/api/download_progress.go`), which implements `ReadFrom` and `Unwrap`. A copy from the file is sent in segments of `downloadSegmentBytes` (8 MiB, a constant, not a setting). Before each segment the write deadline is set to now plus `download.timeout` plus the segment over `download.min_rate`, and the segment goes through the response's own `ReadFrom` as a limited reader over the file, which is the sendfile path. A reader that stops is cut off within about one segment's time. A reader that keeps up is never cut off, and there is no absolute cap on the whole download: a client that loses the connection resumes with a `Range` request, as it does for any dropped connection. Other copies (the parts of a multipart range, which come through a pipe, and any copy of unknown length) set a deadline before each chunk instead. A multipart range is therefore not sent by sendfile; that is net/http's own behaviour for multipart responses and is unchanged. Tests in `sec1_deadlines_test.go`: `TestJSONBodyThatStallsIsEnded` (red without the deadline, by mutation); `TestDownloadThatStopsBeingReadIsCutOffWithinASegment` (red by mutation: the deadline covered the whole file); `TestDownloadCompletesForASlowReaderAboveTheMinimumRate`; `TestDownloadRangesComplete` (a single range and a multipart range both complete); `TestDownloadSendsFileSegmentsThroughReadFrom` (red by mutation: segments not sent through `ReadFrom`, so sendfile is not used). The earlier design, one deadline for the whole file, was rejected on review: at 100 GB it allowed days.
    - *4. `/metrics`.* Off the main listener by default. `metrics_on_main: true` (default false) serves it there; with `metrics_listen` set, it is served only on that address. Tests: `TestMetricsIsOffTheMainListenerByDefault`, `TestMetricsOnTheMainListenerNeedsTheFlag`, `TestMetricsListenWinsOverTheFlag`. Config reference updated in README. Commit 406dc0e.
    - *5. Delegated tokens.* A password reset, a password change, an admin's password set and a disable now end the user's delegated tokens (`endUserTokens`: the same cut-off and WOPI session end as the explicit revoke). Enabling the user again does not bring a token back. The verify path, which activates a pending user, is not changed: a pending user has no tokens. Test: `TestDelegatedTokenEndsWithEachPasswordAndStatusEvent`. Commit 71ba2c8.
    - *6. Zip text extraction.* `officeExt` reads the entry names in one pass that keeps no entry, stops at `mimetype`, and leaves a container over 10,000 entries undecided. Tests: `TestOfficeExtRefusesAZipOverTheEntryCap` (red before: a 12,001-entry zip was decided), `TestOfficeExtDecidesAZipUnderTheEntryCap`. Commit accac4a.
    - *7. JSON answers.* `writeJSON` sets `Cache-Control: no-store` unless the handler set its own, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Tests: `TestWriteJSONSetsNoStoreAndNosniff`, `TestMeAnswerIsNotCachedAndNotSniffed`; `TestWriteJSONKeepsACacheHeaderTheHandlerSet` guards the kept header. Commit acf7590.
    - *8. Mail names.* Share, drop and access-request mails use `mail.Name` for actor, item and folder names, as comment mails do. The API refuses names with invisible or line-separator characters on write, so the bidi and break part is defence in depth; the reachable effect is that a dotted name is no longer a link. `mailText` had no other caller and is removed. Tests: `TestShareMailNamesUseTheMailNameRule`, `TestAccessRequestMailNamesUseTheMailNameRule`; `TestShareMailUsesRecipientLocale` now expects the item name through `mail.Name`. The drop-notice mail changed the same way and has no test of its own. Commit 12b788c.
    - *9. `/wopi` refusals.* A refused forged request warns once per client address per minute (limiter `wopi.refusal`) and logs at debug after that. *Decided against:* rate-limiting the refusals themselves, since a forged request still gets its refusal. Test: `TestWOPIRefusalsWarnOncePerAddressPerWindow` (red: five warnings for five forged requests). Commit 5983304.
    - *10. Webhook address table.* `2001::/23` is denied whole, which covers 2001:1::/32 and 2001:3::/32. Test: `TestDenyTableRestOfIPv6AndSIIT` (red before for 2001:1::1 and 2001:3::1). Commit 6627618.
    - *11. Restricted viewers with `content_url`.* The viewer's inline PDF was refused: the link was judged on the main origin, where `content_url` refuses every inline type, so the answer said viewing was allowed and refused it. Rework after review: the mint-time rule for a restricted caller's inline link is `safeInlineType` (a type a browser shows inline); the serve-time rule is that with `content_url` set, an inline link to a no-download file is served on the content origin only, and on the main origin it is refused with the bad-link answer and no bytes are sent. *Decided against:* binding a "content-origin only" claim into the signed link, which needs a token format change; the serve-time check uses the node's flag and needs none. Consequence stated plainly: an editor's inline link to a no-download file is also served on the content origin only when `content_url` is set. Tests: `TestViewerOpensANoDownloadPDFInlineWithContentURL` (the PDF opens inline on the content host; green before and after), `TestRestrictedInlineLinkIsRefusedOnTheMainOrigin`, `TestRestrictedInlineLinkForAZipIsRefusedAtMint`. Commits 79c85c0, d144fad.
    - *12. Admin hardening.* A key made from an admin session needs the admin's password (`admin_password`), checked by `confirmAdminPassword` as sign-in-as checks it (way `create_key`). An installation admin's key is a key, not a session, and needs no password. A pending owner's link from an admin session needs `admin.tenant_access`. Admin sessions end sooner: `sessions.admin_idle_timeout` 12 h and `sessions.admin_max_age` 7 days, the shorter of these and the user limits. The admin's password on the pending-owner link routes (account create and resend) is in 05b9cb8, and test `TestAdminSessionOwnerLinkNeedsThePassword`. Tests: `TestAdminSessionKeyNeedsThePassword`, `TestAdminSessionEndsSoonerThanAUsersSession`, `TestAdminSessionResetLinkNeedsTenantAccess`; `TestAdminSessionLinkRules` now turns `tenant_access` on. Commit b38f057. The web half is in its own commits (see the related fix below).

    *Choices the owner may want to confirm.* (a) The device cookie: 180 days (`sessions.device_cookie_lifetime`), 10 failed sign-ins an hour per cookie, and a loose cap of 30 failed sign-ins an hour per email, all addresses together (`login.failed`). (b) Admin sessions: 12 hours idle and 7 days at most (`sessions.admin_idle_timeout`, `sessions.admin_max_age`). (c) `/metrics` off the main listener by default (`metrics_on_main`). (d) Every one-request write counts against 300 a minute per caller (`write.one_request`), and a large or unsized one (over 1 MiB, or with no declared length) also against 60 a minute (`write.one_request_large`, as `upload.create`). Both are fixed, not settings (README). (e) `wopi.refusal`: one warning a minute per address. (f) Downloads: `download.timeout` 30 s, `download.min_rate` 64 KiB a second, and the segment size 8 MiB (a constant, `downloadSegmentBytes`). A reader slower than the minimum rate over one segment is cut off. There is no absolute cap on a download's total time; a client resumes with `Range`.

    *Review of sec1 (an independent read of head 09a93bd; findings F1 to F13).* **F1** (a correct password from a browser without the device cookie is refused while the email's cap is spent): kept as built, by the owner's decision. The brief's first property, that an attacker without the password from one address cannot stop the real user from another address, holds only for a browser that holds the device cookie. A new browser waits up to an hour, or uses Forgot password, while someone keeps the email's cap spent. The owner chose an emailed new-browser confirmation as the next slice: when the cap is spent, any password from a browser without the cookie gets the same answer, and only a right password sends a single-use link that signs in and remembers the browser. Not built in sec1; built in sec2, decision 86, which points here: with a mailer the cap's answer is the confirmation, and the refusal stays only for a server without mail. Test `TestNoDeviceCookieIsRefusedWhileTheCapIsSpent` now pins the refusal of a server without a mailer (its test server has none); the mailer case is `sec2_confirm_test.go`. **F2**: the zip and export routes take `serveDownload`, the same progress deadline as a file (`TestZipThatStopsBeingReadIsCutOffWithinASegment`, `TestZipCompletesForASlowReaderAboveTheMinimumRate`). Exports share the helper; no slow-reader test was added for them. **F3**: a one-request write reserves its bytes while its body arrives (`reserveOneRequest`). The disk check counts the one-request bytes in flight and the unwritten bytes of open uploads, in total and per account, and the account's own share (`upload.max_disk_share_percent`) caps what one account holds, as tus and drop pieces do. The reservation is released on every exit. An unsized body reserves its cap (`upload.max_small_file_size`, 16 MiB; or `office.max_file_bytes`, 50 MiB, for WOPI): the cap is small enough to reserve up front, so there is no incremental reservation. The quota is checked, not reserved; the write's own transaction still stops an over-quota write. Tests: `TestConcurrentOneRequestWritesCannotOverrunTheDisk`, `TestOneRequestWritesHoldTheAccountShareOfTheDisk`, `TestLargeOneRequestWritesAreLimitedAt60`, all with mutations. **F4**: the owner link an admin session asks for through the user create route (`POST /accounts/{acc}/users`) needs the admin's password (way `wayOwnerLink`), as the account create and the resend do. The web's only call of that route sends `verification: "email"`, so it needs no change. Test `TestAdminSessionCreateUserOwnerLinkNeedsThePassword`. **F5**: a zip's entries are counted before `zip.NewReader` builds them (`zipEntryCount`, `internal/search/zipcount.go`). The end record's declared count is refused over the cap (zip64 when the count is 0xFFFF, or the size or offset is 0xFFFFFFFF), and the real central directory headers are walked from each start archive/zip could take (base+dirOff, and dirOff when the base is above zero), stopping at the cap, with one fixed header and a buffered reader, so no allocation per entry. The post-parse count check stays as a backstop. Two bypasses were found on review and fixed: a declared count of 100 over 65,636 real headers (archive/zip compares only the count modulo 65,536), and data in front of the zip. Each has a mutation: the declared check off, and the walk from dirOff only (`TestOfficeExtRefusesADeclaredCountOverTheCap`, `TestOfficeExtRefusesAPrependedZipOverTheCap`, `TestOfficeExtRefusesADeclaredCountThatHidesRealHeaders`, and the zip64 and allocation tests). **F6**: `write.one_request` is 300 a minute, as this decision says; the limit was 60 and is now 300 for every one-request write, with `write.one_request_large` at 60 for large ones (Choices (d)). Two tests seed bulk data from one caller and exceed 300 a minute (`TestNameSearchPastUnreadableMatchesWithinTheDeadline` makes 1,540 writes, `TestPlaylistReadCost` 500); each gives its seeding a larger limiter, and `TestOneRequestWritesAreRateLimitedPerCaller` pins the limit. Open for the owner: a bulk script that writes more than 300 files a minute is refused until the minute passes. **F7**: `confirmAdminPassword` refuses a request with no session (403, `reason` `session_required`), before it counts any failure. No legitimate token flow sends a token there: each route that confirms the password requires a session, and a token of an admin-role user cannot be made, since the users table allows the admin role only without an account. Test `TestConfirmAdminPasswordNeedsASession` (it panicked on the nil session before). **F8**: the main-origin refusal of inline links to no-download files applies to every caller, on purpose. Owners' links are minted with `content_url` set, so they point at the content host, which is not refused; a hand-made or pre-`content_url` main-origin link is. Test `TestUnrestrictedInlineLinkWithContentURLStillOpens`. **F9**: a device cookie stops working after a password change, a reset, an admin's set-password or a disable. The cookie carries its issue time (`userID.nonce.issued.expiry.mac`), and `trustedDevice` refuses a cookie issued at or before the user's cut-off (`users.tokens_not_before`, which `endUserTokens` moves on those four paths, so no migration). A cookie made in the same millisecond as the cut-off is void, as the cut-off is kept in milliseconds. Sign-in stamps the cookie with the time its transaction made the session, not the clock after the commit, so a change committed between the login transaction and the cookie write voids it (test hook `afterLoginCommit`). Reset stamps its cookie a millisecond after its own cut-off, in the same transaction, and reads nothing after the commit. Tests: `TestDeviceCookieEndsWithAPasswordChange`, `...WithAReset`, `...WithAnAdminsTypedPassword`, `...WithADisable`, and `TestDeviceCookieIssuedBeforeACommittedChangeIsVoid`; each has a mutation. **F10, F11, F12**: no change; they are documented above (the whole-body JSON deadline, the `min_rate` trade-off). **F13** (the cookie's expiry on the wall clock, not `limitClock()`): not changed. The cut-off is compared with the store's wall clock, so a frozen limiter clock in a test would void a fresh cookie; it is not a one-liner.

    *Related fix (the admin dialogs, found on the dev run; the owner's report).* (A) The New admin dialog says "How the admin gets in" (all seven catalogues) and offers only the email invitation from an admin session, since the server refuses a link for a new admin there (`linkAllowed`). With mail not configured it says an admin can then be added only with `selfcloud admin create-admin`. Commit 4e6d1fe. (B) The other dialogs that offer a link (new tenant, the tenant's member resend, password reset) offer only what `linkAllowed` and `checkVerificationMethod` accept for that caller and target. Commit 3d5b080. (C) The New tenant dialog labels its fields "Tenant name" and "Owner's name" (all seven catalogues), and the first owner's fields sit under a divider; the other admin dialogs' "Name" labels are made specific too. Commit 7fbf69d. (D) The web asks for the admin's password through the sign-in-as dialog (`AdminPassword`) before a key is made, an owner's link is sent, and a tenant with a link owner is made; the server checks it with `confirmAdminPassword` on those three routes (see item 12 above).
